places.name: 串カツさくら 南海難波店 (Kushikatsu Sakura Nankai Namba)
places.gf_detail: Ask. The shop says its kushikatsu batter uses rice flour, fried in 100% plant-based oils (Tabelog shop text), but it does not claim gluten-free: breadcrumbs, the special sauce, the white soy sauce and the shared fryer are not described. Ask which dip is wheat-free.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. Vegetable skewers (onion, shishito, asparagus) are fried in plant-based oil, but the batter may contain egg and is fried alongside meat and seafood.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–22:30; Sat, Sun and holidays 11:00–22:30; open year-round; last order 30 minutes before closing (Tabelog). No reservations on Friday nights, weekends, holidays or peak seasons — first come, first served. Cards accepted; no e-money or QR. Queues are common.
places.neighborhood: Namba 3-1-18, on Nankai-dori — 1 min from Nankai Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Kushikatsu in a thin, crisp rice-flour batter fried in plant oils · large skewers: quail egg, chicken, shrimp, beef, pork, whiting, onion, shishito, asparagus, tulip (chicken wing) · dip in special sauce, grilled salt or white soy sauce · doteyaki beef-tendon stew · free cabbage · 50 seats (1F counter, 2F tables and horigotatsu)
places.notes: [Kushikatsu · rice-flour kushikatsu on Nankai-dori] A 50-seat kushikatsu house a minute from Nankai Namba, open since 2012 and often with a line. The difference is the batter: rice flour instead of wheat, fried in plant-based oils, so the skewers come out ultra-thin and crisp. October 2026 reviewers found it light on the stomach. That's not a gluten-free claim, though; breadcrumbs, sauces and the shared fryer aren't described, so coeliacs should ask. The skewers are big: plump shrimp, excellent pork, a soft quail egg (best with the white soy sauce), plus tulip wings and asparagus. Dip in the special sauce, grilled salt or white soy, and start with doteyaki. Frying happens downstairs, so the second floor stays free of oil smells. On busy nights the kitchen can lag, with a 30-minute wait for skewers in October 2026.

chef_bio.background: Kushikatsu Sakura, which bills its rice-flour skewers as "the original" (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.philosophy: Rice-flour batter to reduce oil absorption; the plant-based frying oils are varied daily (shop text).

anecdotes.text: Shop text: "By using 'rice flour' in the batter, we reduce the oil absorption rate compared to regular kushi-katsu!… we change the types of 100% plant-based oils we use every day."
"The batter made from rice flour is light and incredibly crispy, perfectly enhancing the flavors of the ingredients." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Gyoza · the Gyoza no Ohsho by Shinsaibashi-suji] The Shinsaibashi branch of the Gyoza no Ohsho chain, two minutes from the station: hearty, cheap Chinese food that Kansai people call soul food. Order gyoza with or without garlic, to compare the garlic richness with the ginger. The Chinese rice bowl is lighter on cornstarch than most, packed with shrimp, squid, scallops, quail eggs and vegetables. Tianjin rice is a regular's craving. This branch also serves a "Gyoza no Ohsho lunch" for under ¥800, a roasted-miso ramen on thick noodles, and cold noodles in summer. One July 2026 visitor used a Wednesday half-price gyoza coupon. The manager greets you loudly.

places.notes: [Ramen · build-your-own ramen in a red NY-style Amemura room] A 12-seat ramen shop in Amerika-mura, open since November 2024, decked out in red New York style. The concept is "Suppin" ramen: a bare bowl of broth and noodles from ¥550, built up with your pick of toppings. Fried scallops are ¥280 and rare chashu ¥100, and one reviewer counts over a trillion combinations. The broth is a rich, creamy pork bone, a little salty for some, on chewy noodles. There's also the "Ali Red", a tangy sukiyaki ramen, and a double-chashu classic. The chashu rice bowl comes with cheese. Staff are friendly; check the door at opening time, as one lunch visitor found it still locked.

chef_bio.background: Build-your-own "Suppin" concept (reviews).

places.notes: [Ramen · a hidden one-person shoyu and shio counter by Nagahoribashi] An eight-seat L-shaped counter at the very back of a dark, narrow building passage; look for the sign, or the lantern of Chuka Bar Sakurai. The owner runs it alone, serving ramen at lunch and Chinese dishes with ramen in the evening. It's usually quiet. The house favourite is the shoyu (¥900; special ¥1,350), balanced between sharpness and richness on a carefully made dashi. The shio is a golden broth clear enough to see the bottom of the bowl, topped with pork rare chashu, chicken chashu, shiso and menma. The special shio (¥1,300) adds three chashu, a shiso wonton and a sake-scented egg. A clear shio niboshi (¥1,050 with egg) leans seafood. There are no table condiments; pay at your seat, cash only. Closed Tuesdays.

places.notes: [Ramen · Yokohama iekei at the east end of Dotonbori] A Yokohama iekei shop that opened in April 2026 near Nippombashi. Reviewers call it a direct branch of Daikiya, a well-known Tokyo iekei shop, and there's already a queue of 7–20 at peak times. The broth is very thick pork bone with a sharp soy edge, served with spinach, nori and a seasoned egg; set firmness, richness and oil to taste. Several people warn it's very salty, so start mild if you're not used to iekei. The smoked chashu is the star. Rice is ¥100 for all you can eat, from a self-serve bar of garlic, mayonnaise and a spicy sauce; wrap it in nori dipped in the broth. Tsukemen (large ¥1,150) has a slightly spicy pork-and-chicken dip, with hot or cold noodles. Buy a ticket at the machine; open 10 am to midnight.

chef_bio.background: Reviewers (October 2026) describe it as a direct branch of the Tokyo iekei shop Daikiya.

places.notes: [Thai · Shinsaibashi's long-running Thai house, open to 2 am] A 100-seat Thai restaurant in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2000 and often full. Counter and tables are downstairs and a big room upstairs; the feel is straight out of Thailand. The reliable orders are koh muu yang, grilled pork neck charred outside with a spicy sauce, and gai yang chicken thigh with a nam pla dip. The yam woon sen glass-noodle salad is packed with shrimp, clams and minced seafood, and the pad thai is a regular's craving. Expect real heat even in dishes you thought were mild. For a late finish there's pho in a hot pot, with mango pudding or coconut ice cream. Portions suit two or three people sharing. A long-time regular thinks prices have crept up.

A March 2026 reviewer says it brings a beloved Taipei eatery to Japan for the first time. The signature is pai gu su mian (¥1,500): fried spare ribs, crisp outside and falling-apart tender down to the cartilage, on noodle soup. The broth is variously described as a gentle shrimp-and-daikon soup with a spicy kick, a creamy rich one, and a soy-leaning version that needs the table chili oil and black vinegar. Gan ban mian, the soupless mixed noodle, gets addictive as you stir. Lu rou fan comes on the side. Open to 1:20 am, and often quiet. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · Onomichi-style back-fat soy ramen off Shinsaibashi-suji] An eight-seat counter a block from the Shinsaibashi shopping street, open since 2011, with the nostalgic feel of an old Chinese eatery and the TV on. The Onomichi ramen is a light soy-and-niboshi broth with flecks of back fat and a touch of heat, with sweet chashu. The shoyu mixes soy and tonkotsu, gentle enough to drink to the last drop, and there are also shio and tonkotsu bowls. The owner asks whether you want the noodles firm. Gyoza and a fragrant, moist fried rice round it out. It fills up with overseas visitors at lunch. Buy a ticket; cash only. Smoking is allowed.

places.notes: [Café · gluten-free, additive-free café by Nagahoribashi] A calm, natural-materials café three minutes from Nagahoribashi, open from 7:30 am. Its own billing is gluten-free, additive-free and free of white sugar. Lunch runs to rice-flour craft burgers and a gluten-free curry whose spices win over doubters, plus a Buddha bowl of rice and fermented vegetables and quinoa-mixed rice. One reviewer credits the recipes to a physical therapist. The sweets are the draw: a light, moist brown-rice-flour chiffon (¥700), a kinako chocolate cake, lemon cake and cheesecake to take away, with oat-milk coffee (¥650). Evenings switch to a casual French-style dinner. Portions are modest. Closed Tuesdays; check Instagram, as event days change the hours.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kyushu tonkotsu and tomato ramen opposite NGK] A branch of the Kyushu Ramen Kio chain facing Namba Grand Kagetsu, with tablet ordering, open until midnight. The signature Kio ramen is a creamy, rich tonkotsu mellowed for Kansai palates, with no gaminess, on ultra-thin straight noodles. One reviewer ordered the extra noodles extra-firm and got them almost raw. A long-standing favourite is the tomato ramen (¥890), spicy at three levels and milder than Shin Ramyun; there's a tomato tsukemen too. For something heavier, the burnt-back-fat tonkotsu shoyu with thick noodles and lots of garlic works as a gentle Jiro-style. Summer brings a chilled abura-soba (¥890), and the half fried rice is ¥490. A lunch mix of tourists and local office workers.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura in PARCO's basement dining street] A 24-seat Kamukura on the B2F dining street of Shinsaibashi PARCO, a minute from Shinsaibashi Station. The chain's broth is light, almost consommé-like, sweet with napa cabbage and vegetables, on slightly curly thin noodles with a nice chew. The basic bowl stays under ¥1,000, and the braised-egg ramen has a runny yolk. Build it up from the table: garlic, doubanjiang and chives turn it into a hearty, spicy bowl. A winter special ran in early 2026. A line forms at the ticket machine when tourists arrive, but turnover is quick.

chef_bio.background: Kamukura chain (kamukura.co.jp).

anecdotes.text: "The broth had a unique light flavor reminiscent of consomme, yet it was deliciously addictive. The noodles were slightly curly and thin." — September 2026, braised-egg ramen.
"The thin noodles had a nice chewiness, and the broth was light yet incredibly tasty, packed with plenty of vegetables." — March 2026.

places.cuisine: Shijimi-clam ramen · rich shijimi shio ¥1,100 (large +¥100), also miso and shoyu · Yamato shijimi from Lake Shinji, Shimane · low fat, light · cold ramen with shijimi and oyster paste · clam rice with egg · limited dashi-keema mazesoba (spring 2026) · 8 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Lake Shinji shijimi-clam ramen near Nippombashi] The Namba branch of Shi43ya, a shijimi-clam ramen shop, hidden at the very back of a mixed-use building three minutes from Nippombashi. The No. 1 order is the rich shijimi shio (¥1,100, September 2026), made with plenty of Yamato shijimi from Lake Shinji in Shimane: light, low in fat and packed with clam umami. There are miso and shoyu versions too, and the clam rice with egg is popular. One reviewer counts it among Namba's best clam-broth bowls. In summer the cold ramen with shijimi turns rich once you stir in the oyster paste. Spring 2026 brought a dashi-keema mazesoba with the curry shop Niji no Hotoke. It's light enough to finish a night out; open until 12:30 am. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · lunchtime chicken paitan and shellfish broth west of Namba] A lunch-only ramen counter of about eight seats a short walk west of Namba Station; one reviewer recalls it as an izakaya by night. On one visit two Vietnamese staff were working in the kitchen. The house bowl is a frothy, creamy chicken paitan with fragrant, tender chashu and crunchy onions. There's also a shellfish-broth ramen that one diner drained to the last drop, and a limited chicken, pork and clam shio (¥1,050) that was on the salty side. You choose your noodles, down to ultra-thin, and some toppings are free. The Tennoji shop is the sister branch. Service is by verbal order; one August 2026 visitor had a rough exchange with the kitchen staff. Cash only.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; gyoza, fried rice.

places.cuisine: Hakata Ippudo tonkotsu · Akamaru Shinaji ¥980 with spicy miso and fragrant oil · Shiromaru · Horie-only shoyu tonkotsu ¥950 with back fat and garlic chives on thicker noodles · tantan tsukemen ¥1,090 (limited) · meat-miso tsukemen · Hakata fried rice (small) ¥430 · extra noodles ¥150 · 39 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Ippudo in Minami-Horie, with a branch-only shoyu tonkotsu] Hakata Ippudo's Horie branch, three minutes from Yotsubashi. The customers are mostly international, and one reviewer felt they had walked into an overseas Ippudo. The classic Akamaru Shinaji (¥980) adds spicy miso and fragrant oil to the rich tonkotsu; the Shiromaru is the plain version. Exclusive to this branch is a shoyu tonkotsu (¥950) with soy, back fat and garlic chives on slightly thicker noodles; pair it with a small Hakata fried rice (¥430). Tsukemen fans get thick noodles in a red-oil meat-miso dip, or a limited tantan version (¥1,090). Extra noodles are ¥150, with bean sprouts, takana and pickled ginger now ordered on the touch panel. Staff service is well drilled.

chef_bio.background: Hakata Ippudo chain (ippudo.com).

anecdotes.text: "This unique Shoyu Tonkotsu from the Ippudo Horie branch features a rich tonkotsu broth with a punch of soy sauce and back fat, paired with slightly thicker noodles than usual for Ippudo." — July 2026, ¥950.
"The richness of the tonkotsu broth combined with the spicy miso and fragrant oil creates a depth of flavor that I really enjoy, different from the Shiromaru." — August 2026, Akamaru Shinaji ¥980.

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-and-chicken broth, smoked chashu, horumon.

places.cuisine: Yokohama iekei, direct line of Oudouya · ramen ¥1,000 with two big slices of chashu, spinach and three nori · smoked chashu ramen and chashu rice · Oudou ramen with rice · famous horumon fry · kara-age · firmness, richness and oil to order · unlimited garlic, chopped ginger and mayonnaise at the table · open from 7 am
places.notes: [Ramen · Oudouya-line iekei by JR Namba, open from 7 am] A Yokohama iekei shop in the basement of Minatomachi River Place, a minute from JR Namba, in the direct line of the famous Oudouya. Open December 2024, it runs from 7 am to 3 am and still has a 15-person queue after midnight. The ramen (¥1,000) is a pork-bone soy broth with the sharp soy edge of the style and pork-and-chicken umami, on chewy medium-thick noodles, with two big slices of chashu, spinach and three nori sheets. The smoked chashu is the star of the chashu ramen and chashu rice. Order firmness, richness and oil to taste, then load up on the table garlic, chopped ginger and mayonnaise. The fried horumon is a known side. One devotee calls it Osaka's No. 1 iekei; the saltiness varies visit to visit. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: A direct-line (直系) shop of Oudouya, the Yokohama iekei lineage (shop name).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a pork bone soy sauce base, with fine oil floating on the surface. You can taste the strong presence of soy sauce typical of the Iekei style, along with the umami of pork and chicken. The noodles are medium-thick with a chewy texture." — October 2026, ramen ¥1,000.

"The large slices of chashu covering the bowl are infused with a rich smoky aroma… the extensive selection of table condiments, including unlimited garlic, chopped ginger, and mayonnaise." — October 2026.

places.cuisine: Quiet kissa on the 5th floor of a gallery building · coffee and tea · homemade pudding · cake sets (half-and-half cheese and chocolate) · mixed juice · iced tea and matcha milk ¥600–700 · art on the walls · 15 seats
places.notes: [Kissa · a quiet fifth-floor café opposite Shochikuza] Take the lift to the fifth floor of a gallery building across from Osaka Shochikuza, and the Dotonbori crowds feel far away. Bon is a calm, art-hung kissa of about 15 seats that theatergoers use before a show; you can look down on the theater. The menu is short: coffee, tea, mixed juice, matcha milk, cake sets and a homemade pudding a December 2025 visitor liked. Drinks were around ¥600–700 in August 2026. It's usually run by one person, so service can be slow or brisk; one 2026 visitor found it unfriendly, another the staff kind.

chef_bio.background: A café on the floor above a ground-floor gallery; long reviewed (since 2011).

places.notes: [Yakiniku · a 10-seat aged-wagyu omakase in Hozenji Yokocho] A reservation-only counter of ten seats in Hozenji Yokocho, on Tabelog's yakiniku and grill 100 lists every year from 2023 to 2026. The operator, Plan Do Action Co., is led by Hiroyuki Takeshita, born in Miyazaki Prefecture in 1976, who grew up around pigs and cattle and became a chef to bring cooking into the livestock business. There's one seating at 7 pm and one menu, the ¥19,800 omakase, and bookings run months out. It plays like meat kaiseki more than a grill: a broth of wagyu bones and water with a touch of clam, a yukhoe, aged tuna and seasonal plates, all built on aged Matsusaka and aged Miyazaki wagyu bought straight from producers. At the end you can have as much yakiniku as you like, though one diner was already full by then; the chefs grill it in front of you. Wine pairings are good. A 10% service charge applies. A September 2026 review says a restaurant group runs it.

chef_bio.background: Run by the owner of a restaurant group (September 2026 reviews); wagyu sourced directly from producers in Mie (Matsusaka) and Miyazaki. places.notes: [Oden · a one-owner oden counter in Hozenji Yokocho] A ten-seat counter in Hozenji Yokocho, run single-handed by a friendly owner who keeps drinks and dishes moving. The draw is oden in a carefully built dashi, gentle but deep, especially the clam and Tajima-chicken oden. Around it come seasonal plates: whale, sardines, meat and fish. The omakase of ten dishes (¥6,000) is the way in, and there's a broad Japanese-sake list with an omakase pour. It's quiet and calm, good for a slow drink. Book online, as it's often full by 7 pm. With one person running everything, dishes can take a moment. No children under elementary-school age.

Self-taught, the owner makes the noodles in-house; a sign talks up the flour. The shoyu ramen (¥770, September 2026) is a bargain for the area, strong on niboshi with fish powder, gentle and rich without being heavy. The shoyu-and-mini-curry set (¥1,100) shows the curry could be a main in its own right. Late at night there's a back-fat shoyu, a curry tsukemen and an iron-pan tamago kake gohan. Open until 1:30 am most nights; closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kotan's classic soy-tonkotsu in the Namba CITY basement] A branch of Kotan, a long-running Osaka ramen chain, in the B2F food floor of Namba CITY by Nankai Namba. It's open straight through, handy when you miss lunch. Kotan's signature is a soy-and-tonkotsu broth with shredded carrot and crunchy bean sprouts, on straight noodles a little thicker than medium; add the sesame on the table. Fans return for the nostalgic taste, and one came back after 15 years. A shio version exists, though the shoyu is the comfort order, and there's a vegetable-heavy nananmen. Fried-rice sets are popular but uneven. Summer brings cold noodles and a chilled tantanmen. The counters are well spaced, service is quick, and Namba CITY cardholders get 10% off. Closed the third Thursday.

chef_bio.background: Ramen Kotan chain (ramen-kotan.co.jp), described by reviewers as long-established.

anecdotes.text: "Kotan's signature is its soy sauce and tonkotsu base, complemented by shredded carrots and crunchy bean sprouts. The noodles are a unique straight style, thicker than usual medium noodles. The sesame on the table pairs perfectly with the dish." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Thai · a Thai-run kitchen by the Kuromon Market entrance] A 24-seat Thai restaurant on the corner by the Kuromon Market entrance, a minute from Nippombashi; don't mix it up with the similar Thai place two doors down. It's run by Thai staff, Thai is the language in the room, and plenty of Thai customers eat here, a good sign. The spice isn't softened for Japanese palates. The yum woon sen is a standout, balancing lime, fish sauce and cilantro. The gapao is authentic, and the tom yum goong and coconut-rich green curry draw praise. The lunch sets (¥1,100 in 2025) are the value play; à la carte prices have climbed, and one diner found the portions small for Kuromon-area prices. Service can slow when busy. Closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Run by Thai staff (2025–2026 reviews); a September 2026 reviewer calls it a Thai Select restaurant.

places.notes: [Ramen · an eight-seat machi-chuka by Yotsubashi] A long-standing, old-fashioned local Chinese counter of eight seats on the south side of Yotsubashi Station, cheap and fast, mostly men at lunch. You squeeze past each other to reach the back. The shoyu ramen has a nostalgic, slightly sweet broth, thin wavy noodles with a good bite, bean sprouts, nori and thick marinated chashu. Order it as a half to pair with something: half tantanmen and half shoyu is ¥800. There's also a shio butter-corn ramen and gyoza. The five-dish set meal (¥1,000) piles a Chinese omelette, happosai, kara-age and chashu over cabbage with rice, and a Chinese rice bowl is just ¥650. Cash only; closed Saturdays.

places.cuisine: Oyster ramen, Tabelog 100 Ramen OSAKA 2025 · "Koeru" triple-soup oyster paitan · "Ikasu" oyster dashi · oyster shoyu and oyster shiro-tan · fried oysters with salt and lemon · shirasu rice bowl · citrus accents · projection-mapping interior · 15 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Tabelog 100 oyster ramen on Doguyasuji] A 15-seat oyster-ramen shop on the Doguyasuji kitchenware street, two minutes from Namba, named to Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 for 2025. The house bowl is "Koeru", a triple-soup oyster paitan whose rich oyster umami and slight bitterness come through in every sip, with a citrus lift. There's also "Ikasu", an oyster dashi, plus oyster shoyu and a white version. Soft noodles and juicy, not-greasy chashu carry it; add the table spices for a change. Fried oysters come with salt and lemon, and the shirasu rice bowl with sesame is the side. The room is unusual too, with projection mapping. Buy your ticket outside and wait to be called; queues are mostly overseas visitors.

places.notes: [Ramen · a Chiikawa-character Jiro-style ramen shop in PARCO] A character collaboration in PARCO's B2F, decorated top to bottom in Chiikawa style down to the bowls, ladles, aprons, cups and chopstick wrappers. Fans book ahead and still wait up to an hour; the lift opens at 11 am. The ramen is Jiro-style, but gentler than the real thing: a garlicky soy broth that's lighter, with softer fat, on chewy thick noodles. You call your garlic, vegetables, fat and seasoning. Even "mini" is a full meal, and most people order it; a large with extra vegetables and fat runs ¥1,950. Reviewers split between delicious and "mainly for the merchandise", but the cuteness is the point.

places.notes: [Ramen · a seven-seat creamy chicken paitan in Kitahorie] A seven-seat counter near Yotsubashi, often with a line, serving a chicken paitan covered in fine foam: smooth and rich, the chicken clear without heaviness. The bowl carries three chashu, including low-temperature pork loin and chicken breast, plus shredded leek, mizuna and onion. One menma lover calls the thick, tender, well-soaked bamboo shoots the best ever. Noodles are medium-thick and straight; one August diner got them undercooked. A yodare-chicken rice bowl is the side. In 2026 a touch panel replaced the ticket machine, beef options joined the menu, and a younger crew took over; one long-time fan misses the old feel. It gets warm inside. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: A returning June 2026 reviewer notes a younger staff now runs the counter and the menu has added beef dishes.

anecdotes.text: "The soup was covered in fine bubbles, creating an incredibly smooth texture. Despite its richness, the chicken flavor was prominent without feeling heavy… I can confidently say this was the best menma I've ever had." — July 2026.

It's busy late with people from nearby bars and quiet earlier. Expect a gentle Kansai dashi, chewy udon and decent soba. A January 2026 diner also liked the katsudon, neither too sweet nor too salty. The menu is long, from kakiage udon to oden and a sea-urchin cream udon you can finish as risotto. Critics call it station-stand quality at nightlife prices, but it's quick, served in about a minute. Buy a ticket; some items are ordered verbally. Prices quoted here are from 2024–2025 reviews.

places.notes: [Yakitori · a one-owner charcoal yakitori hideaway north of Dotonbori] A 14-seat yakitori counter tucked into the ground floor of a mixed-use building north of Dotonbori, run by an owner who manages the room alone and still serves quickly. It grills Yamato chicken and Kawachi duck over charcoal. The duck sashimi in several cuts is the signature, and the chicken sashimi is limited, so order it ahead. Raw duck liver, negima and skin skewers, potato salad and an excellent tamagoyaki fill out the evening. Courses run from ¥3,300 (five duck sashimi and five skewers, October 2025) to ¥5,500 (January 2026). There's a good Japanese-whisky list and wine to pair. It closes when sold out, so book. Note that raw poultry is a core part of the menu. QR payment or cash.

chef_bio.background: The owner runs the shop single-handed (December 2025 review); kind service (May 2025 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal yakitori; duck and chicken sashimi.

anecdotes.text: "This hidden gem specializes in charcoal-grilled yakitori, primarily using Yamato chicken and duck meat… a course that included 'five types of duck sashimi' and 'five types of yakitori.' This came to JPY 3,300 per person." — October 2025.
"The owner was managing everything alone, providing attentive service, and the dishes were delicious and served quickly." — December 2025.

places.notes: [Sushi · a young Edomae counter in Hozenji Yokocho] A ten-seat sushi counter behind a soft green noren in Hozenji Yokocho, open since October 2025 and already packed with Japanese diners as well as visitors. The head chef was just 25 when reviewed, working alongside a more experienced chef, aged 40-something, who had recently returned from Australia. A very young team runs it. Nothing is bought in ready-made: kanpyo, dashi and desserts are all house-made. The dinner omakase (¥14,300, August 2026) moves through aged sea bream, Aomori flounder, bonito marinated with katsuobushi, kasugo, and sweet squid sent unfrozen from Kushimoto, with anago brushed with a sauce from its own bones. The rice is large-grained, lightly pressed and punchy with vinegar, salt kept low. A white-miso pudding closes. There's a lunch course too. Book, and note the shop doesn't take guests who can't eat raw food.

chef_bio.background: A young Edomae team; "no pre-made products", with kanpyo, dashi and desserts made in-house (August 2026 review). The head chef was just 25 when reviewed, working alongside a more experienced chef, aged 40-something, who had recently returned from Australia (September 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: House-made everything; low salt (August 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "This restaurant prides itself on using no pre-made products; everything, from the kanpyo (dried gourd) to the dashi (broth) and desserts, is homemade." — August 2026.
"It's been a while since I've tasted sushi with such a strong vinegar flavor in the rice. The grains of rice are large and lightly pressed." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Kappo · a monthly-changing omakase counter at the Hozenji Yokocho entrance] A small kappo counter at the mouth of Hozenji Yokocho, where an owner-chef does nearly all the cooking and the omakase changes every month, so regulars come back each season. An older review notes the chef's wife helping in the room, and that the chef had recently become a father. A June 2026 meal opened with an assorted platter featuring a rarely seen fish and tiny junsai, then sashimi on a block of ice, sweet swordfish and grilled conger eel with plum. The chef quietly adjusted one dish for a diner's bonito allergy. Earlier courses brought a Yanagawa-style hot pot; there are about eight courses with dessert. There's no drink list as such: the chef picks the sake, and the homemade fruit sour is good. Some guests leave with onigiri. Expect roughly ¥10,000–30,000 a head. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: The owner handles almost all the cooking (July 2025 review); the menu changes monthly (June 2026 review). An older review notes the chef's wife helping in the room, and that the chef had recently become a father (June 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The menu changes every month… The sashimi was adjusted slightly for me due to my allergy to bonito. The swordfish was incredibly sweet, and the grilled conger eel was perfectly charred, complemented by delicious plum sauce." — June 2026.
"I was particularly impressed by the large ice used on the platter for the sashimi." — August 2025.

places.cuisine: Shellfish ramen in a kaiseki-style room · "Kai no Hikari" shio ¥1,290 (Hiroshima oysters, clams and dried seafood) · with seasoned egg ¥1,440 · special "Sansho no Hikari" shio ¥1,670 · special shoyu ¥1,570 · shoyu ramen · medium straight Hinomoto Seimen noodles · chashu, menma, yuzu, ikura · 12 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · shellfish shio in a kaiseki-style room by Nankai Namba] The sister shop of Men ni Hikari o, two minutes from Nankai Namba, in a modern-Japanese room that feels more kaiseki than ramen bar, with a queue of 20 at opening. The signature is "Kai no Hikari" (¥1,290), a shio of Hiroshima oysters, clams and dried seafood. It's light yet packed with flavor, served piping hot with a breath of yuzu, on smooth medium-straight noodles from Hinomoto Seimen, topped with chashu, menma and ikura. A sansho version (special ¥1,670) adds a gentle numbing note to the shellfish. The special shoyu (¥1,570) is a clear, deep-amber bowl with assorted chashu and mitsuba. Every bowl is plated like a work of art. Cash only; closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: The "Bettei" (annex) of Men ni Hikari o, the Nishi-Shinsaibashi duck-ramen shop recorded separately (osaka_men_ni_hikari_o).

anecdotes.text: "The soup, made with Hiroshima oysters, clams, and dried seafood, was light yet packed with flavor. It was served piping hot and incredibly delicious! The refreshing scent of yuzu added a wonderful touch." — October 2026, "Shellfish Light" with seasoned egg ¥1,440.
"The medium straight noodles from Hinomoto Seimen are smooth and have a great texture, perfectly complementing the light broth." — October 2026, Kai no Hikari ¥1,290.

places.notes: [Ramen · a late-night iekei counter by Nippombashi] A clean, counter-only Yokohama iekei shop two minutes from Nippombashi, open until 3 am; one reviewer heads to the sauna afterward. It's a rich pork-bone shoyu on thick noodles with spinach and chashu. Pick firmness, richness and oil at the ticket machine, then build with onion, pepper, sesame, chili oil and garlic. The chashu ramen with quail eggs and nori is a classic combination, and the tsukemen has firm, springy noodles in a rich dip. Two staff keep it moving quickly. It's a balanced, crowd-pleasing take on the style, which one reviewer believes is independently franchised.

chef_bio.background: A Yokohama-style iekei shop; one reviewer believes it is an independent franchise (August 2026).

anecdotes.text: "Ikenya's house-style ramen features a rich pork bone broth and thick noodles, creating a deep and satisfying flavor. The toppings of spinach and chashu add texture." — September 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · medicinal-herb tantanmen by Yotsubashi] A tantanmen specialist a minute from Yotsubashi, open since March 2026, built on more than 20 medicinal herbs, per the staff. There are two styles: the signature Kyoto-style white tantanmen, sesame-rich with a herbal edge, and a Sichuan-style red one (¥1,200; large ¥1,400). A September 2026 diner found the Sichuan soy-milk version thin, so start with the Kyoto. Summer brought a chilled Kyoto-style bowl (¥1,300) that a reviewer likened to a famous Shijo-Omiya shop in Kyoto. Add the staff's recommended herbal vinegar or the homemade doubanjiang (sold at ¥300 to take home). The fluffy lettuce fried rice is a sleeper hit. Staff explain everything to first-timers. Reviews range from a favourite to just average.

chef_bio.background: A yakuzen (medicinal-herb) tantanmen specialist; staff explain the herbs and how to eat (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Authentic tantanmen with over 20 medicinal herbs (September–October 2026 reviews).

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: thin wheat noodles.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: tonkotsu broth, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–6:00 (food L.O. 5:45), open year-round (Tabelog). Night-time prices are higher (August 2026). places.cuisine: Ichiran tonkotsu in partitioned booths · ramen ¥1,290 at night prices · salted soft-boiled egg ¥180 · extra garlic ¥180 · thin, low-hydration noodles · order sheet for richness, firmness and secret red sauce · rice, extra noodles · 40 booth seats · open to 6 am
places.notes: [Ramen · Ichiran's booth-counter tonkotsu, nearly round the clock] The Shinsaibashi branch of Ichiran, by Shinsaibashi Station exit 2, open from 10 am to 6 am. You eat in a partitioned booth at the "flavor concentration counter" and rarely see staff. Buy a ticket, fill in an order sheet for richness, firmness and the secret red sauce, then eat and leave. The tonkotsu is mild and creamy without pork funk, on thin, low-hydration noodles; firm is the popular call. A regular orders the red sauce at level 6, and one diner's 10× version was fiercely hot. At night the ramen is ¥1,290, with a salted egg and extra garlic at ¥180 each. Tourist queues can mean a 40-minute wait, though the line is well managed. One 2:30 am visit was walk-in.

chef_bio.background: Ichiran chain (ichiran.com).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was mild and creamy without the typical pork bone smell, and the firm, thin noodles clung well to it… When I mixed in the red secret sauce in the center, it added just the right amount of spiciness and depth." — August 2026.
"At Ichiran, I had ramen for JPY 1290, a soft-boiled salted egg for JPY 180, and an extra serving of garlic for JPY 180. These are all night-time prices." — August 2026.

places.cuisine: Chicken shio ramen from shamo, jidori, salt and seafood · special chicken shio with yuzu, rare and smoked chashu · wonton chicken shio · shoyu ramen · limited rich tonkotsu-seafood · spicy minced-meat ramen · meat tsukemen (three chashu) · grilled black-wagyu sukiyaki rice · chicken-skin gyoza · Setouchi oyster gyoza · counter and tables
places.notes: [Ramen · chicken shio and wagyu sukiyaki rice in Namba Skyo] A spacious ramen shop on the second floor of Namba Skyo, directly connected to Nankai Namba; reviewers note the brand is featured in the Michelin Guide. The signature is a clear chicken shio from shamo and jidori with salt and seafood, gentle and soothing. The special adds yuzu, moist rare chashu and juicy smoked chashu, and a wonton version is popular too. The shoyu has firm noodles, and the menu ranges to a spicy minced-meat ramen, a meat tsukemen with three chashu and a limited tonkotsu-seafood bowl. The popular side is the grilled black-wagyu sukiyaki rice; there's also chicken-skin gyoza and Setouchi oyster gyoza. Order by QR code. No reservations, so come off-peak.

chef_bio.background: Guriko; reviewers say the brand is featured in the Michelin Guide (October 2026).

places.cuisine: Tsukemen only: one vegetable-potage dip (vichyssoise base, clams, seafood, a little acidity) and a choice of three noodles · "Wheat Daiginjo" ridged wing noodles · "Wheat Espresso" medium-thick whole-wheat · "PM Tagliatelle" flat · ¥1,100 each (September 2026) · lemon to finish · 20 seats
places.notes: [Tsukemen · vegetable-potage tsukemen with three noodles to choose] A tsukemen shop between Shinsaibashi and Nagahoribashi, open since 2016 and produced, reviewers say, by Tetsuji of the comedy duo Shampoo Hat, with a line until mid-afternoon. There's one dip: a vegetable potage built on vichyssoise and blended vegetables, with clams and seafood, a little tomato acidity and a light finish. The choice is the noodle, each ¥1,100. Wheat Daiginjo is ridged wing noodles, Wheat Espresso medium-thick with the outer wheat left on, and PM Tagliatelle flat, kishimen-like noodles that cling to the dip. The noodles are the star, good enough to eat plain. Squeeze in lemon partway. One visitor didn't think it was worth the wait. Order on the tablet upstairs. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Produced by Tetsuji of the Kansai comedy duo Shampoo Hat (September–October 2026 reviews); official site miyata-menji.com.

anecdotes.text: "There's one type of dipping sauce, and you can choose from three types of noodles… the special wing noodles 'Wheat Daiginjo' with ridges, the medium-thick 'Wheat Espresso' made with the outer layer of wheat left intact, and the flat noodles 'PM Tagliatelle'." — September 2026, ¥1,100 each.

places.notes: [Chinese · Anhui beef noodles in Shimanouchi] A no-frills Anhui beef-noodle shop in Shimanouchi, east of Nippombashi, where most customers are Chinese and the menu is in Chinese. The staff will walk you through ordering. The signature is beef banmian, flat noodles in a light beef-bone broth that tastes almost like dashi. The red chilies floating in it aren't spicy, and you choose the heat level. Beef lamian is ¥880 (January 2026), with thin, medium or thick noodles. The liangpi has a garlic kick, and the side dishes are startlingly cheap. Tabelog lists no hours; an older review said it opens at 10 am and runs straight through, so check ahead.

chef_bio.background: Anhui-style beef noodle shop with a mostly Chinese clientele (March 2025 review).

places.cuisine: Creative Sichuan cooking, Tabelog 100 Chinese WEST (2021, 2023) · mapo tofu with real Sichuan numbing · Chaozhou-style kanpachi sashimi · soft-shell crab in chili sauce · special mayonnaise shrimp · fluffy egg with shrimp · squid · dan dan noodles · gentle chicken soup noodles to finish · courses and à la carte · 12 counter seats
places.notes: [Chinese · a Tabelog 100 creative Sichuan counter in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi basement] A dim, stylish 12-seat basement counter, twice named to Tabelog's Chinese WEST 100, serving authentic Sichuan cooking with creative ingredients. Booking is hard; one diner got in by phoning at 5:30 pm. The mapo tofu is the must-order: properly spicy, fragrant and numbing with Sichuan pepper, and one course made it with fugu milt. A Chaozhou-style kanpachi sashimi shows the range, alongside soft-shell crab in chili sauce, mayonnaise shrimp, fluffy egg with shrimp, and squid one diner couldn't imagine bettering. A clear, gentle chicken soup noodle closes the night. Expect about ¥10,000 with drinks; it gets warm near the kitchen. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog 100 Chinese WEST 2021 and 2023 (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I started with the must-try Mapo Tofu. One bite revealed a delightful spiciness accompanied by the fragrance and numbing sensation of Sichuan pepper, delivering an authentic taste." — June 2026.
"The Kanpachi was prepared in a way reminiscent of Chaozhou-style raw fish… the Mapo Tofu made with fugu soft roe." — June 2026, course.

places.notes: [Sushi · an 8-seat red-vinegar omakase counter off Shinsaibashi-suji] An eight-seat counter on the second floor of a building just off the Shinsaibashi shopping street, open since 2020 and popular with international guests. The name is the point: the rice is seasoned with red vinegar (akazu), firm and made without sugar. A repeat visitor says the firm rice divides opinion. The seasonal omakase is ¥17,600 (April 2026) and runs to nearly twenty items, with three cuts of tuna, abalone with liver sauce and, unusually, an abalone-liver risotto with truffle and parmesan. Then come nodoguro, sweet shrimp, sea urchin and simmered anago, closing with miso soup and pudding. The head chef is warm and chatty rather than intimidating. Dinner is two fixed seatings where everyone starts together, so be on time. Children are welcome, with udon and curry rice on offer. A service charge is added.

chef_bio.background: Sushi Akasu; a sister shop is in Namba (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Red-vinegar rice made without sugar (April 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The rice was firm, made without sugar, and had a nice vinegar flavor… In between, there was even a risotto with abalone liver sauce!" — April 2026, omakase ¥17,600.
"The rice is firm, and as the name suggests, they use red vinegar, which can be quite polarizing." — October 2026, a repeat visitor.

places.notes: [Chinese · a homey Chinese tavern behind Hozenji Yokocho] A small Chinese tavern hidden behind Hozenji Yokocho, with a round counter and one table. A friendly couple runs it, and the atmosphere is homey. One diner said it's neither neighborhood Chinese nor strict Sichuan: basic dishes built on well-studied seasonings. The popular laziji is properly hot, softened by peanuts and cilantro. The Hakata-style chive omelet, fluffy and a little runny with pickled mustard greens, cools things down, and one fan orders a chive-and-egg rice bowl for everyone, every time. Also mapo tofu, stir-fried water spinach, yodare chicken, scallion-oil noodles and a mapo potato with grilled cheese. Tabelog's average is ¥3,000–4,000. It fills up, so book; the reservation course is seven dishes for ¥3,000 plus tax. Look for the shop's sign, not the building name. Tabelog's hours contradict themselves, so check before going.

chef_bio.background: Run by a couple, according to an April 2026 review; one diner chatted with the owner at the round counter (March 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Well-researched basic seasonings rather than strict Sichuan (March 2026 review).

places.notes: [Steak and pizza · A5 wagyu and Neapolitan pizza near Shinsaibashi] A stylish, cozy 20-seat steak-and-pizza room on the ground floor of Queens Court East, open since late 2025 and opening at 3 pm, which suits early drinkers. The chef is from overseas and communicates well in Japanese. Many guests are visitors from abroad. The menu is in English and Japanese, and the chef speaks both. Steak is the main event: A5 wagyu chuck tender or filet, with salt, wasabi, garlic, soy and truffle on the side. Pizzas come from a high-heat oven with a crisp outside and chewy inside, about seven kinds at 22–24 cm, such as truffle mushroom and bacon or quattro formaggi with honey. Small plates include jamón serrano with caprese (¥1,210) and a Caesar salad grated with plenty of cheese. There's a ¥4,290 course for solo diners. Order by QR code on your phone. One diner found it a little pricey. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Casual fine dining; the chef speaks English and Japanese (September 2026 review); pizza dough supervised by an award-winning pizzaiolo (Tabelog). The chef is from overseas and communicates well in Japanese (September 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: A5 wagyu and Neapolitan pizza in a casual setting (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Osaka okonomiyaki cooked for you by the staff, with crisp tenkasu · pork-tama · beef-tendon and Kujo green onion salt yakisoba · dote-yaki · grilled squid legs · bite-sized gyoza · squid with green onion and mayo-ponzu · spicy cucumber · sours · lunch ¥1,000–2,000, dinner ¥3,000–4,000 · 11 counter and 4 table seats
places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a basement okonomiyaki bar behind Shochikuza] A small, clean basement okonomiyaki bar behind Shochikuza, two minutes from Namba, open since 2018 and now mostly full of visitors from abroad. The staff cook the okonomiyaki for you, and it's beautifully shaped and topped with crisp tenkasu. One visitor liked that it stays open past 10 pm. The surprise hit is the salt yakisoba with beef tendon and Kujo green onion, and the dote-yaki is tender with beer. Lines run 30 minutes to an hour; you wait at the door and order from the menu while you queue. Order all your okonomiyaki at once, since you can't add more later, and there's a one-order-per-person rule. One lunch diner found it merely average. Tabelog posted a temporary closure from 1 September to 18 October, and the newest review is from March 2026, so check before going.

chef_bio.background: Okonomiyaki izakaya with a dashi-forward batter and fresh thick yakisoba noodles (Tabelog); official site dining-o.com.
chef_bio.philosophy: Crisp outside, fluffy inside (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Special rich seafood tsukemen ¥1,200 (October 2025) with chewy whole-grain thick noodles, pork-bone and seafood dip, big nori and chunky braised pork · large portion at the same price · tonkotsu ramen with thin noodles, firmness to order · black tonkotsu ramen · chashu-mayo rice bowl · extra rice ¥100 · counter and tables
places.notes: [Tsukemen · a one-person tsukemen and tonkotsu shop by Nippombashi, open to 2 am] A small shop a minute from Nippombashi exit 7, open since 2017 and run single-handed by a quiet, humble owner. It stays open until 2 am; one pair stopped in after a play. The draw is the special rich seafood tsukemen (¥1,200, October 2025): a pork-bone and seafood dip with chewy, almost soba-like whole-grain thick noodles, a large sheet of nori and thick-cut tender pork. A large portion costs the same; say so when you hand over your ticket. The dip can cool fast against the cold noodles. There's also a tonkotsu ramen with thin, firm noodles, milder than its pork flavor suggests, a black tonkotsu and a chashu-mayo rice bowl. Buy a ticket from the machine outside, and bring cash.

chef_bio.background: Run by one owner working alone (December 2024 and August 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Rich seafood tsukemen with whole-grain noodles.

anecdotes.text: "The dipping sauce was a rich broth made of pork bones and seafood, paired with chewy whole grain thick noodles that were very satisfying." — December 2024, special rich seafood tsukemen, large at no extra charge.
"I visited around 1 AM. There were no other customers, and the quiet owner was the only one in the shop." — August 2026, tonkotsu ramen with extra-firm noodles.

places.neighborhood: Namba Dining Maison 8F (Namba 5-1-18, Takashimaya) — about 1 min from Nankai Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Tai shio soba from a 100% sea-bream dashi of Uwajima sea bream · clear golden broth, thin noodles, grilled chashu, flower-shaped fu and yuzu · ajitama tai shio soba · sesame sea-bream chazuke finished with dashi · tai shio soba with sea-bream rice ¥1,392 · salmon and ikura ochazuke · chuka soba · limited black-wagyu ramen · kids menu · 56 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Uwajima sea-bream shio ramen on Takashimaya's restaurant floor] A calm, modern Japanese-style ramen shop on the eighth-floor restaurant level of Namba Takashimaya, open since December 2025 and popular with families and couples. The broth is all sea-bream dashi from Uwajima sea bream: clear, golden and gentle, over thin noodles with grilled chashu, a flower-shaped piece of fu and yuzu. The move is a set: finish with sesame sea-bream chazuke, rice under sea bream and sesame sauce, loosened with dashi, or take the sea-bream rice (¥1,392 with the ramen, October 2026). One diner found the sea-bream flavor too faint and the noodles clumped near closing. Others call it elegant and delicate, if a bit pricey. Order on the tablet. Children are welcome, with a kids menu.

chef_bio.background: Tai Shio Soba Toka, a sea-bream shio ramen brand with "multiple awards" (Tabelog); official site ramen-toka.com.
chef_bio.philosophy: 100% sea-bream dashi from fresh Uwajima sea bream (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Tai shio soba; sesame sea-bream chazuke.

places.notes: [Ramen · spiny-lobster ramen that ends as a cheese risotto] A small shrimp-ramen specialist near JR Namba, open since 2024, with an Ise-lobster sign out front and a sleek interior. The broth is 100% spiny lobster: milky, thick and creamy, coating medium-thick noodles, with wood ear, bok choy, white onion and a soft-boiled egg. The real show comes after. The Megami Set (¥2,000, shoyu or miso) includes a free extra serving of noodles, then rice and cheese go into the leftover broth, and you torch the cheese at the table into a risotto. Add the lobster powder, chili oil or a squeeze of lemon. One diner said the ramen felt like a starter for the risotto. Prices are high for ramen: ¥3,000 with abalone, and a ¥5,500 Kiwami Set. Buy a ticket at the machine. Closed Thursdays.

places.notes: [Ramen · late-night chicken paitan, mazesoba and cheese ramen by Nippombashi] A casual, stylish ramen shop by Nippombashi exit 7, open since 2023 until midnight or later and popular with overseas guests. The menu runs well past one bowl. The chicken paitan has thin noodles and is milder than most. The mazesoba (¥1,320, July 2026) coats thick flat noodles in oil and sweet soy with egg yolk, onion chips and plenty of chashu, junky and satisfying. The "chicken fromage" is a rich cheese ramen that eats almost like pasta. There's a chilled black-sesame tantanmen (July 2026), and the chicken dan dan noodles are mild unless you ask for more heat. There are kara-age set meals and yakitori too. Food can take 10–15 minutes at busy times. On some nights it stays open until 5 am; check the shop's Instagram.

places.notes: [Tsukemen · kombu-water tsukemen with a shijimi dip near Kuromon] A ten-seat shop near Kuromon Market, rated 3.65 on Tabelog, that grew out of a limited-time ramen at a katsu-sandwich shop in Kitashinchi. The signature is the Rosanjin tsukemen (¥1,350, October 2026; large 300 g for ¥150 more). The noodles arrive in frothy whipped kombu water made with Rausu kombu, so you taste them on their own first. Then dip them in a piping-hot shijimi-clam sauce with a faintly Western edge. A QR code at the table shows how to work through it: tororo kombu, then prosciutto with sudachi or lemon, and finally the leftover kombu water poured into the dip. There's also a light, well-balanced shio ramen. The tempura rice bowls are a hidden hit; one diner thought the egg-tempura bowl could stand as a dish on its own. Buy a ticket at the machine and bring cash. Closed Tuesdays.

"This dipping sauce had a strong flavor of shijimi clam dashi, yet it also had a somewhat Western feel to it." — October 2026, Rosanjin tsukemen with a rice-bowl set, ¥1,700.

places.notes: [Ramen · niboshi-tonkotsu ramen in Kuromon Market] A 12-seat counter in Kuromon Market from GENKIFACTORY, a group based in Tenma known for blending niboshi with tonkotsu. One loyal diner has been coming for about 20 years, through a relocation. The niboshi ramen pairs a pork-bone broth with domestic dried sardines and soy: easy-going, with a gentle niboshi flavor, a good balance of oil and salt, and fish powder waiting at the bottom. Medium-thick curly noodles are springy, and the chashu is thick and tender. At lunch until 3 pm, the set adds tamago kake gohan with niboshi furikake for ¥1,100 (May 2026). Two regulars usually order the tsukemen. In September 2026 a chilled shoyu ramen with frozen-broth ice was ¥1,200, and limited back-fat, shio and spicy versions ran April–June 2026. A couple of reviewers found it merely average. Buy a ticket at the machine. Closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Ramen · 24-hour Takaida-style shoyu ramen by Kuromon] A cramped ten-seat counter by Kuromon Market serving Takaida-style ramen around the clock; it's closed only Thursdays and the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays. Reviewers call the brand "7.5Hz" or "Nanahan". The bowl is a rich, sharp soy broth with more acidity than one visitor expected, thick straight noodles with low moisture, and chashu, best with an extra heap of chopped green onion. One reviewer who knows the original Takaida shop found the same chashu and noodles here, with a slightly milder broth. Chuka soba is ¥800 and a large chashu ramen ¥1,100 (September–October 2026). There's a garlic spice on the counter. People drop in after a night out, or for a morning bowl at 8 am. One person works the shop at a time, and a service charge may be added.

chef_bio.background: A Kuromon branch of the Takaida-style ramen shop Menya 7.5Hz (September 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "While the service differs from the Takai-da branch, the basic concept remains the same. The flavor of the chashu is identical, and the noodles taste the same as well. However, the broth seems slightly milder here." — September 2026.
"The broth, which had a stronger acidity than I expected. The noodles were straight and had a low moisture content." — October 2026, late night, chuka soba with green onions.

places.cuisine: Tonkotsu shoyu ramen that looks rich but eats light, medium-thick noodles, firmness to order · original-flavor ramen and pork-bowl set ¥1,280 · ajitama ramen under ¥1,000 · abura soba ¥1,000 with three chashu, white onion and sesame · spicy meat mazesoba · tsukemen, large free · pork bowl stir-fried to order · eel bowl · pickled ginger and yuzu pepper on the counter · 16 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · light tonkotsu shoyu beside Nankai Namba] A 16-seat counter right beside Nankai Namba Station, open since 2019 and good value. Every ramen here is pork-bone based, and though it looks rich and fatty it eats surprisingly light, with a depth of dashi and medium-thick noodles that soak it up. Generous crunchy green onions add to that. Say how firm you want the noodles when you hand over your ticket. Pickled ginger from the counter works well with the tonkotsu. The ramen-and-pork-bowl set is ¥1,280 (September 2026), and the pork is stir-fried after you order. There's also abura soba (¥1,000) with three slices of chashu, spicy meat mazesoba that can sell out, and tsukemen with a free large size. One diner found it a bit salty. Tabelog only says it opens at 11:00, so check closing times.

chef_bio.background: Second branch of Tenchijin Ramen (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Light tonkotsu shoyu ramen; pork bowl.

anecdotes.text: "At first glance, it looks like it would be rich and fatty, but surprisingly, it was light and easy to eat—delicious! The noodles were medium-thick and absorbed the broth well." — October 2026, second visit.

"The broth was a bit lighter, but it had a rich tonkotsu flavor with a nice depth from the dashi… the combination of tonkotsu and ginger was fantastic." — September 2026, original-flavor ramen and pork-bowl set ¥1,280.

places.notes: [Standing bar · a Tabelog 100 tachinomi with no sign, behind Namba] A small standing bar just off Midosuji near Namba Hips, named to Tabelog's 2025 standing-bar 100 and a sister of Oishi Stand. There's no sign, so it's easy to walk past; the shop's Instagram says to look for it. It gets packed; one evening a regular shuffled over to make room. Reviewers note many women among the crowd, unusual for a tachinomi. Small plates make it easy to try a lot. The cream cheese with crackers, slightly sweet, won over one reviewer who doesn't usually like cream cheese, and the blue cheese has fans too. There's Shine Muscat with prosciutto as shira-ae, an Ezo venison steak served rare, and house satsuma-age with cheese, corn and edamame, fried after you order. A hamburger is limited to three servings. Expect ¥2,000–4,000. Cash only. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Sister shop of Oishi Stand (August 2026 review); Tabelog tachinomi 100, 2025 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: House-made dishes, down to the satsuma-age (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "On Instagram, it said, 'There's no sign, so please find us,' and I actually walked past it without realizing it! The small interior was packed. A regular customer kindly moved to make space for me." — October 2026.

"Even for someone like me who doesn't usually like solid cheese or plain cream cheese, it was absolutely amazing… It's slightly sweet, and when paired with the crackers that come with it, it's just perfect!" — October 2026, second visit.

places.cuisine: American burgers and world bottled beer since 2011 · cheeseburger ¥1,480, drink set +¥350 (July 2026) · bacon cheeseburger · avocado burger · pulled-pork burger with barbecue sauce · macaroni-topped burger featured on TV · grilled-cheese sandwich with bacon and avocado on whole-wheat bread · crisp fries · craft and bottled beers · 6 counter and 14 table seats
places.notes: [Burgers · American burgers and world beer by Hozenji] A stylish American-style burger bar a few steps from the Hozenji entrance, open since 2011 and drawing overseas guests too. The toasted buns get singled out; one burger hunter ranked it in a personal top three, buns especially. The cheeseburger is ¥1,480, plus ¥350 for a drink (July 2026). The bacon cheeseburger layers thick bacon over a juicy patty, and the avocado burger is creamy and rich. The tender pulled pork with an addictive barbecue sauce looks as good as it does on Instagram. A macaroni-topped burger has been on TV. The grilled-cheese sandwich comes on toasted whole-wheat bread with thick bacon and avocado, and the chef adjusted the cheese on request. The fries are crisp without being greasy. There's a long list of bottled beers from around the world. Lunch is burgers only. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: American-style burger and beer bar by Hozenji Yokocho (Tabelog); official site kokopelli-nanba.jp.

anecdotes.text: "I've been to various famous burger joints, but this one ranks in my top three for taste, especially the buns, which might be the best I've ever had." — July 2026, cheeseburger ¥1,480.
"The pulled pork was incredibly tender and juicy, making it delicious, and the barbecue sauce was quite addictive." — February 2026.

places.cuisine: Creative Japanese courses rooted in kappo tradition, with jazz playing · weekday lunch mini course with seasonal clay-pot rice ¥3,000 · lunch course ¥5,000 · seasonal clay-pot rice (corn, scallop and shiso; chestnut), leftovers made into rice balls to take home · lotus-root dumpling soup with broccoli sauce · fried sanma salad or chicken thigh · crispy okra · sea bream, amberjack and octopus sashimi · sake and wine · counter and private rooms, 18 seats
places.notes: [Japanese · a hidden creative kappo by Hozenji Yokocho] A creative kappo counter with private rooms, tucked deep inside a nondescript building by Hozenji Yokocho, open since 2021. Finding the door takes some effort. The kitchen builds colorful courses on Japanese seasonal tradition. Lunch is the easy way in: a weekday mini course with seasonal clay-pot rice for ¥3,000, or ¥5,000 for more. Recent courses ran from a lotus-root dumpling in vivid broccoli sauce to fried sanma served as a salad, with crispy okra among the starters. The clay-pot rice, chestnut in autumn or corn, scallop and shiso in summer, leaves enough for seconds, and what's left is made into rice balls to take home. Several diners praise the tableware and care. One critic found the dishes pre-plated and the egg rice hard and clumped. Dinner runs about ¥8,000–15,000. Closed most Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Contemporary kappo with jazz music and private rooms (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Creative dishes rooted in Japanese seasonal tradition but not limited to it (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The chestnut rice, cooked in a clay pot, was so delicious that even after a second helping, there was still some left." — October 2026, ¥5,000 lunch course; the rest was made into rice balls to take home.
"Most of the dishes are pre-cooked (essentially prepared in advance) and served already plated." — October 2026, a critical review.

Reservations accepted; at dinner, groups with children are seated in a private room. A 5% year-end fee applies 15 December–4 January (Tabelog). Cards, QUICPay, PayPay and Alipay accepted.

places.cuisine: Kobe-beef teppanyaki at a counter overlooking Dotonbori · omakase courses with a choice of black wagyu, Matsusaka or Kobe beef · 14-course black-wagyu strip loin omakase ¥12,000, five-glass wine pairing ¥4,400 (April 2026) · anniversary omakase with tenderloin ¥16,000 (July 2026) · seared wagyu sushi · teppan-fried Nagasaki horse mackerel with pickle tartar · wagyu dumplings in consommé · pan-seared sea bass with shiso genovese · kamadaki rice from Gihei with red miso soup · garlic rice · English menu · 14 seats
places.notes: [Teppanyaki · Kobe-beef teppanyaki with a Dotonbori night view] A 14-seat teppanyaki counter on the eighth floor above Yoshinoya, looking out over the lights of Dotonbori. The head chef came up through luxury hotels (reviewers name the St. Regis Osaka and the Ritz), and the cooking shows it. You choose black wagyu, Matsusaka or Kobe beef for the omakase. A 14-course black-wagyu strip loin course was ¥12,000 (April 2026), and an anniversary course with tenderloin ¥16,000. Beyond the steak, diners rave about the seafood: crisp-skinned sea bass with shiso genovese, and teppan-fried Nagasaki horse mackerel with a pickle tartar, one diner's best ever. Wagyu dumplings in consommé and seared wagyu sushi round it out, and rice cooked in a kamado from Kyoto's Gihei closes the meal. One diner found the seasoning a little salty. Many guests are from abroad; the menu is in English and staff speak English.

chef_bio.background: Head chef trained in hotel kitchens, previously at the St. Regis Osaka and the Ritz (July 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Some dishes run a food-cost ratio above 40% (July 2026 review).

places.notes: [Ramen · a six-seat morning-ramen counter in Shimanouchi] A six-seat counter in Shimanouchi, rated 3.64 on Tabelog, open since 2022 and run by the owner with one helper. The owner previously worked at Menya Joroku and runs the six-seat counter with one female staff member. It opens at 7 am on weekends, and lines can form outside by 8. The regular menu is shoyu: a chicken and seafood broth that's easy to drink to the last drop, chewy flat whole-wheat noodles from Menya Teikaku, and in the Shoyu Special (¥1,600) four kinds of chashu, from low-temperature chicken breast to hanging-roasted pork belly. The fun is the rotating bowls announced on social media. Recent ones included a cement-gray niboshi soba from Himi sardines that is clean, with no bitterness, a clear niboshi-and-scallop shio, a thick crab-and-scallop shio, and a tachiuo tsukemen with a raw-egg kamatama dip. Finish with a ¥100 bowl of rice in the leftover soup. There are no table condiments. Cash only, and bring small notes for the machine. One first-timer singled out the owner's service. Check X or Instagram for closures.

places.notes: [Ramen · a new iekei shop by Kuromon] An iekei ramen counter in a quieter part of Kuromon Market, opened in summer 2026 by an owner who trained in the Kanto region; one reviewer says at Men Master Takenaka in Tokyo. The broth is made in-house and the noodles come from Suzuki Seimen. Reviewers split on the broth: one found it bold, salty and deeply colored, others say the salt is toned down so it's easier to drink than most iekei. Either way, set firmness, richness and chicken oil to taste. The noodles are firmer and more wheaty than usual, so one diner suggests ordering them softer. Prices are fair for the market: regular ¥900, large ¥1,100, with ajitama ¥150, extra chashu ¥400 and spinach ¥200 (September–October 2026). The moist, lightly roasted chashu stands out. Get rice and wrap it in nori. The owner works fast and keeps the energy up. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style staff-meal ramen near NGK] A Jiro-style shop a short walk from NGK, open since 2011, with 18 counter seats and a line of about ten at busy times. The menu is built on the "staff meal": a rich pork-bone broth in shoyu, shio or miso, 400 g of thick, chewy noodles even in a regular, a heap of bean sprouts, generous back fat and two thick slices of chashu. Garlic is your call; the vegetables and fat are fixed. The shoyu staff meal is ¥950 and the shio ¥980 (October 2026). There's a ladies' size, the oil can be halved, and there's a ponzu ramen made with Asahi Ponzu, and a daily-limited rich tsukemen with a ponzu tang. Fans add Tabasco or vinegar near the end to cut the richness. One longtime visitor was underwhelmed. Buy a ticket at the machine.

places.notes: [Ramen · clear tonkotsu chuka soba by Nankai Namba] A ramen shop under a bright yellow sign beside Nankai Namba Station, open since June 2025 and run, per one reviewer, by Yoshinoya Holdings. The specialty surprises people: tonkotsu that's transparent rather than cloudy, in the style of Tokyo's "chan-kei" chuka soba. It's light, with the pork's richness coming through without the heaviness, and plenty of thinly sliced chashu over smooth thin noodles. One diner found it strongly salty, another wanted more punch. Try it plain, then work through the condiments as the shop's guide suggests. The pork-bone clear soup noodles are ¥1,000 (September 2026). A menu revamp on 17 September 2026 added a back-fat chuka soba with rice for ¥880, and there's a spicy umami soba (¥1,000) with optional extra heat. Bottled beer and a ¥500 snack plate of toppings make it a quick drinking stop.

chef_bio.background: Operated by Yoshinoya Holdings (June 2025 review).

anecdotes.text: "When it arrived, my first thought was, 'Is this really tonkotsu?' The broth was surprisingly clear, unlike the typical thick, cloudy tonkotsu." — September 2026, chuka soba with extra pork fat.
"I had heard that it's rare to find a 'chan' style ramen in Namba… The broth was transparent and had a smooth, light flavor without any strong aftertaste." — September 2026.

places.notes: [Chinese · Sichuan beef noodles in Shimanouchi] A small beef-noodle shop in Shimanouchi run by a chef from Sichuan, where most customers and staff are Chinese and the ticket machine is labeled in Chinese. There's always a line, and each bowl is made with care, so allow time; one diner spent an hour from the door to the bowl. The draw is hong shao beef noodles, rich and aromatic with real Sichuan-pepper numbing. There are also premium beef noodles, a spicy beef noodle soup with tender marinated beef and chewy noodles, and a fat-intestine version. Add honeycomb tripe. You pick the numbing and the heat, and even "mild" makes people sweat. One diner found medium numbing and medium spice perfectly balanced. There's no rice to finish. Closed Sundays. Cash only.

Flat, chewy whole-wheat noodles are good enough to eat plain, and a large portion is free. The dip sits over a small flame and stays boiling hot to the last bite, so mind the bowl. Choose the house kombu-water tsukemen or the rich chicken-and-seafood one (¥1,200 with an ajitama, October 2026). There's also a special rich shrimp version with sakura shrimp and a spicy tamago tsukemen. Squeeze sudachi or lime over the noodles near the end. One diner missed a soup-wari to thin the rich dip, which isn't offered. Expect a 20–30 minute line at weekend lunch. The crowd skews to visitors from abroad.

places.notes: [Yakitori · a 1958 yakitori counter by Hozenji] A 12-seat L-shaped counter a few steps from Mizukake Fudo in Hozenji Yokocho, grilling yakitori since 1958. A long-time customer remembers the shop under the previous owner, the second generation. The second- and third-generation owners now run it together and keep the old flavors. Chicken from Ise Akadori, shamo and Tajima birds goes over Kishu binchotan. The tare is just soy sauce and sake, rich and smooth with no extra sweetness, and diners say it lets the chicken speak. First-timers must take a course (Matsu, Take or Ume; one group paid ¥6,000 a head for a course in September 2026) and can order à la carte afterward. Expect negima, chicken breast with shiso and ume, the house Midori-yaki, chicken skin, "tulip" wings and stuffed shiitake, with onsen egg and yamakake on the side. Check sake prices, which add up fast. One September diner found the meat tough and the hygiene off-putting. Book ahead; closed Sundays.

places.cuisine: Zenzai (sweet red-bean soup) since 1883 · Meoto Zenzai ¥820: one serving split into two small bowls, Tanba Dainagon azuki with a few whole beans, a rice-cake dumpling, salt kombu and green tea · chilled zenzai in summer · matcha-azuki kakigori · Meoto Zenzai goods · 18 seats at 5 tables
places.notes: [Japanese sweets · the zenzai shop of Oda Sakunosuke's story, by Hozenji] The zenzai shop beside Mizukake Fudo in Hozenji Yokocho, dating to 1883 and made famous by Oda Sakunosuke's novel "Meoto Zenzai". The signature (¥820, September 2026) arrives as one serving split into two small bowls, a nod to a married couple, and ordering it as a couple is said to bring luck. Don't share: it's one order per guest. The zenzai is made with Tanba Dainagon azuki, gently sweet and a little thick, with a few whole beans and a soft rice-cake dumpling. Salt kombu and green tea cut the sweetness, and staff refill the tea. In summer there's a chilled zenzai, plus matcha-azuki kakigori. Today it's run by the Wasyoku Sato group and open 10 am to 10 pm, handy for dessert after takoyaki. There's a shelf of Meoto Zenzai souvenirs.

chef_bio.background: Linked to Oda Sakunosuke's novel "Meoto Zenzai" (September–October 2026 reviews); part of the Wasyoku Sato group (September 2026 review; official page on sato-res.com).
chef_bio.philosophy: One serving in two bowls, for a harmonious couple (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The specialty here is served in two bowls, representing a harmonious couple, and it is said that ordering it as a couple brings good fortune (however, sharing one serving between two people is considered bad luck)." — October 2026.
"The zenzai made with Tanba Dainagon red beans has a subtle sweetness, allowing the flavor of the beans to shine through, with a few whole beans remaining." — September 2026, Meoto Zenzai ¥820.

places.notes: [Tempura · an 8-seat tempura counter in Hozenji Yokocho] A bright, clean eight-seat tempura counter on the cobbled lanes of Hozenji Yokocho, open since July 2025. Each piece is fried in front of you and served at once: a crisp, light batter that isn't greasy, with the seafood and vegetables tasting of themselves. The ¥12,000 course (November 2025 and January 2026) runs from three appetizers and three sashimi through ten tempura, such as shrimp, crab, large scallop, milt, sweet potato and persimmon, then noodles, rice and dessert. There are surprises, like kiwi tempura. Dip in matcha salt, yuzu salt or tentsuyu with grated daikon, and the staff will suggest which. You can also order à la carte. The chef is cheerful and chatty. Upstairs, the shop's sake bar AWA pours a wide range of sake and whisky for after. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Seasonal tempura counter with a sake bar, AWA, on the second floor (March 2026 reviews); official site tempura-tenzan.com.
chef_bio.philosophy: Fresh seasonal ingredients fried with careful temperature control (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The batter was crispy, while the inside remained fluffy, resulting in a light dish without any greasiness. With a variety of dipping options including matcha salt, yuzu salt, and a broth with grated Japanese radish." — January 2026, ¥12,000 course.
"And I was surprised by the tempura made with kiwi… Moreover, this restaurant actually has a Japanese sake bar called AWA on the second floor." — March 2026.

places.notes: [Yakitori · a one-owner, all-night yakitori bar off Shinsaibashi-suji] A long, narrow yakitori bar just east of the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade, open from 6 pm until 6 am most nights, mostly run single-handed by a friendly owner. Skewers are mainly salt-grilled over charcoal, and one diner ordered extra chicken skin. Chicken sashimi, seared chicken and avocado yukke are popular. A whiteboard lists daily extras, from octopus to garlic shrimp, and grilled rice balls in house chicken broth close the night. The all-you-can-drink courses are good value (¥2,750 with three dishes in April 2025, ¥4,950 with skewers and sashimi in March 2025). Reserve ahead, since one person runs the room; solo bookings are fine. It's a smoking bar full of regulars keeping bottles, and you can't see in from the street. One January 2026 visitor found it average. The newest review is from January 2026, so check before going.

chef_bio.background: The owner usually runs the bar alone (November 2024 and March 2025 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fresh chicken at reasonable prices (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The yakitori is primarily seasoned with salt, and the chicken sashimi, seared chicken, and yukke are delicious too… grilled rice balls served with a homemade chicken broth that wraps everything up perfectly." — November 2024.

"The course includes yakitori, chicken sashimi, and a special ponzu sauce with hinokawa (young chicken), along with two side dishes and grilled rice balls to finish, all for JPY 4950 with all-you-can-drink included." — March 2025.

places.cuisine: Takaida-style chuka soba, Tabelog Ramen 100 every year 2017–2025 · near-black shoyu broth that is lighter than it looks, black pepper, medium-thick straight noodles, thin chashu, menma, green onion · small ¥900, regular ¥1,000 · hayazushi ¥200, wrapped in leaves from Wakayama · shrimp shio ramen with sakura shrimp and niboshi · first-Sunday morning ramen · 7 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Takaida-style black chuka soba, a Tabelog 100 regular] A seven-seat counter down a narrow alley near NGK, named to Tabelog's ramen 100 every year from 2017 to 2025, with lines and a waiting area at lunch. It opened in 2008 at Tempozan Marketplace and moved to Namba in 2010. The chuka soba is Takaida-style: a broth that looks nearly black and smells strongly of soy, yet drinks lighter and less salty than you'd expect, with black pepper on top. Medium-thick straight noodles soak it up, with thin chashu, menma and green onion. A small is ¥900 and a regular ¥1,000 (October 2026). Add the ¥200 hayazushi, vinegared rice wrapped in leaves from Wakayama. There's also a shrimp shio with sakura shrimp and niboshi, limited bowls such as a garlic ramen on special days, and on the first Sunday of the month it opens at 7 am for morning ramen. A Hokkaido visitor found the soy too assertive. Cash only; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog Ramen WEST/OSAKA 100, 2017–2025 (Tabelog); official blog jouroku.blog.fc2.com.

anecdotes.text: "While the broth looked pitch black, which made me think it would be overly salty, I was amazed by the rich flavor that didn't taste salty at all!" — October 2026, chuka soba.
"The Hayazushi is wrapped in the leaves of the Koshiji plant from Wakayama… The vinegared rice is firm, making it easy to eat quickly." — October 2026, hayazushi ¥200 and chuka soba (regular) ¥1,000.

places.cuisine: Fukuchan-group shoyu ramen · Japanese-style ramen ¥880 from a chicken and pork-bone shoyu broth, medium straight noodles, one slice of chashu, menma, nori and a heap of white and green onion · tsukemen with a lighter dip and thinner noodles, thick pork-belly chashu · pork rice bowl (not late at night) · kimchi or menma ¥150 · canned beer ¥400 · pickled ginger on the counter · 12 seats at an L-shaped counter
places.notes: [Ramen · late-night Fukuchan-group shoyu ramen by Kuromon] A 12-seat L-shaped counter near Kuromon Market from the Fukuchan group, the sister of Fukuchan Ramen and Otoko Juku, open until 3 am. The basic Japanese-style ramen (¥880, April and September 2026) is a mild shoyu on chicken and pork bones with medium straight noodles, a thick slice of chashu, menma, nori and plenty of white and green onion. It's crowd-pleasing rather than distinctive. One regular prefers the tsukemen, with a lighter-than-usual dip, thinner noodles and thick, chilled pork-belly chashu. The pork rice bowl is a favorite but isn't served late at night. Sides are just ramen toppings (¥150), and drinks just canned beer (¥400). Prices run higher than at the second branch, with no free extra noodles. Smoking is allowed. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Tenchijin, a Fukuchan-group brand (fukuchan.co.jp); sister of Fukuchan Ramen and Otoko Juku (April 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "Broth: A soy sauce base made from chicken and pork bones. Noodles: Medium-sized straight noodles. Toppings: One slice of chashu, menma, one sheet of grilled nori, and a generous amount of white and chopped green onions." — April 2026, Japanese-style ramen ¥880.
"It has a lighter broth, which makes it a bit unique. The noodles are thinner, and it feels more like ramen that has been transformed into tsukemen." — July 2026, tsukemen.

places.cuisine: Noodle shop open 8 am to 3 am · four tsukemen (duck, motsu, special and more) with your choice of thick udon, thin udon, Chinese noodles or soba · duck tsukemen with grilled leek and lemon · motsu tsukemen · katsu udon with mizuna · ramen · counter seats, self-service
places.notes: [Noodles · an 8 am–3 am tsukemen and udon shop by Nagahoribashi] A self-service noodle counter a short walk from Nagahoribashi, open from 8 in the morning until 3 at night, so it works for breakfast, lunch or the last stop of the evening. There are four tsukemen, and you pick the noodle when you sit down: thick udon, thin udon, Chinese noodles or soba. Several reviewers pick the Chinese noodles. The motsu tsukemen comes with plenty of offal in a seafood-tinged dip, and the duck tsukemen has duck slices, grilled leek and lemon. There's also katsu udon with mizuna, and ramen. Opinions vary: one diner found the duck dip very sweet and watched staff mix it from cartons. Another noted prices have gone up. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Udon-and-tsukemen shop with a choice of four noodles (July–August 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Tsukemen with a choice of noodle; katsu udon.

anecdotes.text: "There were four options: thick udon, thin udon, Chinese noodles, and soba. I was in the mood for ramen this morning, so I chose the Chinese noodles." — July 2026, duck tsukemen at 8 am.
"There was plenty of motsu (offal) in it, and it had a delicious seafood-like flavor!" — August 2026, motsu tsukemen with Chinese noodles.

places.cuisine: Osaka-style curry rice, sweet then spicy, thick and rich · pork cutlet curry ¥930 · large katsu curry with sausage ¥1,400 · fried-shrimp curry with the curry kept off the shrimp · chicken curry · toppings: pork or chicken cutlet, soft-boiled egg, cheese, Kujo green onion, spinach, sausage · pickles, shallots and English-labeled sauces on the counter · 10 seats at an L-shaped counter
places.notes: [Curry · a 10-seat Osaka-style curry counter on Nansan-dori] A narrow ten-seat curry counter on Nansan-dori, three minutes from Nankai Namba, open since 2016 and busy with visitors from abroad. The curry is Osaka-style: thick and rich, sweet up front and then a gentle spice, with a nostalgic, European-style depth. The pork cutlet curry is fried to order and was ¥930 in July 2026. One diner had a large katsu curry with sausage for ¥1,400. Fried-shrimp curry comes with the curry kept off the shrimp so the coating stays crisp. Toppings run from cheese and soft-boiled egg to Kujo green onion and spinach. "Medium spicy" is mild, and there's chili sauce on the counter, along with pickles and English-labeled sauces. The ticket machine sends your order straight to the kitchen, so food comes fast. Open every day.

chef_bio.background: Ticket-machine curry counter on Nansan-dori (July–September 2026 reviews).
