places.notes: [Ramen · a Tokyo shio-soba shop's Osaka branch in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] An eight-seat counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, the Osaka branch of a Tokyo shio-soba shop that reviewers describe as a Tabelog 100 and Michelin-listed name, open since spring 2026. Lines form within minutes of opening. The special shio soba (¥1,480, May and October 2026) is a clear, light chicken broth with a hint of seafood, over thin square-cut noodles from Takai-do Seimen. It comes loaded with four chashu, from low-temperature Daisendori chicken to juicy pork belly, plus a chicken-cartilage tsukune scented with ginger or yuzu, kaiware and menma. One diner wanted more salt; another found the salt pronounced. On weekends there's a special ura shoyu soba at the same price. The set adds a chashu rice bowl heaped with meat. It's cramped when full, and one diner found service slow. Cash only.

places.cuisine: Rich, thick ramen and tsukemen, open to 5 am · ramen ¥800, small ¥100 less, extra noodles ¥180 · tsukemen with thick noodles in a rich chicken-bone, pork-bone and vegetable dip, chashu, menma, ajitama and shredded green onion · spicy green-onion ramen · all-toppings ramen · vinegar, pepper and chili oil on the counter · 8 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · rich late-night ramen near Otaro Road, open to 5 am] An old-school eight-seat counter near Otaro Road, open since 2009 and serving until 5 am, a favorite after a night out or a missed last train. The ramen is thick and rich, with noodles that soak it up and good chashu. It's ¥800 (April 2026), ¥100 less for a small, and ¥180 for a full extra serving of noodles. The tsukemen pairs thick noodles with a rich dip of chicken bones, pork bones and vegetables, plus chashu, menma, a seasoned egg and plenty of shredded green onion, good with a cold beer. The spicy green-onion ramen has a moderate kick. Vinegar, pepper and chili oil sit on the counter. Expect overseas visitors and a short queue late on weekdays. Buy a ticket at the machine; cash only. Closed Tuesdays.

anecdotes.text: "The dipping sauce was rich, made from chicken bones, pork bones, and vegetables. It had a deep flavor, enhanced by the aroma of green onions, making it impossible to stop dipping the thick noodles." — September 2026, tsukemen late at night.

places.notes: [Ramen · Hokkaido and Kyushu miso ramen in Sennichimae] A miso-ramen specialist in Sennichimae, open since 2014, with fair prices for Namba. The menu runs on regional misos. The Hokkaido "100-year miso" vegetable ramen comes topped with crunchy stir-fried bean sprouts, onion, carrot, garlic chives and cabbage over a thick, roasted-tasting broth. The Hokkaido miso with egg is ¥1,150 and the Kyushu miso ¥1,030 (June and September 2026). A limited golden grilled miso had a striking aroma yet stayed easy to drink. Medium-thick, smooth noodles hold up well, and even a regular is filling. One returning diner found the room a little worn after ten years, but the bowl as good as ever. Open daily; PayPay accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · clam and shijimi ramen south of Nankai Namba] A roomy shellfish-ramen shop three minutes from Nankai Namba's south exit, open since 2022, with tables that work for families. The clam ramen packs plenty of clams into a shoyu broth with deep shellfish umami, and big slices of rare chashu drape the rim, softening when dipped. Thick crunchy menma and shredded white negi keep it lively. The shijimi ramen is lighter, a good post-drinks bowl, and one regular always orders it. In summer there's a cold clam ramen with myoga (staff check you're fine with it). The "golden" TKM is egg-yolk-coated noodles scented with scallop broth, with rice to mop up the sauce. The noodles seem to be whole-grain, with a strong wheat flavor. One diner wanted a bigger portion, so consider a large. Cash only.

chef_bio.philosophy: A commitment to shellfish broth (October 2026 review).

Buy a ticket at the machine out front and wait for your number, which can be hard to hear. The takoyaki come fast off a very hot griddle: fluffy outside, gooey and piping hot inside, with decent pieces of octopus. Ask for extra mayonnaise and aonori if you like. The largest order is 12 pieces, and there's a takoyaki-and-beer set served in a cute octopus-shaped tray. It's busy with visitors from abroad, and one diner found the service a little perfunctory. places.notes: [Yakitori · binchotan yakitori in a Dotonbori basement] A basement yakitori bar on Dotonbori's main street, open since 2016, grilling fresh chicken over binchotan. Dinner starts with a ¥385 bowl of grated daikon that's refilled for free. The signature is chicken-thigh tataki (¥858), crisp skin over a rare, tender center. Skewers start at ¥297, and the neck, skirt and liver get the praise, along with heart, wings and vegetables like shiitake and cherry tomato. Don't skip the wing-tip kara-age in three flavors: soy, sweet-spicy yangnyeom and tartar nanban. Finish with the rich grilled rice ball under egg yolk and shaved cheese, or a yakitori ramen with a whole skewer on top. The menu comes in English, Chinese and Korean. Open nightly until midnight.

chef_bio.philosophy: Freshly sourced chicken over binchotan (May 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The signature dish, chicken thigh tataki, features crispy, fragrant skin and a rare, tender interior." — May 2026, ¥858.

"The soy sauce version is a classic and delicious choice, the Yangnyeom has a sweet and spicy sauce that's addictive, and the Tartar Nanban is generously topped with rich tartar sauce." — May 2026, chicken wing kara-age.

places.notes: [Teppanyaki · casual wagyu teppanyaki in Souemoncho, open to 3 am] A 19-seat teppanyaki counter opposite Queens Court in Souemoncho, open since 2020 and serving until 3 am. The star is a limited domestic black-wagyu filet; in July 2026 it was an A5 chateaubriand, seared on the teppan and rested to medium-rare with rosemary; an August diner had it with mashed potatoes. Beyond steak there's wagyu ichibo roast beef, Hokkaido scallop and asparagus in butter soy, a seafood yakisoba, Camembert fondue and white fish with Genoa sauce. Courses add a truffle-scented salad and a pairing of sirloin cap and filet, with wasabi, salt, soy, garlic chips and truffle oil to dip. Reviewers spent ¥5,000–15,000. The shop says on Tabelog that it can handle allergies and vegetarian requests, so say what you need when booking. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Casual teppanyaki in Souemoncho (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Selected ingredients at reasonable prices; allergies and vegetarian options accommodated (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I had the Japanese Black Wagyu A5 Filet Steak, and to my surprise, it was made with the rare cut, Chateaubriand!" — July 2026; it was cooked evenly, then rested on a plate to finish in its own heat.

places.notes: [Yakiniku · a five-seat yakiniku counter in a Souemoncho alley] A five-seat yakiniku counter tucked into a narrow Souemoncho alley, cramped enough that you'll be elbow to elbow, and the kind of casual, affordable solo spot that's getting rare in Minami. A new owner took over in 2025, and a returning diner in July 2026 felt the meat had improved since the change. Everything comes in half portions, so one person can work through salted tongue, cheek, premium loin and kalbi. Omasum, tetchan intestine and liver have fans too. Ask about the off-menu ajillo, grilled rice balls and miso pasta, and finish with fried rice or cold noodles. Expect about ¥3,000–5,000. Book ahead. Smoking is allowed. Closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Ramen · Hakata Ippudo by Nankai Namba] The Namba branch of the Hakata Ippudo chain, three minutes from Nankai Namba and open until 1 am on Fridays and Saturdays. It's busy with visitors from abroad. Reviewers split between the Akamaru Shinaji, with a touch of spicy miso, and the plain Shiromaru tonkotsu, with thin noodles cooked to one of four firmness levels from barikata (extra firm) to yawa (soft). Order a kaedama for more noodles. Ask the staff for the free spicy bean sprouts, takana, pickled ginger and garlic; they come in a generous dish. Limited bowls rotate, such as a garlicky vegetable miso ramen in April and an abura-soba in September 2026. The Ippudo app gives coupons for things like a free egg or extra noodles.

places.notes: [Ramen · Tenka Ippin's kotteri ramen opposite WINS Namba] A 52-seat branch of the Tenka Ippin chain a minute from Nankai Namba's west exit, open since 2003. Everyone comes for the kotteri: a famously thick, rich broth, ¥920 in October 2026. Stir in spicy miso from the table, and load a side plate from the self-service corner with pickled cucumber (which tastes of garlic), red ginger, spicy takana and grated garlic. Green onions were dropped from the corner because of rising prices. Gyoza with crisp edges, fried rice, and a lunch set with a chashu rice bowl fill it out, and a summer cold ramen had a refreshing citrus broth. On Tenka Ippin Day, 1 October, visitors get coupons, and lines form by evening. Closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Tenka Ippin chain (tenkaippin.co.jp).

anecdotes.text: "At the service corner, I prepared some pickled cucumbers, red ginger, and spicy takana on a small plate… When the ramen arrived, I added some spicy miso." — October 2026, rich ramen.

"I noticed several changes, such as a water dispenser being placed near the seating area and the absence of green onions at the service counter. I was told that the lack of green onions was due to rising prices." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kibou Ken's tonkotsu and spicy goma-miso, open to 6 am] A 28-seat counter on Nagahori-dori from the long-running Kibou Ken chain, open from 11 am until 6 am. Two styles anchor the menu. The tonkotsu has a thick broth clinging to thin noodles, not overwhelming, and a nostalgic Shinsaibashi taste for some. The goma-miso is nutty, with a spice level you choose; the "Ultra" level was just about manageable for one spice-shy diner. A regular with thousands of bowls logged swears by the spicy tsukemen (¥1,080, October 2026) and the goma-miso "Pirika" tsukemen, stirred with the free garlic and garlic-chive kimchi and finished with soup-wari. There's an ajitama for ¥120, gyoza and rice sets, hinepon and highballs. One returning diner thought it had slipped. Cash or PayPay.

chef_bio.background: Kibou Ken, a long-standing ramen chain (September 2026 review); official site kibou-ken.com.

anecdotes.text: "I mixed the garlic and kimchi into the broth, which had a spicy sesame miso flavor… After finishing the noodles, I enjoyed the broth with a dilution of soup." — October 2026, spicy tsukemen ¥1,080 with an ajitama ¥120.
"Their signature 'Tonkotsu Ramen' features a thick, flavorful broth that perfectly clings to the thin noodles." — July 2026.

places.notes: [Abura-soba · Roman's mazesoba stand beside the Nankai Namba south gate] A small, clean branch of the Roman abura-soba brand on the second floor of Nankai Namba Station, beside the south ticket gate, open since April 2025. It's convenient from the trains but a little tricky to find on foot. The mazesoba (¥1,000, September 2026) piles meat, egg and a rich sauce on chewy thick noodles, and the portion is generous. Add half rice at the end to soak up what's left. For the abura-soba, follow the shop's advice: two rounds of vinegar, chili oil to taste, extra sauce and a little garlic. One diner found it average and the staff chatter distracting. It also delivers. Cash only.

anecdotes.text: "The chewy thick noodles were perfectly coated with meat, egg, and a rich special sauce… Adding rice at the end mixed wonderfully with the remaining sauce." — July 2026, delivery.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura's cabbage shoyu by Shinsaibashi Station] A branch of the Dotonbori Kamukura chain a minute from Shinsaibashi Station on the Midosuji Line, open since 2021 and running through the night from Friday into Sunday morning. The "delicious ramen" (¥820, October 2026) is a light shoyu broth full of napa cabbage and pork, sweet from the vegetables and gentle enough to finish after a night out, with a large slice of chashu. Sets add gyoza, kara-age or rice. For autumn 2026 there's a limited black-vinegar suanla noodle on the house broth, until 4 November. Expect a short wait and slower service when busy with visitors; one diner waited 20 minutes at 10 pm after a concert.

places.notes: [Chinese · build-your-own malatang by Nagahoribashi] A two-floor malatang and hot-pot shop two minutes from Nagahoribashi, part of the Tonsha group, with a calm counter downstairs and private rooms upstairs. You order on your phone: pick from more than 40 ingredients and one of five spice levels, and the price isn't by weight, so a loaded bowl comes to about ¥1,300–1,500. The broth leans more numbing than hot, with real umami, and level 1 already has a kick. Fans recommend winter melon, white fungus, shrimp balls and knife-cut or sweet-potato noodles (two noodle types at most), with the sesame sauce and free green onion, coriander and garlic piled on. There's also a tomato mala soup with sweetness and acidity. Hot-pot courses run in the evening.

chef_bio.background: Tonsha malatang and hot-pot shops; this is the Nagahoribashi branch, with another in a station building (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The highlight of this place is the ability to customize your dish with over 40 ingredients and five levels of spiciness… making it easy to choose without worrying about weight-based pricing." — September 2026.
"The mala soup here has a stronger numbing sensation than spiciness… It's great that green onions and cilantro can be added for free!" — August 2026, level-2 mala soup ¥1,270.

places.cuisine: Kappa back-fat tonkotsu shoyu · Kappa ramen ¥930, ajitama +¥130 · Kuro Kappa with garlic oil · Aka Kappa with red chili · Aka Kappa chashu ramen · Kapa Saburo with a mountain of vegetables, back fat and thick noodles, ¥1,300 with ajitama · limited squid-ink Tsukimi ramen ¥1,100 and warm niboshi tsukemen ¥1,000 (2026) · free extra noodles and kimchi · fried garlic · half fried-rice set ¥330 · gyoza · 23 counter and 10 table seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Kappa's back-fat tonkotsu in Amerikamura, open to 4 am] The Amerikamura branch of the Kappa Ramen Honpo chain, three minutes from Yotsubashi and open until 4 am, a reliable stop after a night out. The base Kappa ramen (¥930, 2026) is a mild pork-bone shoyu with no off-smell. Kuro Kappa adds garlic oil and Aka Kappa red chili. Thin, well-drained noodles come with a free extra serving, and kimchi is free while you wait. The Kapa Saburo is the big one, with a mountain of vegetables, back fat and thick chewy noodles. Limited bowls rotate, like a jet-black squid-ink Tsukimi ramen with shiso in October 2026. Gyoza, a ¥330 half fried rice and fried garlic round it out, and there are snacks for a drink first.

anecdotes.text: "The broth, infused with garlic oil, was surprisingly not too heavy, offering a rich flavor that made me keep reaching for my spoon… I appreciated the free extra noodles." — August 2026, Kuro Kappa ¥930 + ajitama ¥130.

"The squid ink tonkotsu broth was jet black, packed with a powerful squid flavor and umami, creating a striking impact complemented by the refreshing aroma of shiso leaves." — October 2026, limited Tsukimi ramen ¥1,100.

places.cuisine: Hida Takayama-style chuka soba · light Japanese-style shoyu broth with bonito, super-thin curly noodles, big chashu, green onion and plenty of menma · house tsukemen, regular 130 g ¥1,100, with glossy flat noodles, kabosu and a chicken-and-bonito shoyu dip · grilled chashu · lunch sets with kara-age, rice or chashu rice bowl · counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Hida Takayama chuka soba near Nankai Namba] A modern counter near Nankai Namba, open since November 2023, serving the chuka soba of Hida Takayama in Gifu. The broth is a light, Japanese-style shoyu fragrant with bonito, and the noodles are startlingly thin, barely thicker than somen, so they slip right down. Toppings are a large chashu, green onion and plenty of menma. The house tsukemen (regular 130 g, ¥1,100, July 2026) arrives beautifully arranged: glossy flat noodles to dip in a chicken-and-bonito shoyu, with kabosu to squeeze over. Reviewers praise the grilled chashu. Lunch sets add kara-age with rice or a chashu rice bowl. It draws many overseas visitors.

chef_bio.background: Osaka Namba branch of Menya Shirakawa, serving Hida Takayama ramen from Gifu (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a Japanese-style soy sauce soup that spreads the umami and aroma of seafood, including bonito flakes. I was surprised by the noodles—they're super thin, just slightly thicker than somen." — October 2026, chuka soba.
"The glossy, wheat-colored flat noodles shone brightly. Squeezing some kabosu citrus enhanced the flavor even more." — July 2026, homemade tsukemen (regular, 130 g) ¥1,100.

places.cuisine: Okonomiyaki cooked in front of you at the counter · signature negiyaki "Fujiyama" piled with green onion, with beef tendon · seafood negiyaki with shrimp and octopus · mixed okonomiyaki · modan-yaki with noodles · tonpeiyaki · kimchi okonomiyaki · Sanpei set for two and pair set · batter made with soy milk and nagaimo · house blend of Osaka sauces · about 30 shochu · English menu · 15 counter seats
places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a negiyaki counter off Shinsaibashi-suji since 2004] A long counter under a red lantern, tucked into a building of snack bars off Shinsaibashi-suji, cooking okonomiyaki right in front of you since 2004. The draw is the negiyaki "Fujiyama", heaped with green onion over tender beef tendon; one visitor came back a year later just for it. The batter is made with soy milk and nagaimo for a smooth texture, and the sauce is a house blend of Osaka sauces. There's also a seafood negiyaki packed with shrimp and octopus, a well-balanced mixed okonomiyaki, a modan-yaki with chewy noodles and the popular tonpeiyaki, with around 30 shochu to drink. Sets for two let you try a mini negiyaki and two okonomiyaki. Prices are low for the area, and there's an English menu. No reservations; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Featured on Osaka TV programs in 2017 (Tabelog); official site okonomiyaki-sanpei.com.
chef_bio.philosophy: House batter with plenty of soy milk and nagaimo; a blend of Osaka sauces (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I was introduced to this restaurant by the concierge during my visit to Osaka last year, and I was amazed by the okonomiyaki with green onions and beef tendon." — September 2026, a return visit.
"The menu is now also available in English… I ordered the Negiyaki, and it was just as delicious as I remembered! My friend from Tokyo was surprised by the low prices." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Seafood · a six-seat lobster-and-wine counter off Shinsaibashi-suji] A privately run six-seat counter behind lanterns near Shinsaibashi-suji, open since 2013 and built for dates and celebrations. The shop describes itself as run by a couple, with warm hospitality and carefully chosen wines. The specialty is live lobster, steamed in front of you and served with three sauces; order it by the day before. The ¥12,000 course with lobster (January 2026) runs through inventive dishes such as a rich ajillo and a "Kanpou curry". À la carte there's meaty crab, big shrimp-and-chive dumplings and a shochu highball made with a whole lemon. Shared dishes come portioned for two, and there's a good wine list with pairings. Lunch is a chef's select course for one group a day, booked three days ahead. The master seems gruff at first but warms up. Note the tipping system and one-drink policy, and leave big luggage in a locker. Closed irregularly.

chef_bio.background: A small, privately run counter (Tabelog); official site kaiebi.com. The shop describes itself as run by a couple, with warm hospitality and carefully chosen wines (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.philosophy: Live lobster with wine for special occasions (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I had the satisfaction course featuring live lobster as the main dish (JPY 12,000)… This was my first time enjoying such plump and flavorful lobster. Personally, I loved the rich and savory ajillo." — January 2026.
"There are three different sauces to enhance the flavor… Be sure to make a reservation for the lobster by the day before!" — May 2026.

places.notes: [Yakiniku · a second-floor yakiniku counter from a meat supplier] A cozy second-floor yakiniku spot off Shinsaibashi-suji, run by a direct meat supplier, with a counter that works for solo diners and tables for groups. Ask the friendly master what's best today, and plates arrive in a well-paced order. Cuts run about ¥1,500–2,000 each (January 2026): thick salted tongue to finish with lemon, kuri, hanging tender, nakaochi, thin top blade and tripe. Regulars praise the quality for the price, though one August diner found the meat average. Finish with the strip-loin dashi chazuke or yuzu-tea rice. Courses can be built to a budget. It fills up on Fridays, but same-day online booking sometimes works. There's a ¥500 cover charge. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.philosophy: Premium cuts at wholesale value (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I order items like tongue, thinly sliced top blade, kuri (chestnut), hanging tender, and mountain chain tripe, all priced between JPY 1500 and JPY 2000, while asking the master for recommendations of the day." — January 2026.

places.notes: [Kushikatsu · creative kushikatsu beside Hozenji since 1946] A calm, jazz-playing kushikatsu counter right next to Mizukake Fudo in Hozenji Yokocho, from a kushikatsu house founded in 1946, with sister branches elsewhere. Thirty to forty creative skewers use seasonal ingredients in a light, crisp batter, each with its own sauce. The fun is the omakase: skewers keep coming one by one until you say stop. There are set courses too, such as a ¥5,720 seasonal course of ten skewers with fresh vegetables, a drink and ochazuke or rice with red miso soup (January 2025). Favorites include beef tenderloin, shrimp, pork, clams and whiting, and dessert might be a fig, with jasmine tea to close. One diner who has been coming for more than 50 years says it never sits heavy. Expect ¥8,000–15,000. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients in a light, crisp batter; omakase at your pace (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "Shiru Hisa is one of my favorite Osaka spots that I've been visiting for over 50 years… No matter how much you eat, the lightness of the dishes ensures that even my over-60 stomach feels great." — July 2026.
"Seasonal Special Course… JPY 5,720 x 2: 10 Assorted Select Kushi-katsu, Fresh Vegetables, 1 Drink, Choice of Ochazuke or Rice with Red Miso Soup." — January 2025.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kadoya Shokudo's tsukesoba in the Crysta Nagahori mall] A 28-seat counter branch of the well-known Kadoya Shokudo, in the Crysta Nagahori underground mall a short walk from Nagahoribashi, open since 2020. Most reviewers order the tsukesoba (¥1,550, October 2026): neatly folded, chewy, wheaty noodles dipped in a lightly tangy, slightly sweet soy broth with generous chashu, finished with soup-wari. One diner singled out the marinated egg, and the melt-in-the-mouth pig's trotters come with seasoned salt, garlic and doubanjiang. A chashu-mayo rice is ¥300. Expect about 15 minutes for tsukemen to boil. You can usually walk in, with no time limit, though a couple of diners found the noodles softer than at the main branch.

chef_bio.background: Branch of the Kadoya Shokudo ramen shop; reviewers compare it with the main branch (October 2026).

anecdotes.text: "I noticed a pleasantly chewy texture due to the higher water content… when I dipped it into the sauce, I found it to be a slightly sweet soy sauce broth that I could eat endlessly." — October 2026, tsukemen and pig's trotters.
"The noodles feel softer and thinner compared to what I had at the main branch… The dipping sauce is addictively tasty." — October 2026, tsukesoba ¥1,550, chashu mayo ¥300.

places.notes: [Ramen · a 7-seat chicken ramen counter by Yotsubashi] A seven-seat counter right by Yotsubashi Station, open since 2021, with a straightforward, high-quality chicken broth: no citrus or aroma oils, gentle salt, the chicken's sweetness up front. The shoyu is balanced and very drinkable, over flat, thin, smooth noodles. A standout is the limited cold genmaicha shio ramen (¥1,050, September–October 2026), roasted brown-rice tea in a chilled salt broth with chicken chashu, broccoli, cherry tomato and rice crackers. Finish with the ¥100 mini rice and wasabi poured over as tea porridge. A cold yuzu shio has appeared too, and the ¥400 aemen adds a second serving of noodles with diced chashu and fish powder. On Friday and Saturday evenings a small izakaya service adds drinks and plates. Cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Horie branch of Ramen Shion (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Chicken shio and shoyu; cold genmaicha shio.

anecdotes.text: "The chicken broth was straightforward, without any citrus or aromatic oils. The saltiness was gentle yet not too subtle, bringing out the sweetness of the chicken in a high-quality bowl." — September 2026.

"The soup is made with cold genmaicha, and the saltiness is just right, complementing the delicious flavor of the tea." — September 2026, cold genmaicha shio ramen ¥1,050, ajitama ¥150, mini rice ¥100.

places.notes: [Ramen · big-portion tsukemen south of Nankai Namba] A counter-only tsukemen and ramen shop south of Nankai Namba, open since 2022 in a space that once held a well-known tsukemen shop. Portions are the draw: the tsukemen (¥980, July 2026) comes with a big pile of flat, wheaty noodles, and a double portion is possible. The dip is soy-based, light and seafood-forward, and you can finish with soup-wari; one big eater found there wasn't enough dip for all the noodles. The chashu ramen has a light, well-balanced seafood broth on chewy medium-thick straight noodles, with good chashu. Reviews are mixed: one diner found the broth fishy and bitter, another called it unremarkable. Buy a ticket outside; cash only. Closed Wednesdays.

places.notes: [Ramen · light shrimp ramen by Kuromon Market] A nine-seat counter on the Nippombashi 2-chōme street by Kuromon Market, marked by stall-style plastic curtains, run by the owner with one helper and open since 2022. The owner and one female staff member run the nine-seat counter. Unlike the thick shrimp-miso style, the ebi shio here is light and gentle: a clear chicken-bone broth with a sauce from sweet shrimp, and the shrimp flavor hits from the first sip. It's ¥950, or ¥1,350 as the special (May and October 2026) with two wontons, bean sprouts and a hint of yuzu. You pick your chashu from thick pork belly, pork shoulder or fatty beef. The Kiwami Kuromon shoyu layers several soy sauces over chicken, pork, shrimp and scallop, with medium-thin noodles from Mie's Ayahikari flour; one diner found the soy drowned the shrimp. Most customers are visitors, and there's a short line at weekend lunch. Pay after eating, in cash.

places.notes: [Abura-soba · free-large abura-soba in Crysta Nagahori] A branch of the Ganso Aburado abura-soba chain in the Crysta Nagahori underground mall near Shinsaibashi, open since February 2026 and handy on a rainy day. The noodles are chewy and medium-thick in a slightly sweet, not-too-oily sauce; the "A" version with egg yolk and parmesan tastes almost like carbonara, and there's a spicy miso too. Large and extra-large are free, so many go big; a paid jumbo comes in a basin-sized bowl, though one diner found its toppings sparse. Grab free onion, pickled ginger and garlic, play with chili oil and vinegar, then add rice to the leftover sauce or ask for soup to finish it as ramen. Free drinks (jasmine and oolong tea, fruit water) and paper aprons make it good value. A cheese set is ¥1,000 (October 2026). Open daily until 11 pm.

places.notes: [Standing bar · a Tabelog 100 standing bar in an old house by Hozenji] A stylish, often-packed standing bar in a renovated old house on a back alley toward Hozenji, with beams and earthen walls, named to Tabelog's 2025 standing-bar 100. Downstairs you stand around the kitchen; upstairs is seated (¥330) with mobile ordering and its own menu. Big platters of daily obanzai line the counter. Small plates are cheap and inventive, mostly ¥380–600 (October 2026): assorted sashimi, spicy coriander pork shumai, fig and prosciutto with ricotta, smoked mayonnaise with chikuwa, and a squid liver in an Okinawan-style marinade that one regular orders every time. Bigger dishes include crab-miso cream croquettes, sanma confit with eggplant purée and rare wild boar with red wine sauce. Drinks run to mega highballs, fruit sours and a grated-peach bellini, and you can grab bottled beer from the self-service fridge.

chef_bio.background: Standing bar in a renovated old building; Tabelog tachinomi 100, 2025 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Daily obanzai and free-spirited snacks (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The squid liver in Okinawan-style marinade, which I order every time, pairs perfectly with drinks! Everyone also raved about the smoked mayonnaise!" — October 2026, second floor.
"The taste, presentation, speed of service, hospitality, interior design, and cost performance—all were outstanding." — October 2026, third stop of a bar crawl.

places.notes: [Gyoza · a nine-seat bite-size gyoza counter at the Mitsudera end] A nine-seat gyoza counter tucked into a building just off Mitsudera-dori, open since 2016 and run by the owner alone, who wraps, fries and pours while the Tigers play on the radio. Each order is ten bite-size gyoza for ¥550 (September 2026): thin, crisp-bottomed wrappers with a little chew around a punchy pork filling heavy on pepper and garlic. Eat them with just vinegar, or vinegar and soy. Two servings per person is the suggestion, and some order four or five between two. Octopus kimchi and cucumbers fill the wait, which can be long: an hour to get in at 7 pm, and about 30 minutes for gyoza at busy times. It's great with a Sapporo Lager. Cash only; closed Mondays and when sold out.

places.notes: [Udon · a late-night udon bar with free karaoke, 8 pm to 5 am] A dim, bar-like udon spot on the third floor of a Shinsaibashi building, open from 8 pm to 5 am for the end of a night out. The popular mentaiko cream udon is a recipe handed down from a former Italian-restaurant chef. The base is a Kansai-style dashi of kombu and sea bream with chewy Sanuki udon. The most popular bowl is the creamy mentaiko cream udon (¥1,380, April 2026); a chilled pork shabu-shabu udon (¥1,180) is lighter, and one repeat visitor raves about the ume udon with wakame and that dashi. A newer herbal hot-pot course piles leafy greens into a gentle Chinese-style broth, then chicken, pork and beef with an egg dip, and udon to finish. There are kara-age and drinking snacks, free karaoke and TV for sports. Smoking is allowed throughout. ¥300 charge; cash only; closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Sushi · a seven-seat creative sushi counter in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi alley] A chic, black-toned seven-seat counter in a back alley of Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since June 2025 and run by a young chef who handles everything alone; the name takes a character from the chef's own. The seasonal omakase (¥12,500, September 2026) mixes aged fish with playful creative dishes. Expect tuna aged 13 days, aged sea bream, four-day striped horse mackerel and dry-aged chutoro from the Oki Islands, alongside a rare-fried pike conger or a rare-fried eel sandwich and French-inspired sides that impressed diners. The rice is on the firm side. Drinks are reasonably priced, from ¥400. Book ahead, arrive on time since everyone starts together, and mention allergies when you reserve. Families are welcome.

places.notes: [Ramen · Akutagawa-line iekei near Shinsaibashi] A 20-seat counter two minutes from Shinsaibashi, open since 2023 and serving iekei ramen from the Akutagawa line of the Musashiya family. The Yoshikawa ramen is a rich pork-bone shoyu with chicken-fat aroma, deeper than it is heavy, over medium-thick noodles with smoked chashu; set firmness, richness and oil when you hand over the ticket. The Gyoton!! balances seafood umami with pork sweetness. Rice is ¥100 with free refills, so pour broth over it and add the table's doubanjiang and garlic. Reviewers call it a solid, classic bowl rather than a standout, and one found it a bit salty. Office workers line up at lunch. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Direct lineage of Menya Akutagawa, in the Shin-Nakano Musashiya family tree (Tabelog name; October 2026 review); official site menya-yoshikawa.com.

anecdotes.text: "The rich flavor of the pork bone broth combined with a deep soy sauce base is quite satisfying, yet it remains relatively mild and easy to drink. The aroma of chicken fat enhances the experience." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · morning wonton noodles in Kitahorie] An 11-seat counter in Kitahorie, three minutes from Yotsubashi, open since October 2023 from 8 am until the soup runs out, so noon visitors sometimes find it closed. The owner is from Busan, South Korea. The owner trained at Yakumo, Tokyo's famous wonton-noodle shop, and the name means "cloud" in Korean as a nod to it. Choose black, a clear 100% jidori chicken broth with dark soy, or white, a shio with a light yuzu lift. The draw is the wontons: springy shrimp ones and juicy pork ones in big, slippery wrappers; the pork and shrimp wonton noodles are ¥1,200 (September–October 2026). Medium-thin noodles and thin, wide chashu complete it. One reviewer found the table pepper unnecessary. Expect a short line most mornings. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Owner trained at the Tokyo wonton-noodle shop Yakumo; "KURUMU" means cloud in Korean, inspired by Yakumo (October 2026 review). The owner is from Busan, South Korea (October 2026 review).

places.notes: [Ramen · late-night tonkotsu with a marked order sheet, near Nippombashi] An 11-seat tonkotsu counter two minutes from Nippombashi exit 7, open since 2013 and now serving until 1 am. Despite the name ("concentration 8") and the looks, the pork-bone broth is creamy but lighter and easier than you'd expect; one diner braved the limited "concentration 27" and found it only a little richer. After buying a ticket you mark a sheet for noodle firmness, green onion, back fat, garlic and spicy miso. Thin straight noodles are the default, with a thicker wavy option on another bowl. The all-toppings ramen adds chashu and a good seasoned egg, and you can finish with rice in the broth. A regular calls it reliably solid. Cash only.

places.notes: [Tsukemen · seafood-tonkotsu tsukemen by Nagahoribashi] A 12-seat counter two minutes from Nagahoribashi, a branch (since 2011) of a group known for seafood tonkotsu, with its head office in Higashiyodogawa. The broth simmers pork bones and vegetables until they dissolve, then adds seafood and kombu, for a dark, thick, additive-free dip with a gentle flavor. Tsukemen is ¥1,050, or ¥1,150 with a seasoned egg (June 2026), and one repeat visitor loves the chashu and noodles in the large chashu tsukemen. The onsen-tamago special ramen has a niboshi-forward fish tonkotsu, easy to drink, on medium-thin firm noodles. Limited bowls rotate: rich niboshi or spicy tsukemen, a standout chilled curry ramen, a mackerel ramen. One diner wanted the dip hotter and the noodles chewier. The listed hours aren't always kept, so check first. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · dashi-first shio ramen in Namba Parks] A ramen shop on the sixth floor of Namba Parks, in front of Parks Cinema, open since 2021 and usually easy to get into, though one October lunch had a long line. The name says it: "dashi is life" shio ramen. A balanced shio with a well-seasoned egg was ¥1,250 (October 2026), and a former regular of an earlier Gyogyogyo near Namba Shrine was happy to find its seafood shio again here. There's also a niboshi black ramen, a frothy, spicy rich tonkotsu (¥1,000) and kara-age sets. Thin noodles are the norm. One diner saw a Michelin Bib Gourmand mention in the shop. Order on the table tablet; reviewers found prices a bit high and service slow at times.

chef_bio.background: A reviewer remembers an earlier Gyogyogyo near Namba Shrine in Honmachi (August 2026); one diner noticed a Michelin Bib Gourmand listing displayed (August 2026).

places.notes: [Champon · white and red champon near Namba Parks] A classic neighborhood Chinese shop near Namba Parks, three minutes from Nankai Namba, serving champon since 2008, with regulars who have come for years. There are two bowls, ¥900 each (September 2026). The white champon is a rich yet smooth pork-bone broth with finely chopped toppings; the red is a chicken-bone broth with Sichuan doubanjiang, mildly spicy. Both use chewy medium-thick champon noodles. For ¥50 more it becomes a set with rice, which you can drop into the leftover soup like porridge; a set with fried rice is ¥1,200. Follow the table guide and add vinegar and chili oil partway. There's sara udon too. Cash only; smoking allowed. Closed Saturdays and holidays.

places.notes: [Ramen · iekei with a Jiro-style option by Nagahoribashi] An iekei ramen shop 20 m from Nagahoribashi Station, open since 2020 and busy in the evenings. places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone broth, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Tabelog lists Mon–Fri 11:00–24:00, Sat 10:30–1:00, Sun and holidays 10:30–24:00, but the same listing says the shop is currently on reduced hours of 11:00–21:00; open year-round. places.neighborhood: Nambanaka 2-4-3, Naniwa — near Nippombashi, about 5 min from Namba Stn
places.cuisine: Yokohama iekei chain · Konshinya ramen ¥1,000 in shoyu, shio, miso or black-pepper miso · thick curly noodles · firmness, richness and fat to order, or "light and less" · free white rice with refills · fried-rice set ¥1,200 · finish the soup for a "makuri" ticket of free toppings for a month · 15 counter seats and 2 tables
places.notes: [Ramen · Konshinya iekei with free rice, near Nippombashi] A branch of the Konshinya Yokohama-iekei chain between Namba and Nippombashi, open since 2012. The Konshinya ramen (¥1,000, August–September 2026) comes in shoyu, shio, miso or black-pepper miso; the miso is surprisingly creamy, and thick curly noodles are chewy. Set firmness, richness and fat, or go "light and less". White rice is free with refills all day, and the salty broth makes the case for it; the fried-rice set (¥1,200) is an alternative. Finish every drop of soup and you earn a "makuri" ticket for a month of free toppings. Expect a short line at peak times. The listing says it's currently on reduced hours, 11:00–21:00. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Konshinya Yokohama-iekei chain, with shops beyond Osaka such as near Zeze Station, Shiga (September 2026 review); official site konshinya.com.

anecdotes.text: "When ordering, you can choose from soy sauce, salt, miso, or black pepper miso for the broth… Once I placed my ramen order, I found out that white rice is free and refillable." — September 2026, Konshinya ramen ¥1,000.
"The broth was incredibly creamy despite being miso-based. The thick, curly noodles were chewy and satisfying!" — August 2026.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: tare and soy-marinated dishes; chawanmushi and kamameshi broths not described.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken throughout.
places.hours_raw: Daily 18:00–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); closed irregularly, posted on Instagram (Tabelog). Reservations essential and hard to get (August–October 2026). Service charge ¥500 (Tabelog). 1F yakitori counter; 2F hot-pot courses and private bookings (August–October 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted.
places.neighborhood: Namba 1-3-13 — 1 min from Namba Walk exit B16
places.cuisine: Yakitori courses of 5, 7 or 9 skewers · 9 skewers with chawanmushi ¥3,500 (August 2026) · seseri, kokoro, zuri, tebasaki, sasami, negima, chochin, cartilage, the rare "sori" cut · jidori sashimi, fresh liver sashimi and tataki · soy-marinated kumquat (unlaid yolk) and cream cheese · liver kamameshi · Toyo Bijin junmai daiginjo and other sake · beer from a swing tap · 6-seat L-shaped counter and tables, 14 seats
places.notes: [Yakitori · a hard-to-book yakitori counter by Namba Walk] A 14-seat yakitori spot a minute from Namba Walk exit B16, open since 2024, with a six-seat L-shaped counter around the grill downstairs and hot-pot courses upstairs. The young owner is attentive, and the sake list is good. Book ahead; it fills up. Courses run 5, 7 or 9 skewers, and nine skewers with chawanmushi was just ¥3,500 in August 2026, big skewers, perfectly seasoned. Favorites include seseri, chochin, negima, cartilage and the rare "sori" cut. Start with the very fresh liver sashimi or tataki, and don't skip the soy-marinated kumquat. The liver kamameshi, cooked to finish, is a highlight. The sake list is strong (a limited Toyo Bijin junmai daiginjo stood out), and draft beer comes from a swing tap. One October diner noticed fewer items than in August for the same price. The owner accommodated one guest's special requests. ¥500 service charge.

chef_bio.background: Yakitori counter with a second-floor hot-pot room (August–October 2026 reviews). The young owner is attentive, and the sake list is good (September 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fresh chicken and careful seasoning (August 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "I reserved the course with 9 skewers of yakitori and chawanmushi for JPY 3,500. The grilling and seasoning were perfect, and every skewer was incredibly delicious." — August 2026.
"The broth was refined, and the rice was perfectly cooked, standing out beautifully. I was truly impressed by how delicious kamameshi can be." — September 2026, kamameshi to finish.

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: Ise lobster, black wagyu, abalone.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:30 (L.O. 14:30) and 17:00–22:00 (L.O. 20:30); closing days may vary (Tabelog). Reservations recommended (limited seats). Entrance shared with Chunagon; tell the reception you want teppanyaki (Tabelog). Service charge 10% (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money.
places.neighborhood: Namba 1-4-4, Sennichimae Mirakukan B1F — by Namba Walk exit 16, on Sennichimae-dori
places.cuisine: Teppanyaki from the Ise-lobster house Chunagon · courses with live Ise lobster as sashimi, soup and teppan-grilled, plus black-wagyu fillet with three sauces and garlic chips · Hikari course · Ran lunch course about ¥10,000 · ¥8,800 course with lobster or meat · Ise-lobster ramen with Kujo green onion or garlic rice to finish · yuzu sorbet and dessert, anniversary plate by reservation · 20 counter seats
places.notes: [Teppanyaki · Chunagon's Ise-lobster and wagyu teppanyaki counter] A 20-seat teppanyaki counter in the basement of Sennichimae Mirakukan, run by Chunagon, the Ise-lobster specialist; you enter through Chunagon and tell reception you're here for teppanyaki. Courses center on live Ise lobster, served as sashimi with sashimi and sake soy, as a rich soup and grilled on the teppan with a special sauce, then black-wagyu fillet with three sauces and garlic chips. Finish with garlic rice or an Ise-lobster ramen with Kujo green onion. The Ran lunch course came to about ¥10,000 (May 2026), an ¥8,800 course offers lobster or meat as the main, and the Hikari course does both. Staff are chatty and good with celebrations, with an anniversary plate by reservation, and the kitchen swapped the soup for a guest's shrimp allergy. 10% service charge.

chef_bio.background: Teppanyaki produced by Chunagon, the Ise-lobster restaurant (Tabelog); official page chunagon.com/hikari.
chef_bio.philosophy: Live Ise lobster, black abalone and wagyu (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I enjoyed the 'Hikari Course' featuring a full course of Ise lobster and beef fillet… To finish, I had garlic rice and ramen topped with Kujo green onions, packed with plenty of Ise lobster." — October 2026.
"The anniversary plate was beautifully decorated with chocolate, almost too pretty to eat!" — May 2026, a celebration where the soup was switched to pumpkin for a shrimp allergy.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat tempura batter; tentsuyu.

places.cuisine: Casual tempura izakaya · tempura from ¥275 a piece, fried to order · head-on shrimp, sweetfish, conger eel, pumpkin, maitake, shiitake · tempura-egg rice to finish · sashimi platter as otoshi (¥550) · yam with ume · wide range of local sake, wine · 8 counter seats and a table for six
places.notes: [Tempura · casual counter tempura with local sake near Shinsaibashi] A narrow tempura izakaya on the ground floor of a Shinsaibashi-suji building, open since 2020, with eight counter seats and a table at the back. The owner, who cooks the menu, has 30 years in the trade. It's tempura without the stiffness: pieces from ¥275, fried to order and sent out at a steady pace, light and not greasy, so diners feel fine the next day. The head-on shrimp is the star, crisp head and juicy body, and sweetfish, conger eel and maitake are favorites; finish with a tempura-egg rice bowl. Meals start with a ¥550 sashimi-platter otoshi, and the local sake list is long. The owner is friendly and the service attentive. Expect ¥5,000–8,000 with drinks. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Tempura izakaya with local sake (Tabelog). The owner, who cooks the menu, has 30 years in the trade (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients served simply and hot (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I had always thought that tempura was a bit intimidating, but the owner was very approachable… I also noticed that I had no stomach discomfort the next day." — March 2026.
"The conger eel was crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, generous in portion, and incredibly tasty. All the tempura was not greasy at all." — August 2026.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: hamburg steak usually uses breadcrumbs; demi-glace, teriyaki and onion sauces; fried shrimp.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: black-wagyu hamburg steak and steaks.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–23:00 (L.O. food 22:30, drinks 22:45) (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; walk-ins usually fine (June–July 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Black-wagyu hamburg steak and steak on a sizzling plate · Western Mama hamburg 200 g ¥1,100 · hamburg with fried shrimp 200 g ¥1,650 · "Wrestler" 500 g ¥2,700 · five sauces: demi-glace, ponzu, onion, teriyaki, salt · strip-loin steak from 100 g, pre-cut for chopsticks · Mega Combo 450 g (hamburg, chicken, pork, skirt) · small rice ¥150, set A with rice and mini salad · red wine · paper bibs · 14 seats
places.notes: [Steak · black-wagyu hamburg steak on a sizzling plate in Sennichimae] The original Cowboy, a 14-seat Western-style steak and hamburg shop just off an alley in Sennichimae, with wooden decor and counter seats easy for solo diners. The hamburg steak is pure black wagyu, no pork mixed in, served sizzling on a teppan so the sauce spits (a paper bib is provided), fluffy and juicy when you cut in. Pick from five sauces: demi-glace, ponzu, onion, teriyaki or salt. The Western Mama 200 g is ¥1,100 and the 500 g "Wrestler" ¥2,700 (2025–2026). Steaks start at 100 g and come pre-cut for chopsticks, and the Mega Combo piles 450 g of hamburg, chicken, pork and skirt. Add rice and salad for a set, or red wine. Open daily until 11 pm.

chef_bio.background: Cowboy steak and hamburg shops; official site steakcowboy.jp (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Black wagyu only for the hamburg (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "No mixed meats or pork—just pure Black Wagyu! Served sizzling hot on a teppan… There are 5 types of hamburger sauces to choose from: Demiglace, Ponzu, Onion, Teriyaki, and Salt Sauce." — September 2026, Wrestler 500 g ¥2,700.
"It comes sizzling hot on a teppan, so the sauce splatters everywhere!!" — November 2025, Western Mama hamburg 200 g ¥1,100; a paper bib is provided.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; shoyu tare.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: back fat, chicken and pork chashu, diced meat.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–21:30; hours may change (Tabelog). Weekday lunch service adds rice or ice cream (September 2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Abura-soba specialist · shoyu abura-soba with medium-thick curly noodles, back fat, cabbage and bean sprouts · chicken-and-pork (aburi) abura-soba, special large available · limited spicy bowls: "Shakunetsu no Rei" and the hotter "Yogan" cold tantan abura-soba with diced meat · ajitama · garlic, mayonnaise, chili oil and vinegar to finish · a small ginger soup first · rice with raw egg · weekday lunch rice or ice cream · 8 counter seats and a table for four
places.notes: [Abura-soba · back-fat abura-soba on the Otaroad side of Nippombashi] A 12-seat abura-soba specialist toward Otaroad, open since 2018, small inside but with repeat visitors. Mix the bowl from the bottom: medium-thick curly noodles in a shoyu sauce with back fat, crunchy cabbage and bean sprouts, and chashu that isn't greasy. A couple of newcomers expected heavy and found it surprisingly light. Then work through garlic, mayonnaise, chili oil and vinegar. The chicken-and-pork version adds seared meat, and spicy limited bowls run from "Shakunetsu no Rei" to the hotter "Yogan" cold tantan with diced meat, which left one diner's mouth sore. A small ginger soup comes first, and weekday lunch adds rice or ice cream. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Kasugatei abura-soba shops; official site kasugatei.com (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The chashu is not greasy but has just the right amount of fat, and the cabbage and bean sprouts are crunchy. Above all, the medium-thick curly noodles pair perfectly with the back fat." — September 2026, special large chicken-and-pork abura-soba.
"At first, I was a bit wary, thinking it might be too greasy based on the photos. But it was surprisingly light!" — October 2026.

places.notes: [Tantanmen · tantanmen and mapo rice sets by Nagahoribashi] A branch of the Chinmaya tantanmen-and-mapo chain a minute from Nagahoribashi Station, open until midnight and busy with office workers at lunch. The cooking is by a Chinese chef. The tantanmen is creamy with sesame and milder than its level suggests; one regular finds it a touch sweet alone and pairs it with the numbing mapo rice bowl in a half set. Sets add half fried rice, mapo rice or Tianjin rice, and half sizes keep it manageable. There's a mapo ramen too, and in summer a chilled tantanmen over ice with watercress, cucumber and meat miso. Some found the thin noodles clumped and the fried rice light; the spicy tantanmen (¥1,200, September 2026) gets its heat from chili oil. A long menu of sides like gyoza and water spinach makes it a drinking stop too.

places.notes: [Tsukemen · Mita Seimenjo inside Namba CITY] A 44-seat branch of the Mita Seimenjo tsukemen chain on the first floor of Namba CITY's South Building, a separate shop from the chain's Sennichimae branch. It's rarely crowded. Order by QR code; noodles are boiled fresh, so allow 10 minutes or more. The big perk: anything from 200 g to 500 g of noodles costs the same. Wheaty, medium-thick noodles go with a reliable rich tsukemen, a spicy version, or a light chilled sea-bream shio tsukemen with yuzu peel; you can choose hot or cold noodles. On the 3rd of each month a coupon makes all toppings free. The kara-age is better than you'd expect. One diner found the toppings ice-cold with cold noodles, and another the chashu a little tough.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kinmugi's chicken paitan by Nankai Namba] The second shop of Kinmugi, after the Amerikamura original, opened in September 2025 on a back street two minutes from Nankai Namba's west exit, with a clean, elegant interior and good service. The chicken paitan ramen (¥1,000, August–October 2026) is creamy and frothy, sweet and gentle rather than heavy, with chicken and pork chashu and a well-cooked soft-boiled egg. The tsukemen (¥1,100, large +¥150) pairs a light, foamy paitan dip with chilled thick curly noodles. Add a ¥300 yodare-chicken rice bowl. Summer brought a chilled corn-potage noodle with sweet potato, broccoli and chicken. There's sometimes a short line. Buy at the touch-panel machine; cards and PayPay accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · a Tabelog 100 dashi and tsukemen shop under Yotsubashi Station] An 18-seat basement shop directly above Yotsubashi Station, formerly known as Jikon, open since 2015 and named to Tabelog's ramen 100 from 2023 to 2025. Expect a short line at the 11 am opening; it's mostly a lunch shop and closes when the soup runs out. The regular favorite is the Kamatsu tsukemen, noodles soaked in kombu water seasoned well enough to eat on their own; upgrade to the smooth Mochihime noodles for ¥100. The shellfish-broth ramen is gentle and comforting, with a perfectly seasoned egg. Seasonal limited bowls are the draw: in October 2026 a creamy Tanohata duck paitan shio (¥1,300), and a chilled ramen of double Rausu kombu with mushroom oil that one diner rated above any kombu tsukemen. Finish with a dashi rice ball. Cash only; open Thursday and Friday evenings only.

chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal limited bowls built on rich broths (October 2026 review).

places.notes: [Ramen · an 8-seat Tabelog 100 chicken ramen counter in Kozu] A tiny eight-seat shop in Kozu, six to eight minutes from Nippombashi exit 7, its walls covered in signatures, named to Tabelog's ramen 100 six times and loved by regulars with hundreds of visits. A friendly owner and one female staff member run the room. The signature is the chicken-bonito extreme shio (¥1,000, October 2026): a deep, chicken-packed salt broth brightened with plenty of yuzu, two kinds of chashu and a soft-boiled egg on Teigaku noodles. The shoyu version is just as refined, and the chicken doro tsukemen (¥1,300) brings a bubbling-hot, thick chicken-soy dip for glossy flat noodles. Limited bowls appear on social media, like a salt chicken paitan or the hearty Youji ramen. Add a rare-chashu rice bowl (¥350) or the stone-grilled cheese omurice. Buy a ticket outside and wait for your number. Cash only.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 9 May 2013; reopened under the current name 28 January 2014 (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Tabelog Ramen WEST 100 2018–2020 and OSAKA 100 2023–2025 (Tabelog); run by two staff (October 2026 review). A friendly owner and one female staff member run the room (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Chicken-bonito shio ramen; chicken doro tsukemen.

places.notes: [Ramen · thick-noodle chuka soba and monthly specials near Shinsaibashi] A daytime-only chuka soba shop in Minamisenba near Shinsaibashi, open since 2019 and busy at lunch with solo diners and a quick-moving line. The core is a soy-heavy chuka soba on thick, wheaty curly noodles: one diner called the regular the best shoyu ramen ever, strong yet gentle and not greasy, and there's an extra-rich back-fat version and mazesoba. The fun is the monthly special: October 2026's ankake spicy-numbing shoyu (¥1,350) is thick like mapo with an egg yolk and garlic chives, though several found it milder than its name; September brought a miso-butter corn bowl under back fat. Don't skip the rich fried rice (+¥280), and small rice is free at lunch until 2 pm. Cash only; closes by 5 pm.

chef_bio.philosophy: A monthly limited bowl alongside the regulars (September–October 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "Honestly, I think it's the best soy sauce-based ramen I've ever had. It has a gentle flavor while still delivering a strong soy sauce taste. The fat isn't greasy at all." — October 2026, regular chuka soba.

"The first bite surprised me with a slightly sweet flavor in the sauce, but as I continued eating, the spiciness and umami gradually intensified… The thick, curly noodles held up well under the weight of the sauce." — October 2026, limited ankake ramen.

places.cuisine: A broad ramen menu · jet-black shoyu ramen with garlic umami · shellfish-forward chuka soba · clam-broth ramen · oyster shoyu ramen · creamy chicken paitan · special tsukemen with a rich seafood dip, thick noodles and rare chashu · chashu and chicken-tataki rice bowls · seafood rice bowls · English menu · 17 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · a many-bowled ramen shop off Midosuji near Shinsaibashi] A 17-seat ramen shop a couple of minutes north of Shinsaibashi Station, open since 2012 and reopened in 2020, with an English menu and plenty of overseas guests. The range is wide: a jet-black shoyu that isn't too salty, with soy richness and garlic umami; a shellfish-forward chuka soba; clam and oyster ramen; and a creamy chicken paitan that one diner rated highly. The standout for one tsukemen skeptic was the special tsukemen, a rich seafood dip with chewy thick noodles and plenty of moist rare chashu, which jumped to the top of a personal ranking. Rice bowls run from chashu to chicken tataki and seafood. Reviews are mixed on value, with one large clam ramen and mini bowl at ¥1,710, and one diner found the soup lukewarm. Cash only; closes when sold out.

places.notes: [Yoshoku · a 74-year-old Western-food diner near Amerikamura] A long-running yoshoku restaurant in Nishi-Shinsaibashi near Amerikamura, about 74 years in business and still busy with local regulars; the name is read "Nanpu". Downstairs is a counter that suits solo diners, upstairs tables. Weekday lunches are the bargain: around ¥1,000–1,100 for a plate like the Familiar Lunch of bite-size cutlet, shrimp fry and omelet, with rice and a mini bowl of somen. À la carte, the pork cutlet (¥1,600) is fried hot for a light, crunchy coat, the hamburg (¥1,600) comes juicy with spaghetti, a fried egg and bacon, and the big crab cream croquettes are creamy inside. The demi-glace tastes properly old-school. Cash only; Sundays lunch only.

places.notes: [Sweets · a strawberry sweets shop with a café upstairs] A strawberry-only sweets shop on Shinsaibashi-suji from Tsukiji Soratsuki, a Tokyo sweets maker, using strawberries its buyers source from around Japan all year. The ground-floor case is a pink wall of shortcakes, tarts, éclairs and daifuku, with crepes and soft serve to go. Upstairs, the 20-seat café, with dried flowers and strawberry-shaped lamps, serves cake plates with ice cream and a free drink (¥2,000, March 2026). Favorites are the strawberry tart in a jar (¥800, August 2026), layered with almond cream, crumble and custard; the red strawberry éclair with chocolate mousse; and a shortcake twice the usual size for ¥650. Most sweets are made by in-house pastry chefs. The café opens at noon, takeaway at 11. Cash or PayPay only.

The draw is raw oysters from different regions, best as a tasting of five; in summer the rock oysters from Murotsu in Hyogo and Naruto in Tokushima were called rich, "the milk of the sea". Cooked, there are steamed and fried oysters (hot and much praised), gratin, ajillo, a spicy oyster jjigae and oyster pasta. Order the oyster clay-pot rice first, as it takes about 30 minutes. Prices are fair for the amount of oysters, with wines to match. One repeat visitor found a batch of raw oysters a bit fishy. Open until 1 am.

places.notes: [Japanese · an 11-seat small-plates counter tucked in a Nishi-Shinsaibashi alley] An easy-to-miss 11-seat counter down a narrow alley off Midosuji, open since 2015, which describes itself as more than an izakaya but less than kaiseki. places.notes: [Ramen · a seven-seat chicken-and-seafood shoyu counter near JR Namba] A small seven-seat counter three minutes from JR Namba's south exit, open since 2011, with regulars who come for the limited bowls. Two ramen anchor the menu. The Kanade shoyu (¥1,050, September 2026) balances sweet chicken umami with a tightening seafood finish over thin noodles, and two chashu, moist pork and chicken. The most popular Chicken Kanade ramen (¥1,000) layers chicken paitan, seafood and shoyu into a thick but drinkable broth that one diner found a touch sweet. Add garlic to punch it up, or a seared-chashu rice bowl (¥450). There's mazesoba too. One diner found the seafood fishy. Waits are short; buy a ticket at the machine. Closed Sundays, and Tuesday and Saturday are lunch only.

places.notes: [Ramen · a shio-ramen specialist south of Nankai Namba] A shio-ramen specialist two minutes from Nankai Namba, open since 2019, in a clean room of white wood and stainless steel. The clear broth of chicken and seafood is accented with chicken katsuobushi: light, but full of umami, and good enough that one diner drank every drop. A hint of black pepper gives it punch. Teigaku noodles, chewy, flat and wavy (one reviewer likened them to Kitakata), soak it up, with chashu, ajitama, green onion and kaiware. The fluffy fried rice, whole or half, is a classic partner. In summer there was a chilled ramen with lemon vinegar to finish. It's rarely crowded late in the afternoon. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · a lunch-only niboshi shop in Kozu, opened 2025] A lunch-only ramen counter in Kozu, opened in April 2025 and run by the owner with one helper, already drawing regulars who have been more than twenty times. A cheerful owner and one female staff member run the seven-seat counter. The heart of it is niboshi: a clear sardine shoyu (¥950) with a whole niboshi on top, or the shio niboshi clear soup (¥950), sardine-forward on the first sip, then clean, with a little ume, though one fan found the niboshi subdued. There's also a special, shoyu, shio and an old-style bowl, all on chewy medium-thin noodles. Limited bowls keep coming: back-fat shoyu mazesoba until the end of November, and in summer chilled chuka soba and chilled niboshi. Pair it with tamago kake gohan (¥300) or a seared-chashu bowl (¥350). Pay after eating, in cash. Closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style ramen on the Otaroad side of Nippombashi] A small Jiro-style counter toward Otaroad, open since 2017 and part of the same group as Fukuchan Ramen and Tenchijin. The Juku-cho ramen has a punchy broth and noodles fans like; customize with free extra vegetables, chashu fat and garlic, or swap garlic for ginger if you're working tomorrow. The garlic is fierce, so go easy. The soupless miso Juku-cho (¥1,060) and the dry ramen with grated cheese are hits, and the spicy Juku-cho is ¥1,100 (August 2026). The house kombu salt for the bean sprouts gets special praise, and the chashu is thick. A smaller noodle portion with extra vegetables suits lighter eaters. One person runs everything, so expect a wait at weekends and brisk seating directions. Cash only.

places.cuisine: Creamy chicken soba · Tori Soba shoyu ¥1,000 and shio · spicy Tori Soba ¥1,100 · potage-like chicken broth · fried burdock root · moist chicken and chewy pork chashu · thin curly noodles · summer chilled jidori soba with flat noodles · limited Jiro-style bowl · rice · 15 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · a Ramen 100 chicken-soba shop north of Shinsaibashi] A Tori Soba Zagin branch open since 2015, picked for Tabelog's Ramen 100 every year from 2019 to 2024, with a quietly upscale feel for a ramen shop. The tori soba is a creamy chicken broth that one diner likened to a rich potage, intense yet smooth. Thin curly noodles, two chashu (moist chicken and chewy pork) and crunchy fried burdock root complete it. Choose shoyu (¥1,000) or shio, or the spicy version (¥1,100), which ran hotter than one fan of spice expected. Summer brought a chilled jidori soba with flat noodles and plenty of chicken chashu, and there has been a limited Jiro-style bowl. Expect a line: 20 to 40 minutes at peak times. Open 10:00 to 22:00 daily. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Tori Soba Zagin branch; operator site silver-grape.com (Tabelog). Tabelog Ramen WEST 100 2019–2022 and Ramen OSAKA 100 2023–2024.

anecdotes.text: "The creamy broth had a delightful texture, and the chicken stock tasted like a rich potage—intense yet smooth… The fried burdock root added a nice crunch." — October 2026, tori soba.

"Both the soup and the bowl were nicely chilled… The flat noodles were well-chilled in cold water, and rather than being chewy, they had a delightful, mochi-like texture." — October 2026, chilled jidori soba.

places.notes: [Ramen · Tokyo's Tsujita tsukemen on Senba Shinsaibashi street] The Shinsaibashi branch of Kanda's Tsujita, the Tokyo tsukemen chain, opened in October 2024 on the Senba Shinsaibashi shopping street. The rich tsukemen pairs noodles with a great texture with a thick dipping sauce of seafood and pork. Squeeze the sudachi over the noodles to freshen it and add black shichimi, then finish with soup to thin what's left. The rich flavored-egg tsukemen was ¥1,210 in September 2026. One diner called it a reliable classic rather than anything new. Lines were long after opening and mostly overseas visitors on one Sunday; now there are days with no wait. Buy a ticket at the machine. Open until midnight on weekdays.

anecdotes.text: "The dipping sauce was wonderfully rich, with a classic flavor that highlighted the umami of seafood… When I squeezed some sudachi (a type of citrus) into it, it added a refreshing touch." — September 2026, large rich tsukemen.

places.notes: [Ramen · Mugen's beef-bone white soup north of Shinsaibashi] The Shinsaibashi branch of Mugen Ramen, open since September 2024, five minutes from the station. The beef-bone white soup ramen (¥1,050, October 2026) is creamy and bubbly, with a rich, slightly sweet broth that drinks easier than it looks, and a rich option. Thin, firm noodles reminded one diner of Hakata ramen. Add a seasoned egg (¥130) or pair it with a small melt-in-your-mouth chashu rice bowl. One of the two chashu was a little gamey for one diner, and another got only one slice. The priciest bowl carries marbled strip loin like roast beef, and there's even a kiwi ramen. Toppings may differ from other branches. Lines can be long. No cards. See also Mugen Ramen Sennichimae.

chef_bio.background: Branch of Mugen Ramen; a diner who had tried other branches noted toppings vary by shop (October 2026).

anecdotes.text: "I started with the broth, which had a rich flavor with a strong essence of beef bone… Although it looked quite thick, it was surprisingly easy to drink." — September 2026, beef-bone white soup ramen, rich.
"I chose the most expensive ramen. I think it was marbled strip loin? It felt like roast beef, rich yet easy to eat." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · a late-night abura soba counter near Nagahoribashi] A 15-seat counter two minutes from Nagahoribashi, open since 2011 and serving until midnight, which makes it a stop after a night out. The draw is abura soba (mazesoba), with ramen and niboshi dishes too. The spicy oil noodles impressed one diner with heat balanced by umami and a sauce that clings to the noodles. The chashu has fans, best with a green onion chashu rice bowl. Water comes with lemon slices. The staff changed about a year before April 2026, and a long-time customer found the flavor milder since and the new staff attentive. Not everyone is won over: one September visitor found the oil soba mediocre. Buy a ticket at the machine. Closed Sundays and holidays. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Abura soba and ramen counter; official site menya-norio.com (Tabelog). Staff changed about a year before an April 2026 review.

anecdotes.text: "True to its name, it has a solid spicy kick, but it's not just heat; the balance with the umami is exquisite. The sauce clings well to the noodles." — June 2026, spicy oil noodles.
"I've been coming here for a long time, and although the staff changed about a year ago, the experience remains great… The new staff is very attentive." — April 2026.

places.notes: [Japanese · a seafood-and-seasonal izakaya off Shinsaibashi-suji] A 19-seat izakaya open since 2019, which calls itself a hideout for adults built on hot pot, seafood, seasonal vegetables and drink. One diner says the food comes first. Fresh assorted sashimi is the constant. The signature giant shrimp tempura is plump and crisp; one diner had shrimp tempura wrapped in sakura shrimp. Karasumi goes with drinks, and the karasumi soba finish eats almost like pasta. Others order grilled grouper in Saikyo miso, horse sashimi with tategami fat, a rich potato salad, oysters, and seasonal crab. A ¥6,000 Japanese course is an option. The appetizer rarely changes. Smoking is allowed, which one non-smoker minded. Reserve; it gets busy. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Seafood izakaya; "A hideout for adults...hot pot x Seafood x seasonal vegetables x alcohol" (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The signature giant shrimp tempura was impressive once again, with its plump meat and crispy batter that was simply irresistible." — December 2025, course meal.
"To finish off, the karasumi soba was a unique experience—almost like pasta, and it was delicious." — February 2026.

places.notes: [Japanese · an Aomori izakaya with live Tsugaru shamisen in Sennichimae] A rare Aomori izakaya in Osaka, open since 2011 on the third floor of a Sennichimae building, a little hard to find. Live Tsugaru shamisen plays twice a night, around 19:00 and 21:00, and one diner was captivated by its power. Start with the Horoyoi Set of sake, sashimi and appetizers, then move to northern dishes: Nebuta-zuke, koji-marinated herring and red salmon, Appa-yaki (scallops simmered in egg), komai, and iburigakko with cream cheese. The taro croquettes, tempura, chicken nanban and beef tendon round it out, with Aomori sake. The owner is bright and attentive, and the regulars make newcomers feel at home. Book early. Cash only.

places.notes: [Japanese · counter shabu-shabu and sukiyaki in Souemoncho until 4 am] A 16-seat counter in late-night Souemoncho where each diner gets a personal pot, so solo diners are at ease. Choose shabu-shabu or sukiyaki: kuroge wagyu and Kurobuta pork that melt in the mouth, with a homemade sesame sauce. The top beef can even be eaten raw with wasabi and soy over rice. One regular's after-drinks order is a rice bowl of seared rare beef with a sweet-spicy sauce. The menu has run to stew, hamburg steak and chicken sashimi too. Staff walk first-timers through it. It isn't cheap: reviewers spent ¥6,000–15,000 on hot pot. Open until 4 am most nights; closed Sundays. Smoking allowed.

places.notes: [Yakitori · a creative skewer counter on quiet Dotonbori 2-chome] A yakitori izakaya open since 2014 on the quieter stretch of Dotonbori west of Midosuji, three minutes from Namba. Chicken leads: hearts, seseri, tamahimo and chochin (one diner reserved just for it), plus charcoal-grilled thigh and cheek. The tsukune is grilled just right. Pork, beef and seafood skewers keep it varied; the meat-wrapped cherry tomatoes burn the unwary. There's chicken sashimi, salmon tartare and a filling katsu udon, and the daily specials are worth asking about. The master is fun to talk to from the counter, and there are semi-private rooms in back. One May evening the room was half overseas visitors. Otoshi ¥200. Smoking allowed.

places.notes: [Japanese · a kinki shabu-shabu specialist in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A seasonal seafood restaurant tucked at the back of the ground floor of a nightlife building, behind a cabaret-style entrance that can make a first visit feel like a wrong turn. Inside is a calm Japanese room with private rooms, used for business dinners and special occasions. The specialty is kinki shabu-shabu: the Hokkaido fish, rare in Osaka, has a refined fat that melts into the broth, and the course ends with a rich rice porridge. Sashimi and the simmered, grilled and fried courses also draw praise, as does a deep sake list. It's a splurge: reviewers spent ¥8,000–30,000. The shop has moved from its old building. Menu in English and Chinese. The newest review is from March 2026.

anecdotes.text: "The Kinki sourced from Kushiro has a refined fat that blends beautifully with the broth, making it exquisite. The finishing rice porridge has a rich umami that is different from fugu." — November 2025.

"The restaurant is located at the back of the first floor of a building that houses nightlife establishments, so you might initially wonder, 'Is this the right place?' But don't worry, it is!" — June 2025.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kurume and Hakata tonkotsu in Kozu] A 13-seat tonkotsu counter near Nipponbashi, open since 2010; the owner changed in August 2025 and lunch was added. The rich broth comes white, red or black. Hakuryu, the basic rich tonkotsu (¥900), is soy-seasoned, a little oily and properly salty over very thin, firm straight noodles. The White Dragon is a Kurume tonkotsu with a red chili paste in the center, the White Tiger is Hakata-style, and the Kuro Ryu is the garlic version; one diner had black garlic oil. Toppings are chashu (thin and fatty), crunchy kikurage and green onion; pickled ginger, spicy takana and sesame sit on the counter. Add rice (¥150 at lunch), extra noodles, or garlicky gyoza. Service is quick, and it's often quiet. Closed Wednesdays; Sunday is lunch only.

places.notes: [Ramen · an overnight tantanmen counter off Matsuyamachi-suji] An eight-seat tantanmen shop and izakaya that opens in the evening and runs into the next morning, so it feeds night-shift workers and late drinkers. The soup tantanmen comes white or black (¥1,000; ¥1,100 for the black in August 2026). The white is sesame-rich but surprisingly light; the black is thick and jet-black. Both numb with Sichuan pepper and homemade chili oil, over thin straight noodles topped with meat miso, dried shrimp, mizuna and takuan, which one diner likened to a laksa note. There's a brothless version on thick wavy noodles, spice up to level 5, extra noodles, and a garlicky kara-age. Water comes scented with orange peel. Hours shift, so check first.

places.notes: [Chinese · hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodles with free refills near Nagahoribashi] A spacious 79-seat Lanzhou beef-noodle shop open since 2024, where a noodle maker stretches and twists the dough after you order, a show in itself. The beef noodle soup (¥950) is a light, clear broth of beef bones and meat with beef, daikon, garlic shoots and cilantro. Pick the noodle width, from 1 mm threads to extra-wide flat ribbons like lasagna sheets, and refills are free and unlimited. Spice comes to order; add chili oil and the black vinegar the wall recommends. Lunch set B (¥1,000) adds three gyoza and a small vegetable dish. There are also shrimp dumplings in sour soup, a cumin beef burger and beef skewers. It's busy at lunch, and the room has an overseas feel.

chef_bio.background: Lanzhou beef noodle shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained); official site niuyizui-jp.com.

anecdotes.text: "Soon enough, I received noodles that were truly massive, resembling bandages, and I added them to the remaining broth… it was amusing, like eating lasagna sheets. Yet, it was delicious." — September 2026, free extra-wide noodle refill.
"Watching the noodle chef in the kitchen skillfully stretch and twist the dough was captivating." — September 2026.

places.notes: [Chinese · build-your-own mala tang in Namba Parks] A small, cramped mala-tang counter on the sixth floor of Namba Parks, around since before the mala-tang boom, and packed with young women on one visit. Mark your noodles, broth, ingredients, sides and spice level on a sheet at the table; it's slower than the usual line-and-grab, which suits first-timers, though the small print makes the total hard to add up. One regular builds a bowl of mulukhiyah, white fungus, king oyster mushroom, tomato and cilantro with thick sweet-potato noodles (seven items ran ¥1,500 in August 2026). The broth tastes strongly herbal, with an addictive numbing heat, and garlic, black vinegar and Sichuan pepper oil wait on the table. Portions can feel small; add a pork shabu-shabu rice bowl if hungry.

chef_bio.background: Mala tang shop in Namba Parks; "around long before the mala tang craze" (August 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "I can't resist the reliable mulukhiyah, white fungus, king oyster mushrooms, tomatoes, and cilantro. I always get the thick sweet potato noodles at level 2!! It was JPY 1500 for 7 items!" — August 2026.
"On the table, you'll find garlic, black vinegar, and Sichuan pepper oil, which allows for some great flavor customization!" — August 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · espuma chicken paitan in Minamisenba] A 16-seat chicken paitan shop open since 2019 as Mugi x Tori and renamed Kinmugi in September 2026, the name the group's other shops use. Domestic chicken is simmered for hours and foamed just before serving, and you can hear the frothing while you wait. The result is a creamy, bubbly broth over chewy medium-thick straight noodles from Kyoto's Menya Teigaku. The most popular special topping ramen (¥1,450) adds rare, tender pork-loin and chicken-breast chashu, egg and menma. Limited bowls rotate, such as an uni ramen with a delicate sea-urchin aroma, though one diner couldn't find the uni in the tsukemen. Summer brings chilled corn soup noodles (¥1,400); add rice to finish as risotto. There can be a line at noon. Cash-only ticket machine.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 17 June 2019 (Tabelog) as Mugi x Tori; renamed Kinmugi in September 2026 (September 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Espuma chicken paitan shop; official site mugi-tori.com (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "Made from carefully selected domestic chicken, it is simmered for a long time and foamed just before serving, resulting in a very creamy texture." — September 2026, special topping ramen.

places.notes: [Ramen · rich chicken paitan near Nagahoribashi] A 12-seat chicken paitan shop near Nagahoribashi, open since 2020, with lines even after lunch and a ten-minute wait at Saturday noon. Buy a ticket at the cash-only machine outside, then wait to be seated. The chicken paitan is rich, bold and piping hot, clinging to the noodles, and two diners drank nearly every drop. The special ramen with extra-fat rice came to ¥1,800. The mazesoba is the other draw: homemade flat medium-thick noodles tossed with the sauce and an egg, with coarse black pepper, and free rice to finish. Tabelog lists kara-age too. A sister shop runs elsewhere.

chef_bio.background: Chicken paitan and mazesoba shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained); a sister shop is open (Tabelog).

places.notes: [Ramen · late-night Iekei with free noodles and rice near Matsuyamachi] A 17-seat Iekei shop near Matsuyamachi, open since 2016, serving lunch and again from 21:00 to 3:00 am. The tonkotsu shoyu is creamy with a punch that still lets the pork through, topped with nori, spinach and quail egg; shio is an option. Medium noodles are the house choice. Large noodles, rice and extra noodles come free, as do kimchi and pickles, so a full meal ran in the ¥900s. One diner found it closer to Hakata tonkotsu. Ordering extra-rich made it far too salty for a newcomer. Sides include a negi chashu bowl, mini kara-age bowl and gyoza. The owner has been seen running it alone and comes across as friendly. Hours can slip, so check first.
