anecdotes.text: "The rich soy sauce dressing paired perfectly with the hearty flat thick noodles… You can choose between 150g and 200g of noodles, and customize the amount of vegetables, fat, and garlic from less to extra." — March 2025, MAZE soba.
"The chicken paitan ramen costs JPY 1000, and the chashu (braised pork) is tender and delicious." — October 2026, ninth visit.

places.notes: [Ramen · Agu pork and Tanba black chicken shoyu and shio, with inventive limited bowls, by Kujo] A nine-seat counter near Kujo, open since 2019 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen 100 in 2024 and 2025, with lines at the 11:00 opening. A husband-and-wife team runs it; the owner trained at ramen shops before opening. The base is an additive-free double soup of Agu pork and Tanba black chicken with a layered fish dashi; the ajitama shoyu (¥1,250) floats Agu back fat over flat noodles from Tsurumi Seimen, with juicy Agu belly chashu. The shio is clear and mellow, its umami building as you go. For the simplest taste of broth and noodle, there's a kake-style shio or shoyu soba with only onion. Repeat diners come for the limited bowls: a stir-fried chicken-shoulder noodle tossed in a cast-iron pan, an Onomichi-style back-fat shoyu, chilled ramen in summer. Add the seasonal takikomi rice. Ticket machine, cash only; closed Mondays.

places.notes: [Ramen · rich miso on thick curly noodles near Kitahama] A fifteen-seat counter in the Kitahama office district, open since 2020 and run by the same people as the nearby Tsukemen Ide, with a lunch line that some diners call routine. The miso ramen (¥1,000) is rich and slightly gritty, with a pork-bone base beneath, on thick, chewy curly noodles of whole wheat, brightened by chopped purple onion and white negi with yuzu peel. Two variations stand out: the spicy miso, with five heat levels and the first three free, where the miso stays the star; and the "Wasan sansho" miso (¥1,100), whose aroma greets you at the door and gives a refreshing finish. Buy your ticket inside before you line up. Cards and PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Miso ramen shop; sister of Tsukemen Ide (2021 and September 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is quite rich in miso flavor. You can taste the pork bone flavor beneath the miso, but there's a slight graininess… The noodles are thick, curly, and made from whole wheat, strong enough to stand up to the broth." — October 2026, miso ramen ¥1,000.
"The broth had a rich miso flavor without being heavy, and the fragrance and mild spiciness of the sansho created a refreshing aftertaste." — March 2026, Wasan sansho miso ramen ¥1,100.

places.notes: [Ramen · thick pork-bone and seafood tsukemen in Kitahama since 2011] A busy fifteen-seat tsukemen shop in the Kitahama office district, open since 2011, where lunch means buying a ticket, a short wait outside and often a shared table. The tsukemen (¥1,100) pairs glossy, chewy thick noodles with a strong wheat flavor and a thick, rich dipping soup of pork bone and seafood, "rich without being overly heavy," with chashu and menma already in it; one October diner got 300 g for ¥1,100. Finish with soup-wari from the table. Add all the toppings (¥600) or a rice bowl of shredded pork or niku-miso. There's also a curry tsukemen. One diner found it simply average. Its sister shop, Miso Noodle Koji, is a few blocks west. Cards and PayPay accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · whipped chicken paitan by Taisho Station] A bright, clean seven-seat counter a block from Taisho Station, open since September 2024 and serving the chicken paitan that one diner hadn't found anywhere else in Taisho. The soup is whipped until frothy and creamy but not too heavy, on thin straight noodles, with two chashu: rare pork shoulder and a roasted or grilled pork belly. Choose shio, shoyu (the soy comes through strongly) or a spicy version; one diner found the extra noodles salty. Order rice (¥100) and you get takana and spicy mentaiko free, or go for the rare chashu bowl with egg yolk. In summer there are chilled bowls such as a sea bream and clam shio with tempura, which can sell out at lunch; one August evening there was a line of six. Closed Wednesdays; Tuesday is lunch only.

places.notes: [Ramen · bonito-kombu-pork shoyu with burdock, near Uehommachi] A seven-seat counter on Sennichimae-dori between Uehommachi and Tsuruhashi, open since 2016 with late hours after 19:00. The Tokimaru shoyu ramen (¥780) is a triple soup of bonito, kombu and pork bone with a gentle soy, on flat, medium-thick whole-wheat noodles, topped with cabbage, bean sprouts and the house signature: tender simmered burdock, which makes it taste distinctly Japanese. Add extra vegetables for a fuller bowl. The tsukemen (¥900 for 100 g) and a spicy tonkotsu shoyu draw mixed reviews, and one diner found the niboshi version too salty. In summer there's a sticky, spicy neba-neba chilled noodle with okra, yam and kimchi. Closes when the soup runs out.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; official site tokimaru.com).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles are flat, medium-thick, and made from whole wheat flour. The broth is a rich triple soup combining bonito, kombu kelp, and pork bones, seasoned with soy sauce… the standout ingredient is definitely the burdock root!" — October 2025, Tokimaru shoyu ramen ¥780.

"The rich pork bone broth was infused with seafood flavors, particularly strong notes of bonito… An unusual topping of burdock root was included, but it didn't leave a strong impression." — January 2026, tsukemen 100 g ¥900.

places.notes: [Ramen · shrimp-bushi chuka men and shrimp abura soba by Awaza, with morning ramen] A clean, calm eight-seat shop two minutes from Awaza, opened in April 2026 and described by one diner as the next brand from Ramen Kasumi, with morning ramen from 8:00 on Friday to Sunday. Start with the Moto-Aji chuka men, a light but rich, slightly sweet shoyu on curly whole-wheat noodles, or go straight to the Shin-Aji ebi-bushi chuka men (¥1,000): a salt broth of house-made shrimp, squid and chicken bushi that blooms when you stir in the red shrimp oil, over chewy flat twisted noodles. The ebi shio abura soba is the other favorite. Use the table's niboshi vinegar and spicy mala takuan to change it up midway. Cash-only ticket machine; you may get a coupon for next time.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop described by an October 2026 diner as "Kasumi's next brand" (Ramen Kasumi); Tabelog.
chef_bio.philosophy: Menu board: "a fragrant oil soup made with homemade shrimp bushi, squid, and chicken bushi… Seifuuken's neo-Chinese ramen" (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "When tasting the salt-based broth alone, it had a perfect saltiness and rich umami… Then I mixed in the red liquid that resembled shrimp oil… The flavor and aroma of shrimp spread throughout the broth." — September 2026, Shin-Aji ebi-bushi chuka men ¥1,000.

"The broth was light yet rich, offering a comforting and flavorful taste… The slightly sweet soy sauce flavor was well pronounced… The curly whole wheat noodles had a wonderful chewy and smooth texture." — September 2026, Moto-Aji chuka soba.

places.name: らーめん砦 大阪京町堀店 (Ramen Toride Osaka Kyomachibori)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: thin wheat noodles; tare.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: clam broth; chashu; clam rice bowl.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); public holidays 11:30–22:00 (L.O. 21:45); closing days vary (Tabelog). Cards, IC cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). LINE coupons.
places.neighborhood: Kyomachibori 1-10-10 — 5 min from Higobashi Stn exit 7
places.cuisine: Clam paitan ramen · Toride ramen: milky, creamy clam broth, thick yet clean, thin noodles, rare chashu, charred green onion, kaiware, shredded nori · Toride set ¥1,100 with "dunk rice" to finish risotto-style · clam rice bowl and seasoned-egg set · chilled clam ramen with thicker chashu · limited niboshi ramen with pork and chicken-breast chashu · 14 counter seats and a table for four
places.notes: [Ramen · creamy clam paitan with dunk rice near Higobashi] A calm counter in Kyomachibori, open all day since 2017, whose Toride ramen is a milky clam paitan that one diner likened to clam chowder: thick and rich but with a clean, oceanic finish, on thin noodles with rare chashu and charred green onion. The owner is a woman, which surprised a reviewer expecting a samurai type from the name. Get the Toride set (¥1,100) and tip the "dunk rice" into the last of the soup for a risotto-like finish, or pair the bowl with a clam rice bowl and a well-seasoned egg. A chilled version comes with thicker chashu, and a gentle limited niboshi ramen has appeared. Light enough that one diner found it went down easily even with no appetite. Open daily until 23:00; cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Clam paitan ramen shop, Kyomachibori branch (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). The owner is a woman, which surprised a reviewer expecting a samurai type from the name (April 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The Toride Ramen features a creamy and rich clam-based broth. It's thick yet has a refreshing aftertaste, perfectly complementing the thin noodles." — July 2026, Toride set.
"In a nutshell, it tastes like clam chowder, but it's impressive how it has been transformed into ramen… a delicious ramen that was light and easy to eat." — June 2025, clam paitan ramen.

places.notes: [Italian · one-person Italian bar with ¥890 iron-pan pasta lunches in Ura-Namba] A cozy, slightly chaotic Italian bar in the Ura-Namba backstreets behind the old Kabukiza, running since 1999 and cooked by one person. Weekday lunch is the find: ¥890–990 (2026) buys the day's pasta with a tangy mini salad and bread, or the Napolitan, served sizzling in an iron pan ringed with egg, in a large size one diner thought could feed three. The iron-pot doria hides a melting egg under ketchup rice and cheese, and the carbonara (¥890) pairs well with a ¥550 glass of white. Expect a wait: one diner waited about 20 minutes, and another saw a fellow diner carry plates to help. At night it's a wine bar with Italian plates (¥300 seat charge). On Friday to Sunday lunch the room becomes the curry shop Curry Ya Miyan. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Italian bar run by one person (September–October 2026 reviews); official site rakurakuza.smafo.biz.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Authentic Italian in a homey atmosphere, where you can eat and drink cheerfully" (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The iron pot was sizzling with a generous amount of ketchup-covered Neapolitan spaghetti! The edges of the pot were lined with eggs… a rich and nostalgic flavor!" — October 2026, iron-pot pasta lunch, large.
"Today's special pasta lunch for JPY 890. Includes a salad and toast. Since it's a one-man operation, it takes a little time." — September 2026.

places.cuisine: Yakiniku of A5 female Kuroge wagyu and fresh horumon · heart sashimi ¥1,000 · white raw senmai with cho-jang ¥1,000 · seared sirloin-cap yukhoe with egg yolk ¥1,600 · premium tongue ¥3,200–3,800 · tongue kalbi ¥900 · grilled wagyu shabu-shabu, seared by the owner, with ponzu or egg yolk ¥2,800 · outside skirt ¥2,800 · sirloin cap ¥2,500 · A5 strip loin ¥4,000 · kalbi ¥1,900 · thinly sliced salted tripe ¥1,200 · colon ¥1,200 · white honeycomb tripe ¥900 · a different sauce or salt for each cut, incl. a Kyoto-style "washing" dip · sudachi cold noodles ¥1,100–1,200 · 5 counter seats downstairs; private tatami rooms upstairs
places.notes: [Yakiniku · A5 wagyu and fresh horumon with a sauce for every cut, down a Soemoncho alley] A small yakiniku house hidden in an alley off Sennichimae-suji, open since 2022, with a five-seat counter below and private tatami rooms above, taking only three groups at a time. Non-offal cuts are A5 female Kuroge wagyu, the shop says, and the offal is chosen for freshness: start with the clean heart sashimi and the white senmai, then the seared yukhoe with egg yolk. Each cut comes with its own sauce, salt or dip, including a light Kyoto-style dip that washes away excess fat, and staff explain how to eat each one; the owner sears the wagyu yaki-shabu for you. Finish with the bright sudachi cold noodles. Diners spent ¥8,000–15,000. Open late; reserve for after 02:00. No small children.

chef_bio.background: Yakiniku restaurant (official site kyoto-anjutei.com; Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Offal such as tongue, skirt, liver and mino chosen above all for freshness; other cuts limited to A5 female Kuroge wagyu; only three groups at a time (official site).

places.notes: [Curry · weekend-only three-curry plates in Ura-Namba] A Friday-to-Sunday lunch curry counter that takes over the Italian bar Rakuraku Za in the Ura-Namba backstreets. There's one order: the three-curry plate (¥1,300), which changes with the season but in every review has paired a beef and pork keema, a gentle vegetable potage curry and a pork green keema. Recent potages have been new potato, corn, scallop and seaweed; the keemas have run from spring cabbage to citrus and red miso. Each is mild and well balanced, and the menu suggests mixing all three at the end. Add grilled cheese (+¥100) or grilled corn (+¥200). Lovers of fiery curry may find it tame. It can sell out; one diner was charged less when a curry ran short. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Weekend curry shop run in the Rakuraku Za space (2026 reviews; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The potage had a gentle flavor, combining the sweetness and umami of the fresh vegetables with a hint of spice. The two types of keema were not overly spicy, offering a well-balanced spice profile." — March 2026, three types ¥1,300.
"The standout was definitely the scallop potage. What a creative idea! The Beef, Pork, Shrimp, and Tomato Keema was also exceptional." — April 2026.

places.cuisine: Creative Japanese omakase that changes monthly · courses ¥8,800 and ¥11,000 · seasonal platter of about ten small appetizers · warm dish (hamo and matsutake in autumn) · toro-taku on red-vinegar rice · Saga beef roast beef over achar · Western-style seafood dish (abalone gratin or butter sauté) · Kuroge wagyu with simmered egg in a small pot, or a wagyu mille-feuille cutlet · ayu; turtle hot pot as an add-on · clay-pot rice · "Japanese ultra-smooth pudding" · sake and wine pairings · 6 counter seats, 8 semi-private table seats; private room for 4+
places.notes: [Japanese · hidden creative washoku omakase on a 7th floor in Amemura] A hideaway on the seventh floor of an Amemura building across from BIG STEP, reached through a narrow alley on the building's south side (call when close; first-timers get lost), open since 2017. The chef trained at a famous restaurant. The monthly omakase (¥8,800 or ¥11,000) is Japanese at heart with Western and ethnic twists, from a platter of about ten seasonal small bites to a warm hamo and matsutake bowl in autumn. The fixtures are what bring repeat diners back each month: toro-taku on red-vinegar rice, Saga beef roast beef over achar, a bubbling pot of wagyu with simmered egg, clay-pot rice, and a melting pudding one diner said could rival a dessert shop. Staff suggest sake and wine to match. Report allergies when you book.

chef_bio.background: Creative Japanese restaurant (official site jampa.co.jp; Tabelog). The chef trained at a famous restaurant (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The red vinegar sushi and roast beef are my all-time favorites… The black-haired Wagyu was served with simmered eggs… When the lid of the small pot was lifted, it was bubbling away." — September 2026, seasonal omakase, ninth visit.
"Despite being Japanese cuisine, the addition of ethnic flavors created a perfect balance… The conger eel was served in an ethnic style, wrapped in lettuce." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · light or rich chicken ramen and two-yolk mazesoba by Awaza] A small, clean ramen shop two minutes north of Awaza, open since 2022, where you order and pay on your phone by QR code. The light chicken ramen (¥900) is clear and full-flavored under generous thin-sliced chashu; the rich chicken and pork (¥950) is chicken-led, silky and not greasy despite the name, and you choose thin straight noodles or medium-thick curly hand-kneaded ones. For something different, the tamago-kake mazesoba (¥800) tosses firm flat noodles with two egg yolks and a seafood-flavored sauce. Mix it well. There's also a rich tsukemen on the hand-kneaded noodles, and sea bream bowls come and go. One diner found the phone ordering a hassle when the room was empty.

anecdotes.text: "Despite being rich, the broth was not overly greasy; it had a clear, silky texture that I really enjoyed!" — August 2026, rich chicken and pork ramen ¥950.

places.notes: [Ramen · niboshi and katsuobushi pork-bone ramen facing Nishisenba Park since 2010] A counter of 14 stylish seats down a small alley in front of Nishisenba Park, near Utsubo Park, running since 2010. Four broths share a pork-bone base: the most popular niboshi ramen (¥900), rich but balanced, with two chashu, half an egg, nori, menma and kaiware included; a rich, creamy katsuobushi seafood ramen that the owner recommends to first-timers; a sea bream shio soba; and a plain chuka soba. One diner of ten years usually orders the plum seafood shio with a free dab of wasabi. A chili-heaped version is milder than it looks. Order on a tablet, pay at the machine at the back. Weekday lunch, dinner on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, until sold out. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style ramen with beef tendon instead of pork, by Taisho Station] A Jiro-style shop a minute south of Taisho Station, opened in September 2024 in a former ramen shop, with a Kansai twist: instead of slabs of pork, the beef tendon ramen (¥1,000) comes topped with sweet-savory simmered beef tendon whose collagen melts into a light tonkotsu-shoyu. Call your vegetables, garlic and back fat as usual; it's lighter and easier than most Jiro bowls, so beginners do fine. The show-off topping is Negi Fire, scallions flash-fried tableside with hot onion oil, and you can film it. Spicy garlic chives (¥300) pack a real kick. Change it up midway with the table's pickled ginger or kombu-niboshi vinegar. There's a set with mini curry, and late hours most nights. Cash only.

"The visual impact was impressive, but surprisingly, the taste was much lighter than it looked. However, the umami was rich, and the collagen from the beef tendon melted into the broth." — August 2026, with Negi Fire.

places.notes: [Ramen · a lighter Jiro-style ramen with crisp vegetables in Taisho] A small counter near Taisho Station, open since 2015, serving Jiro-style ramen that is gentler than the genre: the broth is light enough to finish, the thick noodles are easy to eat, and the vegetables are blanched for seconds so they stay crisp. The ramen (¥990) comes with free large noodles; call garlic and back fat as you like, and the back fat really gets piled on. One regular wished the garlic and chashu were bolder. Spicy miso is a good variation, and there are Taiwanese mazesoba and tsukemen. Staff are kind and attentive. One diner found it opened at noon, not 11:30. Cash only; closed Mondays.

places.cuisine: Mazesoba and chuka ramen at the station · seafood mazesoba ¥900, large +¥100: pork-bone and seafood-stock sauce on the sweet side, chewy noodles, soft-boiled egg, menma, diced chashu, fish powder, green onion; rice to finish if you select it · noodles described as "Jumian" from a long-established Shin-Imamiya noodle maker · Taiwanese mazesoba · chuka ramen: nostalgic shoyu with chashu, menma, green onion, nori · kara-age, gyoza, rice · kombu vinegar, chili oil and shichimi on the table · counter and tables
places.notes: [Ramen · seafood mazesoba right by the Nankai gates at Shin-Imamiya] A new, clean noodle shop under Shin-Imamiya Station, steps from the Nankai ticket gates and open 11:00 to 23:00, so it's an easy stop before or after a train. The seafood mazesoba (¥900) mixes chewy noodles with a slightly sweet pork-bone and seafood sauce, egg, diced chashu and fish powder; select rice on the machine if you want to finish the sauce with it, and change it up with the table's kombu vinegar or chili oil. One diner wanted more seafood flavor. The chuka ramen is a nostalgic shoyu, easy to share with a child; staff brought a family separate plates and cups. Kara-age and gyoza fill out the menu. Reviews are mixed: one diner found it mediocre and the machine fussy with cash. Cards and QR accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · parent-chicken shoyu tori soba until 2 am, near Kyocera Dome] A second-floor chicken-ramen counter between Taisho Station and Kyocera Dome, open since 2023 and open until 2 am, so baseball crowds line the stairs after games. One diner traced the style to the nabeyaki ramen of Susaki in Kochi. The tori soba (¥900) is a piping-hot soy broth of long-simmered parent-hen bones with Kochi and Osaka soy and a bright hit of yuzu, on medium-thin straight egg noodles; one diner found the yuzu overpowering. The BLACK version packs garlic and black pepper; RED brings heat; the yuzu shio and a garlicky tori mazesoba fill out the menu. Finish with a chicken chazuke (¥550) or a mini chashu bowl. The limited chicken paitan often sells out. Cash only.

"I ordered the Chicken Soba Black for JPY 950… The garlic and black pepper really packed a punch, and the garlic flavor was delicious. It definitely got richer as I continued eating." — July 2025.

places.notes: [Ramen · weekday-lunch chuka soba with ¥250 unlimited mentaiko rice, near Higobashi] A retro-signed, second-floor bar near Higobashi that becomes a ramen shop at weekday lunch. The famous draw is the rice bar: add ¥250 and help yourself to unlimited rice, mentaiko, raw eggs, nori and furikake, and you can order it alone. The chuka soba (¥750) is a sweet, Kyushu-style soy broth on straight noodles that pairs well with all that rice. Heartier options include a back-fat mazesoba with raw egg (¥950, garlic to taste) and the Stanira soba, a spicy, garlicky bowl of garlic chives, chili and ginger. places.cuisine: Late-night tonkotsu ramen · Tenryu ramen, the recommendation: rich tonkotsu shoyu, melt-in-the-mouth chashu · classic ramen under a layer of fine back fat: rich pork-bone flavor yet not heavy, two thick slices of pork-belly chashu, plenty of green onion · lighter shio tonkotsu · chuka soba · miso ramen · ramen and fried rice set ¥1,150 · gyoza · extra noodles · bottled Asahi Super Dry · 13 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · late-night tonkotsu near Shin-Imamiya and Shinsekai] A thirteen-seat counter a few minutes from Shin-Imamiya, open since 2015 from 11:00 to midnight and packed late in the evening, when it serves as a finishing bowl after a night out. Indian staff keep the room running efficiently. The recommended Tenryu ramen is a rich tonkotsu shoyu with melt-in-the-mouth chashu; the classic bowl floats a layer of fine back fat over a pork-bone soup that is rich but not heavy, with two thick slices of pork belly. The shio tonkotsu is the lighter choice. Pair it with gyoza or the ramen and fried rice set (¥1,150), or order extra noodles. One nine-visit regular says every ramen here is good. Close to Shinsekai and busy with visitors, but not a tourist trap, one diner felt. Cash only; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Indian staff keep the room running efficiently (August 2026 review).

"The surface of the broth is generously covered with fine back fat… Surprisingly, it's not too heavy despite its appearance, and the broth has a solid depth and umami." — August 2026, classic ramen.

places.cuisine: Japanese sweets café and takeout · mitarashi dango, served warm in the café; takeout ¥90 each or 3 for ¥270 · "Moheji-yaki" dorayaki with a moist, refined batter · kintsuba with less-sweet azuki · fukumochi: chewy skin around chunky red bean · mitarashi soft serve with warm sauce · set B ¥880: mitarashi dango, kinako kanten, anko, shiratama and soft serve · parfait · matcha and hojicha · 20 seats
places.notes: [Sweets · warm mitarashi dango and dorayaki in the Namba underground mall] A small Japanese-sweets café and takeout counter in the NAMBA Nannan underground mall, connected to Namba Station and open 10:00 to 21:00. The thing to try is mitarashi dango, chewy and served warm in the café, which one diner had never had warm before; to go, it's ¥90 each or three for ¥270. The "Moheji-yaki" dorayaki has a moist, refined batter, the kintsuba lets the azuki speak and can sell out late in the day, and the fukumochi is chewy around chunky red bean. Sitting down, the set B (¥880) gathers warm dango, kinako kanten, anko, shiratama and soft serve, and the mitarashi soft serve pairs warm sauce with cold cream. Expect a short line at busy times. Cards accepted.

places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · light, fluffy okonomiyaki upstairs by Namba Station] A twelve-seat second-floor okonomiyaki shop a few minutes from Namba Station, cooked on the teppan in front of you. The batter is the point: crisp outside and fluffy within, thick but light, with a sauce that doesn't linger, so you leave without a heavy feeling. One repeat diner always orders the pork modern-yaki with a fried egg before a Shinkigeki show; the suji-negi-tama of slow-cooked beef tendon and green onion is another favorite. Try the house "Take soba," yakisoba wrapped in omelet and pressed. Add the spicy sauce from the table if you like it sharper. Being upstairs, it is easier to get in if you time your visit, one diner notes. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Okonomiyaki restaurant (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "I was amazed by how fluffy the batter was. The outside was perfectly grilled, while the inside was surprisingly soft… Despite its thickness, it didn't feel heavy at all." — September 2026, suji-negi-tama and butatama.
"It was essentially yakisoba wrapped in an omelet and slightly pressed… two types of sauce—spicy and regular—along with mayonnaise and bonito flakes." — May 2026, Take soba.

places.notes: [Japanese · seasonal Kansai kaiseki at a pine counter since 2005, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, sukiya-style kappo near Nipponbashi, open since 2005, serving kaiseki courses only, built on seasonal ingredients from the Kinki region and a gentle, deep dashi. Sit at the five-seat counter of single-board pine to watch the cooking, or take the horigotatsu tatami room. Dishes arrive in seasonal tableware with matching chopstick rests, and the sake list is wide; ask for pairings. The menu follows what's good that day, so one diner who booked expecting matsutake and turtle got conger eel and abalone instead. Rice comes with refills. Diners spent about ¥15,000–30,000, and the shop raised some prices in October 2026 for matsutake and crab. Children only with the same course.

chef_bio.background: Kappo serving kaiseki courses (official site shunsenwaraku-sanai.com; Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Kaiseki built on the five flavors, colors, senses and methods; Kinki-region seasonal ingredients in their early, peak and late stages; dishes adjusted to guests' requests (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The seasonal chopstick rests and tableware added to the visual delight of the experience. I also appreciated the variety of Japanese sake available." — May 2025.
"Each dish is crafted with great care, and the dashi (broth) was incredibly delicious and gentle in flavor. The service was excellent." — January 2026.

places.cuisine: Horse-meat specialist with Kumamoto touches · assorted basashi of five kinds, or seven with heart and tongue: thigh, tenderloin, loin, mane (fat), futaego and more · sakura yukhoe · horse tataki with onion and ponzu · horse shabu-shabu ("dashi shabu") finished with thick soba or rice porridge · grilled horse skewers, each with its own salt or sauce · horse tsukune · saibo (smoked dried horse) · horse gyoza · horse salami · carpaccio salad · horse sushi · horse nyumen · yukhoe rice bowl · Kumamoto-style hitomoji with vinegar miso · courses with all-you-can-drink · 20 seats: counter at the front, tables inside
places.notes: [Horse meat · basashi and horse shabu-shabu in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A horse-meat specialist set back in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building behind a noren, open since 2020, with a narrow counter by the kitchen and tables further in. The meat is sourced direct from producers, and diners remark on how clean it tastes, with none of the usual odor. Start with the assorted basashi, five kinds or seven with heart and tongue, from lean thigh and tenderloin to the rich mane fat, then a sakura yukhoe or tataki. On a cold night, the horse shabu-shabu is the warming choice, finished with unusually thick, soft soba; skewers come each with its own salt or sauce. One diner comes almost monthly and books Friday and Saturday well ahead. Smoking is allowed, so no one under 20.

chef_bio.background: Horse-meat specialist (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Horse meat sourced directly from producers (April 2026 review).

places.notes: [Ramen · late-night Takaida-style dark shoyu on thick noodles, near Tennoji] A one-person chuka soba counter on Tanimachi-suji a short walk from Tennoji, open from 19:00 to 03:00, a natural stop after a night out. It serves Takaida-style ramen, the Osaka and Higashi-Osaka genre: a dark, clear soy broth and thick straight noodles with real chew, under chashu, menma and green onion cut in big, crunchy pieces. The chuka soba is ¥700 and the chashu ramen ¥900 with generous slices. Diners differ on the broth: some find it punchy, one found it milder than it looks, another lukewarm, with tough chashu. Grab a rice ball from the counter, and help yourself to a canned beer. The owner is cheerful. Cash only; closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Ramen · garlic tonkotsu shoyu almost all night, by Kyocera Dome] The Kujo shop of the Tenyo garlic-ramen family, open since 1988 and now renovated and renamed from "Garlic Ramen Tenyo," serving from 11:00 straight through to 05:00 or 06:00. It fills after Kyocera Dome games. The ramen (¥1,100) is a surprisingly light tonkotsu shoyu that the garlic transforms: ask for none, a little or a lot, and stir it up from the bottom. The chashu is slow-cooked domestic pork so soft it falls apart, and it's even better shredded in sweet-spicy sauce over the B-set rice bowl (¥450, large free). The menu now runs to miso, a negi ramen, a tangy W vinegar ramen, curry noodles and tsukemen. One diner found the noodles clumped. Tenyo's Shinmachi and Taishobashi shops are also in this guide.

places.cuisine: Beef-bone paitan ramen · gyukotsu paitan ramen with soft-boiled egg ¥850: white, creamy yet light beef-bone soup slowly simmered, no dairy, beef-belly chashu, white negi, pea shoots, baby corn, homemade straight noodles · extra-meat gyukotsu paitan ¥1,250 · spicy gyukotsu paitan with egg ¥1,100 · lunch white rice ¥100 · roast beef rice · grilled pork rice bowl · 11 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · creamy beef-bone paitan ramen from ¥850 in Kitahama] A small weekday counter in Kitahama serving gyukotsu ramen, a white soup slow-simmered from beef bones, part of a family of beef-bone shops. It looks like tonkotsu but tastes lighter and gentler, creamy without dairy, so you'll likely finish the soup. The basic bowl with a soft-boiled egg is only ¥850; the extra-meat version (¥1,250) piles on thin, flavorful beef-belly chashu, and pea shoots and baby corn keep it fresh. The spicy version (¥1,100) brings real heat without hiding the beef. Noodles are homemade and straight, a bit firm. Add lunch rice for ¥100 or a roast beef rice bowl. One diner found the chashu tired one day. Weekdays only per Tabelog; cash only.

chef_bio.background: Beef-bone ramen shop, Kitahama branch, part of a group of beef-bone ramen shops (September 2026 review; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The distinctive feature of this ramen is the white broth, slowly simmered from beef bones. The rich umami of the beef is concentrated yet not overpowering, and the texture is creamy." — October 2026, extra-meat gyukotsu paitan ¥1,250.
"At first glance, the soup looks like a traditional tonkotsu ramen, but in reality, it's creamy yet light and very easy to drink, with a gentle flavor." — October 2026, gyukotsu paitan with egg ¥850.

places.notes: [Ramen · mapo mazesoba under a giant fried-to-order katsu, near Higobashi] A stylish, black-themed counter near Higobashi, open since 2024, whose signature is built for photos: a mapo mazesoba hidden under a chicken-thigh katsu so large it covers the bowl. Mix the noodles through the thick mapo first; it's rich with sweet bean sauce and a Sichuan-pepper tingle rather than fiery, and the katsu, fried to order, stays crisp in the sauce. Pick from five heat levels (three free); level 3 is sweat-inducing, one diner warns. A mini rice comes on the side to dive into the leftovers. The bowl now runs ¥1,600 after a price rise, and it's a lot of food. There's also a mapo rice, cold noodles in summer and a weekly set. Expect a short wait at lunch. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · abura soba by Kitahama, mixed from the bottom] A small, bright and clean abura soba shop between Kitahama and Yodoyabashi, open since 2018, busy at office lunch. The house Densho abura soba (¥890) is slightly spicy: smooth curly noodles coated in a moderately rich sauce under thin-sliced chashu and a pile of white negi. The wall sign says to mix everything thoroughly from the bottom, and the noodles turn chewy as you do. If you don't want heat, the chicken-negi abura soba (¥960) is mild and light. A shrimp shio version comes with rare chashu, and there's a light chicken shio soup ramen. Tune it with the vinegar, chili oil and garlic chips on the table. A ¥1,300 drink set adds menma and a menchi-katsu. Cash-only ticket machine; closed Sundays.

The draw for many is the rich tonkotsu tsukemen: thick, smooth, chewy noodles in a rich yet clean seafood and pork dip with chopped onion and thick grilled chashu, large at no extra cost. A repeat diner, though, swears by the mazesoba: choose shoyu (seafood-soy sauce, cheese, nori, flat chewy noodles) or curry (¥1,150, minced meat, garlic chives and a raw egg), and you'll be asked which when you hand over the ticket. Finish by tipping the small yuzu-kosho rice into the leftovers with a splash of dashi. One diner found the chashu a little salty. Cash only.

The shoyu ramen (¥1,100) is light, with a sharp soy and clean umami; diners split on it, from refreshing to too plain and sour. places.notes: [Ramen · golden-sesame tantanmen near Tenmabashi] A twelve-seat tantanmen counter near Tenmabashi with a regular who has logged 17 visits and can't go two weeks without it. The kin-goma tantanmen (¥980) is the order: a thick, creamy, sesame-forward soup that's easy to drink, somewhere between soup and dry tantanmen, over thin noodles with minced meat and a good amount of vegetables. Pick a heat level, with three free; level 3 makes the lips tingle. The ritual is the finish: add set A (¥170) and tip the rice and kimchi into the last of the soup like a porridge, with more ground sesame and Sichuan pepper from the table. At lunch, large noodles are free. A chilled tantanmen appears in summer. Cash only.

places.notes: [Eel · crisp, unsteamed eel courses with eel shabu-shabu, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] An eight-seat eel counter on a second floor in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, opened at the end of August 2026 and on some days already booked from noon to close. Live eels are prepared on the spot and grilled Kansai-style without steaming over fierce heat, so the skin comes out crisp, like a potato chip in the shirayaki, while the flesh stays fluffy and juicy. The ¥7,700 course walks through it all: a creamy yuba sesame tofu, rare eel shabu-shabu in ponzu, crisp shirayaki and kabayaki side by side, then an unaju of a whole eel with liver soup; three kinds of sansho let you play with the finish. A ¥4,800 unadon is the shorter route. Call ahead for red-vinegar sushi. Diners compare it favorably with Japan's best eel shops. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Eel restaurant (Tabelog; September–October 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Live eels prepared to order; no steaming, grilled over strong heat for crisp skin and fluffy flesh (October 2026 reviews).

Small dishes are shown at the counter and you pick what you like, then grilled fish, sashimi and nigiri as you please, so light drinkers can go straight to sushi and sake lovers can linger. The rice is pressed so gently that it settles under the topping, and one diner singles out a surprising shiitake nigiri and crisp-skinned eel. The chef keeps the room lively and picks sake to match. Expect ¥15,000–30,000. One diner has come for 24 years. Closed Thursday and Sunday; last entry 20:30.

places.notes: [Japanese · one-chef creative washoku counter by Shinsaibashi] A quiet counter of six to eight seats on the fourth floor of a building a minute from Shinsaibashi, open since 2024 and run by a single chef who cooks, serves and watches over every guest. A young chef opened this eight-seat counter after seven years at a Michelin two-star restaurant. The cooking is refined rather than flashy: the seven-dish course with drinks (¥11,000) runs from a mizuna and beef appetizer through a sashimi platter with sea urchin and crab, a chewy lotus-root dumpling in kuzu sauce and Saikyo-grilled flounder to seasonal tempura and a clay-pot rice, with leftovers turned into onigiri for tomorrow. À la carte, diners praise the firm tuna, very fresh sea urchin and a precisely cooked steak. The sake list is broad. Open late, and on Sunday nights when much of Minami is closed. Heated tobacco only.

chef_bio.background: Creative Japanese counter run by one chef (August 2026 review; Tabelog). A young chef opened this eight-seat counter after seven years at a Michelin two-star restaurant (July 2026 review).

places.cuisine: Oden and Japanese plates with sake · house dashi blended on the base of the long-established 神楽's taste · oden: daikon cut with a star in the middle, tofu scored like sea anemones, shungiku steeped in broth, beef tendon, yuba, mochi kinchaku · sashimi platter · fried dishes, gyoza, salted green peppers · broad sake list · 12 counter seats and a table for four; semi-private seating
places.notes: [Izakaya · oden and sake by Nagahoribashi] A modern, lively oden izakaya in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2020, where the counter lets you watch the cooking and it's often fully booked, even on a rainy Monday. Three young men run it, with refreshing service. The house dashi is a blend built on the taste of the long-established 神楽; diners call it fresh and deep, though one wanted it stronger. The oden is playfully cut, with a star in the daikon and tofu scored like sea anemones; one diner had never understood shungiku in oden until it arrived here, steeped and fragrant. The sashimi is serious, there's gyoza and fried food, and the sake list is long. Service is quick and friendly. Note the ¥600 seat charge, the two-hour limit, and that smoking is allowed.

places.notes: [Izakaya · one-person Showa-retro izakaya deep in Jumbo Yokocho] A tiny, warm counter at the back of the neon-lit Jumbo Yokocho alley in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, run single-handed since 2009 by a friendly owner. It feels straight out of the Showa era: cheap, homemade dishes like natto-yaki, pork kimchi, butter-fried itawasa and edamame, nikujaga and chikuzen-ni, and drinks poured famously strong, with shochu and green tea at about seven to three. Order a few dishes at a time, since one person cooks everything; customers end up helping each other out and chatting, which is half the charm. The entrance is easy to miss, so allow time to find it. Open until 2 am most nights. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · whipped chicken paitan with fried burdock, on Tabelog's Ramen 100 since 2020, Higobashi] The original Zagin, a twelve-seat counter two minutes from Higobashi and on Tabelog's Ramen 100 every year from 2020 to 2025. The tori soba (¥1,000) is a chicken paitan whipped to a creamy froth before it's served, on thin straight noodles with low-temperature chicken and pork chashu and a tangle of fried burdock that turns from crunchy to soft as it soaks (one diner found the burdock missing on one visit); an eleven-visit regular calls it a favorite ramen in Osaka. There's a shoyu version and a chicken tsuke soba with a thick, concentrated dip; one regular found the rich shio and the shoyu less special than the original. Buy a ticket outside, then queue; staff are calm and polite. Open 10:30 to 22:30 every day. Cash only. The Niboshi branch is also in this guide.

places.cuisine: Sea bream tantanmen · tai tanmen ¥960: creamy sea bream (Uwajima) and sesame soup with spice and numbing to order, medium-thick wavy noodles, meat miso, mizuna, rare pork and chicken chashu, menma, shredded fried potato, crisp lotus root with balsamic · tai tanmen + tai-meshi set ¥1,200: finish the sea-bream rice with the soup like a risotto, then with poured tai dashi like ochazuke · soupless tai tanmen lunch set ¥1,200 · seasoned egg +¥150 · monthly limited bowls ¥1,600, e.g. crab and porcini bisque (October), chilled scallop and basil (August) · 4 counter seats and tables
places.notes: [Ramen · sea bream tantanmen with a tai-meshi finish, near Higobashi] A popular tantanmen shop near Higobashi, open since 2018, which one review describes as crossing Japanese sea bream dashi, Sichuan tantanmen and French technique. The tai tanmen was created by a chef with 12 years in French cuisine. The tai tanmen (¥960) is a creamy soup of Uwajima sea bream and sesame, heat and numbing to order (level 2 is moderate, level 3 genuinely hot), over chewy wavy noodles with meat miso, rare chashu, mizuna and shredded fried potato. Order the set with tai-meshi (¥1,200): eat some plain, add soup for a risotto, then pour on the free tai dashi for ochazuke. A soupless version and a ¥1,600 monthly special, such as crab and porcini bisque, keep one four-visit diner coming back. One diner barely tasted the sea bream in the noodles, but loved the rice. Buy a ticket and expect a short line after 11:30.

chef_bio.background: Tai tanmen specialist (official site taitanmendakishimetai.com; Tabelog). The tai tanmen was created by a chef with 12 years in French cuisine (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Japanese sea bream dashi with Sichuan dandan noodles and French techniques; Uwajima sea bream (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The soup is a spicy broth based on sea bream, paired with medium-thick wavy noodles. The toppings include meat miso, mizuna greens, pork and chicken chashu, menma (bamboo shoots), and shredded fried potatoes." — October 2026, tai tanmen level 2 ¥960.
"I enjoyed it in three stages: first as is, then adding the soup for a risotto-like experience, and finally pouring the Tai broth over it for a delightful ochazuke." — October 2026, tai-meshi set.

places.notes: [Ramen · clam-broth ramen with three kinds of chashu, by Higobashi] A quiet, café-like ramen shop a minute from Higobashi, open since 2022, built on clam broth. The owner trained at Kaimen Mikawa in Shimokitazawa, Tokyo. The clam ramen comes clear and light in shio or shoyu, rich in shellfish umami, over thin noodles with crunchy chopped onion, thick menma and three kinds of low-temperature chashu; one repeat diner, after trying everything, still names the clam and Kyoto bonito chuka soba (special ¥1,150) the one everyone will like. At lunch any rice is ¥100: take the clam rice and pour the last of the soup over it as chazuke. Seasonal bowls rotate, from Ise lobster with truffle butter to chilled oyster and the cold Suriyan with two egg yolks. One diner found the plain clam ramen monotonous. Expect a short wait at weekday noon. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Clam-broth ramen shop (official site ramenthree.com; Tabelog). The owner trained at Kaimen Mikawa in Shimokitazawa, Tokyo (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The three types of chashu are cooked at low temperatures, making them thick and moist, while the thin noodles pair well with the clear broth, allowing you to enjoy the lightness typical of shio ramen along with the rich umami of the shellfish." — October 2026, special clam ramen ¥1,200.

"After finishing the noodles, I poured the leftover soup over the Finishing Clam Rice. It turned into a clam broth chazuke, and the flavors of the asari (clam) tsukudani, rice crackers, seaweed, and rice filled my mouth." — October 2026, Suriyan ¥1,000.

places.notes: [Ramen · fish-powder tonkotsu-gyokai ramen and mazesoba, large free, near Higobashi] A thirteen-seat branch of the Kozou ramen shops on the Edobori side of Higobashi, open daily since 2021, and one diner's monthly habit. The Kozou ramen (¥1,000) is a thick, creamy tonkotsu-seafood soup heaped with fish powder, rich but not heavy enough to stop you finishing it; the large size costs nothing extra. The tonkotsu-gyokai mazesoba (¥1,150), billed as the most popular, gets the same fish powder with egg, chashu and chopped onion; mix it well from the bottom and add garlic from the table. One diner found the mazesoba a bit sweet and preferred the ramen. Seasonal specials rotate, from a chilled negi chuka to a chashu zaru chuka with up to 350 g of free noodles. Open 11:00 to 22:00 every day; PayPay accepted.

anecdotes.text: "Packed with fish powder, the rich tonkotsu broth is thick and creamy, yet not heavy at all! Before I knew it, I had finished the entire bowl of soup!" — September 2026, Kozou ramen ¥1,000.
"I mixed it well to coat everything with the rich sauce, and it was a real treat. The egg and chashu (braised pork) were both incredibly satisfying." — October 2026, tonkotsu-gyokai mazesoba ¥1,150.

places.notes: [Ramen · Niigata-style back-fat niboshi chuka soba in Kitahama] A thirteen-seat counter a few minutes from Kitahama, reopened in March 2026 with a new name and menu, serving a style that one diner calls hard to find in Osaka: Niigata back-fat niboshi chuka soba. The bowl (¥1,140 with a seasoned egg) is a pork clear soup with a strong niboshi hit and soy, buried in back fat, minced onion and iwanori seaweed, over thick, wavy, low-hydration noodles you chew more than slurp, under a big, tender slice of pork-shoulder chashu. A plainer chuka soba (¥890) comes light or rich. Add the chashu-egg rice bowl (¥500). The broth can run salty; one diner couldn't finish it one day. Open until 00:30 on weeknights. Cards and IC accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · clear jidori shoyu and shio, and inventive summer chilled bowls, by Kujo] A small, slightly hidden counter three minutes from Kujo, open since 2023 and usually run by one cook who chats with guests and has adjusted a recipe in response to guest feedback. The owner previously ran Naniwa Tonkotsu Ramen Taisho Bashi Manten near Taisho Station before going independent. The broth is a clear soup of Tajima chicken and Tanba black chicken with real kombu and a delicate seafood dashi; the shoyu ramen is deep enough to drink to the last drop, with firm straight noodles and pink rare chashu. Pair it with the tamago-kake gohan, made with a branded egg. Summer brings the stars: a chilled shio ramen (¥1,200) with tomato ice cubes and two chashu, and a weekend chilled hamo ramen with sudachi, best tried on the spoon first. With one person cooking, expect waits when it's busy. Order and pay in cash up front.

places.notes: [Ramen · beginner-friendly Jiro-style ramen in Edobori] A thirteen-seat counter near Higobashi, open since November 2024, serving Jiro-style ramen without the rituals: you buy a ticket, enter in order and skip the topping call. The standard 200 g bowl has a sharp soy flavor balanced by the sweetness of noodles and vegetables, which go up to double-extra; the fat is unseasoned, so eat it with the noodles, and the pork is firm and lean. The soupless ramen (¥1,100) is a repeat diner's order, the cold TKM coats the noodles in egg, and the soupless tantanmen with an onsen egg is properly spicy. Pile on mayonnaise, pork scraps or a raw egg if you want the full effect. Lunch rarely has a wait. Cash only.

places.cuisine: Creative sushi course · course ¥22,000 (September 2026) · each piece with its own house sauce and condiments, and hidden knife work · grilled kuruma shrimp with eggplant, bell pepper and karasumi · flounder · sea bream with yuzu · aori squid scored fine and topped with sea urchin · Beni Haruka sweet potato chawanmushi · charcoal-grilled mackerel with condiments and ume · bonito in shuto · sardine · tuna (chutoro, marinated akami) · Kanazawa saba sushi · anago in nori · add-ons: toro-taku roll, "adult" ebi-mayo, sea urchin hand roll (¥10,000) · spend ¥20,000–40,000 · 6 counter seats, one table for four
places.notes: [Sushi · creative sushi with a sauce for every piece, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A ten-seat sushi room on Suomachi-dori, open since 2016, a Tabelog Award Bronze winner in 2025 and 2026 and so hard to book that one diner waited a year. It breaks from Edomae: each piece comes with its own house sauce or condiments and hidden knife work, like aori squid scored so finely it turns fluffy, topped with sea urchin. The ¥22,000 course might open with grilled kuruma shrimp under karasumi, run through flounder, yuzu-scented sea bream and a sweet potato chawanmushi, then grilled mackerel with ume and condiments, tuna and anago. Save room for the add-ons: a toro-taku roll and an "adult" ebi-mayo one diner calls a must, though one diner found the ¥10,000 uni hand roll and the overall bill steep, and the extras not offered clearly. Closed Wednesdays.

places.notes: [Rice bowl · ten slices of marinated tuna for ¥1,100 in Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A six-seat wooden counter tucked at the back of a building near Shinsaibashi, run by two people and serving essentially one thing: tekka-don. Ten slices of lean tuna, marinated in a sesame-scented soy sauce, are fanned over warm rice and shredded nori with a quail egg yolk and wasabi in the middle, ¥1,100 with red miso soup and pickles; seven slices are ¥900. On Thursday and Friday it switches to a melting chutoro version. One diner has come for 27 years. The sauce comes already on and runs a little strong for one diner, and the rice is soft. It fills at opening but turns over fast, and it closes when the tuna runs out, so go early. Cash only.

The hot-and-cold contrast is the point; eat it quickly before the ice cream melts. Choose vanilla, chocolate or mixed. Opinions vary from "incredibly delicious" to just average, and one diner found ¥700 for a mixed soft serve steep, but it's a fun, cheap Amemura stop and easy to eat walking. Open 11:00 to 21:00. Cash only.

places.notes: [Yakitori · ¥3,500 chicken course grilled on a teppan in front of you, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A quiet twelve-seat counter on the third floor of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, open since 2020, where chicken is grilled not over charcoal but on an iron plate at your place, then served with three sauces and salt. There's one ¥3,500 course: appetizers, assorted chicken cuts, a tsukune with cheese and quail egg, and a finale of grilled rice balls, crisp outside and soaked in sauce, which diners single out. Add a potato salad, and drinks run ¥400–700, so the night comes to about ¥4,000–6,000. The cook often works alone, so on a full night drinks can be slow and one diner found the cook too busy to talk. Reservation only, same day is fine. Cash only. The sign is easy to miss.

places.notes: [Izakaya · live octopus a dozen ways, on a 7th floor by Shinsaibashi] A calm, hidden izakaya on the seventh floor of a building two minutes from Shinsaibashi, open since 2020 and devoted to live octopus, mainly from Akashi. It's rare to find octopus treated this many ways: firm, sweet sashimi; octopus shabu-shabu, sliced thin and swished briefly in broth (the dish to try); grilled octopus; octopus kimchi and yukhoe; and takoyaki and Akashiyaki made with live octopus, which have a different texture from the usual. Finish with the octopus rice or an octopus-dashi chazuke. A whole-octopus course lets you choose from the day's preparations, and portions are generous enough that leftovers can be packed to go. Service is warm. Open until midnight. Cards and QR accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · light tonkotsu and egg-topped char-rice by Tennoji] A nine-seat, dimly lit counter about five minutes from Tennoji, known for its char-rice: fried rice under a fluffy omelet, seasoned lightly on purpose so you finish it with the garlic or wasabi sauces on the table. The tonkotsu comes white, black (with black garlic oil) or red, and one diner found it lighter and less salty than expected, closer to Mokkosu than Hakata; it comes with about five slices of chashu and wood ear mushroom. Extra back fat is free, and so are pickled ginger, spicy takana, grated garlic, fried onion and mayonnaise. The Manpuku set pairs a bowl with a small char-rice. A chashu chuka soba (¥1,300) on thick noodles is the other option. Free half-size kaedama until 15:00 on weekdays. Buy tickets at the machine outside; cash or PayPay only.

places.notes: [Ramen · punchy chili-and-garlic chuka soba by Tenmabashi] An eleven-seat shop a minute from Tenmabashi, open since 2023 and now busy thanks to social media: check in on the touch panel out front and expect a wait (about 25 minutes to get in, one August lunch). The beef horumon chuka soba brings more chili and garlic, and one diner found the sour and spicy djanmen (¥1,800) rich to the last bite. Limited bowls rotate: Bachiro (¥1,100 with extra sprouts) on borrowed noodles, and a chilled tantan mazesoba in summer. Add a meat-taku rice bowl (¥550). Cards and QR accepted.

places.cuisine: Yokohama-style iekei ramen · ramen: pork bones and chicken carcasses with a mild soy tare, chicken oil, medium-thick short noodles from Inoue Seimen, smoked oven-roasted pork-thigh chashu and shredded chashu, komatsuna, negi, nori; noodles, flavor and oil to order · jō ramen ¥1,000: extra chashu, two more nori, half a seasoned egg · chashu ramen ¥1,100 · fresh spinach instead +¥50 · chopped onion ¥100 · rice free at lunch (100 or 150 g), 200 g ¥100 · table: doubanjiang, garlic, ginger, vinegar, sesame, ramen pepper, pickled cucumber, furikake · 8 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · lighter iekei with smoked chashu by Tsuruhashi] An eight-seat counter about ten minutes from Tsuruhashi, open since May 2025, with lines on weekends. The broth of pork bones and chicken carcasses is creamy and rich but easy to drink, with a mild soy tare and chicken oil, over chewy medium-thick short noodles from Inoue Seimen; order firmness, flavor and oil to taste. Smoked, oven-roasted thigh chashu (firm and meaty) and shredded chashu sit with komatsuna and nori. The jō ramen (¥1,000) adds chashu, nori and half an egg. Rice is free at lunch; top it with the pickled cucumber and furikake, and finish with doubanjiang from the table. One diner calls it possibly the best iekei in Osaka; another found the broth thinner and the chashu dry on a later visit. Staff see you off at the door.

"The noodles were thick and had a strong texture, giving a firm impression with less chewiness. The chashu was moist and tender, with a perfect contrast of smoky flavor and meaty goodness." — October 2026, firm noodles and extra oil.

places.notes: [Ramen · tidy mazesoba with a rice finish at Higobashi] An eleven-seat shop right by Higobashi exit 9, open since April 2023 and part of MAREN, the mazesoba shop with a branch in Shinsaibashi. The shoyu mazesoba (¥980) coats thick, chewy noodles in a sauce that's rich but not heavy and arrives neatly arranged; add niboshi vinegar halfway, then mix the small scoop of rice into what's left. The chicken shio mazesoba gets its lift from shiso, and there's a chicken shoyu chashu version. The chicken paitan ramen is less loved: one diner saw it made from powders blended into a clear liquid on an IH burner. Order on the touch panel. Lines build after 12:00, so go early or late. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Mazesoba shop; sister shop of MAREN Shinsaibashi (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The thick noodles are coated in a flavorful sauce that's delicious! It's rich but not too heavy… I added some niboshi vinegar for a flavor change, which made it even smoother!" — October 2026, shoyu mazesoba.
"To finish off, you can mix in a small plate of rice, which is so tasty that I can't help but finish it all…" — September 2026, shoyu mazesoba ¥980.

places.notes: [Ramen · clam-broth ramen and a ¥650 breakfast bowl at Higobashi] A stylish ten-seat counter three minutes from Higobashi, open since October 2025 and sharing its name with Ramen ThreE nearby. The house bowl is a light broth of clam, scallop and dried seafood, with clam out front, over straight, medium-thin low-hydration noodles, topped with two kinds of chicken chashu and rare pork loin; sansho from the table lifts the aroma. There's also a clam and Kyoto bonito chuka soba, a creamy clam-and-pork shio and a rich tonkotsu shoyu. On weekdays it opens at 7:00 for morning ramen (¥650) with free egg-over-rice or natto rice. One diner found the morning bowls a bit salty. Register on LINE and the fourth bowl is free. Cards and QR accepted.

anecdotes.text: "The soup was a blend of clam, scallop, and dried seafood, with the clam flavor being slightly dominant. It was a light broth… The noodles were straight, medium-thin, and had a low water content, giving them a nice bite." — October 2026, clam tare ramen (shoyu).
"With the morning ramen, you can enjoy free egg over rice or natto rice. Both the Shoyu Ramen and the clam broth ramen are priced the same at JPY 650." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · chicken stewed ramen and lunch sets, izakaya by night, by Tenmabashi] A fifteen-seat basement counter on Tanimachi-suji, five minutes from Tenmabashi, serving ramen at lunch and turning into an all-you-can-eat-and-drink izakaya in the evening; by name and one diner's account, it is a branch of Okamoto Shoten near Kitahama. The chicken stewed ramen (¥950, with chashu and egg) looks rich and frothy but drinks smooth, with chicken sweetness. The menu is long: sets pair a bowl with a mini rice bowl, chicken curry or kara-age, and there's seafood shoyu with rare chashu, chicken paitan tsukemen and a spicy seafood ramen that one diner found heavy and short on seafood. Another found the ramen average but good value. From 13:30 a mini rice bowl is free. Cash or PayPay; smoking allowed.

places.cuisine: Seafood and chicken paitan ramen · ramen ¥850: double soup of seafood and chicken paitan, slightly thick, on thin low-hydration noodles from Menya Teigaku in Kyoto; pork-belly chashu, menma, green onion, white onion · chashu ramen ¥1,000 (three thick slices; seasoned egg to ¥1,150) · Dive Rice: kimchi rice to drop into the leftover soup · chashu rice bowl ¥300 at lunch · rice ¥200, ¥100 at lunch · 8 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · seafood-and-chicken paitan in the Yodoyabashi basement] An eight-seat, calm, Japanese-style counter in the basement of the Keihan Yodoyabashi Building, reachable underground from Yodoyabashi and Kitahama, open since 2023 as a new concept from Yawaragi, an izakaya in Shinsaibashi. The ramen (¥850) is a double soup of seafood and chicken paitan, slightly thick, rich but easy to drink, with the seafood coming through as you slurp the thin, firm, low-hydration Menya Teigaku noodles. Tender pork-belly chashu comes in thick slices in the chashu ramen (¥1,000). Finish with Dive Rice: kimchi rice you drop into the last of the soup. Rice is half price at lunch. Pay as you order. Cards and QR accepted.

places.cuisine: Chuka soba, seasonal white tonkotsu soba and fried rice · chuka soba (most popular): kombu and shellfish broth, wheat-forward noodles, two kinds of chashu incl. grilled pork belly · shio soba · seasonal white tonkotsu ("shiro-tan") soba, changing four times a year: autumn salmon and miso ¥1,180 (frothy miso white soup, loosely wavy noodles, grilled salmon, chashu, sautéed onion, cabbage and shimeji, bean sprouts, kinome, fried onion); summer Sichuan Chengdu tantan; spring firefly squid and sakura shrimp · summer chilled tantanmen with rare chashu, chicken breast, lemon and cream cheese · wok fried rice with burnt soy, extra butter or large · ramen and fried rice set ¥1,580 · gyoza
places.notes: [Ramen · kombu-shellfish chuka soba and seasonal white soups, with wok fried rice, by Kujo] A clean counter by Kujo Station, open here since April 2025 after moving from Namba, where you can watch the fried rice tossed in the wok and the bowls carefully plated. The most popular bowl is the chuka soba: a kombu and shellfish broth with a strong wheat aroma from the noodles and two kinds of chashu, one a grilled pork belly. The white tonkotsu soba changes every three months; autumn 2026 is salmon and miso in a frothy soup with sautéed vegetables (¥1,180). Summer brings a chilled tantanmen with cream cheese and lemon. The fried rice, fluffy with burnt soy and optional butter, draws its own fans (one diner warns it can taste a bit salty), and the set (¥1,580) pairs it with a bowl. Warm service. Buy a ticket at the entrance; cash only. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.origin: Opened in Namba on 12 December 2022 and moved to Kujo on 1 April 2025; a second shop, mendokoro HACK Nakazaki, opened March 2026 (October 2026 review; Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: Ramen and fried-rice counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Chuka soba; seasonal white tonkotsu soba; wok fried rice.

places.notes: [Sushi · ¥4,400 omakase that ends in seafood ramen, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] An eight-seat counter of the 881 Group, open since January 2026 on a hard-to-find third floor (take the emergency stairs from the second; the door has no sign). The listing says the chef trained at Michelin-rated and well-known sushi restaurants in Ginza. There's one course, ¥4,400, in two seatings at 17:30 and 20:00: soft-shell turtle soup, rare katsuo, then nigiri worked by aging, kombu-curing and vinegaring, such as four-day saba, kombu suzuki, sardine and nodoguro, plus a mackerel bozushi, steamed anago and a tuna and herring-roe hand roll. It finishes with a seafood shio ramen in the size you choose, then sweet tamago. All-you-can-drink is ¥2,200 more. Several diners rate the value outstanding. Lively, casual and good for a first sushi counter. Card only.

places.notes: [Sushi · ¥18,000 aged-sushi course with drinks included, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm ten-seat counter on a fourth floor, open since November 2025, with one all-in course (¥18,000) that includes alcohol or soft drinks. The rice is seasoned firmly with red vinegar and carries aged toppings, such as four-day sea bream, kombu-cured kisu and tuna from the Osaka supplier Teramoto Shoten, served as chutoro, marinated bluefin and otoro. Between pieces come creative plates: a mascarpone chawanmushi that eats like carbonara, Densuke anago shabu-shabu, abalone liver sauce and an uni don with two kinds of sea urchin. A fried mehikari roll and milk pudding close it out. Two seatings nightly, weekend lunch, reserve by the day before; 5% service charge.

places.cuisine: Mizutaki (jidori chicken hot pot) · courses: Hashi (smallest), Sai (with chicken sashimi) · mizutaki of Gunma black chicken: a rich but not heavy broth, soft-cooked Chinese cabbage, grated yam, house yuzu-kosho; staff cook the pot · finish: broth poured over rice, zosui or tea rice · chicken starters: peperoncino, tsukune hamburger, chicken prosciutto · chicken shabu-shabu · pasta with lettuce · baguette with chicken prosciutto and cheese · salt-grilled chicken neck · chicken ponzu · dessert · 4 counter seats and 3 tables (2 low kotatsu tables)
places.notes: [Chicken · mizutaki hot pot of jidori chicken in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, Japanese-style mizutaki specialist on the fifth floor of a bar building just off the arcade from Shinsaibashi, with a short counter, low kotatsu tables and three staff. The courses start with chicken plates (peperoncino, a tsukune hamburger, chicken prosciutto, and sashimi on the Sai course) before the hot pot, which staff cook for you. Gunma black chicken is tender in a rich but not heavy broth, with soft cabbage, grated yam and house yuzu-kosho. Finish with broth poured over rice, zosui or tea rice. One diner liked the pasta with lettuce enough to want seconds. Courses run from the small Hashi upward. Seen off at the elevator. Cards accepted; closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Ramen · rich miso ramen on thick curly noodles, Edobori] A two-floor miso ramen shop four minutes from Higobashi, open since February 2026, in an area where one diner calls proper miso ramen rare. The miso soup is rich and a little sweet under a thin layer of oil, clinging to medium-thick curly noodles that are firm and chewy, with thick, meaty chashu. The ajitama miso ramen (¥1,150) adds a soft, well-seasoned egg. A large size costs nothing extra, and there's tamago-kake gohan. One diner found a link to Miso Noodle Koji of the Tsukemen Ide brand; another got a lukewarm bowl. Ticket machine (cash or PayPay).

places.notes: [Ramen · weekly-changing ramen in a Kitahama basement bar] A hidden basement counter near Kitahama, open since September 2025: by day it serves ramen, by night it is the whiskey bar BULLSEYE. The ramen is the creation of a former curry chef. The menu changes every week (check Instagram) and leans on seafood broths and spice. Past bowls include a chilled seafood-broth clear shio with grilled pork and chicken breast, a chilled clam ramen whose deep, clear broth one diner found astonishing, a chilled tororo ramen with grilled gizzards, and a shrimp paitan with a hint of curry. Many come with a mini takikomi rice; pour the leftover broth over it. One diner disliked the seasoning powder on a cold bowl. One person ran it on an August visit, and bowls took 10–15 minutes. PayPay only.

places.cuisine: Emulsified Jiro-style ramen · Fukurou ramen: creamy, emulsified tonkotsu soup, slightly sweet and not too salty, bean sprouts and cabbage, medium-thick flat straight noodles, tender chashu; garlic, vegetables and seasoned back fat to taste · mini 150 g ¥1,000 · 200 g ¥1,100 · 250 g +¥100 · 300 g +¥150 · miso ramen ¥1,050 · soupless ramen · tsukemen · summer chilled chuka · extra chashu slice +¥200 · spicy minced meat +¥200 · quail eggs · raw egg · extra vegetables in a side bowl +¥150 · table: vinegar, fish powder, pepper, chili · 8 counter seats
places.notes: [Ramen · emulsified Jiro-style tonkotsu by Tsuruhashi] An eight-seat counter a few minutes from Tsuruhashi, open since 2019, which one diner with more than twenty visits calls the best Jiro-style ramen in Kansai. Unlike the usual soy-heavy Jiro bowl, the soup is a creamy, emulsified tonkotsu, slightly sweet and not too salty, so even extra back fat goes down easily. Noodles are medium-thick, flat and straight, smooth rather than chewy. Pick the noodle weight (150–300 g) and your garlic, vegetables and fat on the touch panel, so there's no call to learn; extra vegetables can water the soup down. There's also miso, soupless and tsukemen. Vinegar or fish powder from the table changes the flavor. Expect a line at opening; keep the narrow sidewalk clear. Cash only. Kept clean.

The pick of one long-time diner is the Tomaton, tonkotsu with a spicy tomato and garlic sauce that one compares to soup pasta, though two others found it ordinary. Half kaedama is ¥140. places.notes: [Chinese · neighborhood champon, gyoza and fried rice by Tamatsukuri] A small local Chinese diner just south of Nagahori-dori near Tamatsukuri, open since 2012, run by an elderly couple with the TV on. The chef has nearly half a century of experience. The menu runs to fifteen noodle dishes, and the champon stands out: a big, piping-hot bowl of chicken-and-soy soup piled with pork, shrimp and vegetables over chewy noodles. Sets are cheap: champon with half fried rice for ¥750–1,000. The fried rice is fluffy, with roast ham, sausage and bacon. The gyoza have handmade wrappers and a ginger-heavy filling (five for ¥350). There's also gomoku ramen, a tonkotsu Kyushu ramen, yakisoba and kara-age. Order out loud and pay after. Cash only; smoking area inside.

places.notes: [Ramen · sansho mazesoba in a retro arcade behind Tennoji] A street-stall-style counter of eight, walled with clear vinyl, inside the dim, Showa-era Hanwa shopping arcade just north of JR Tennoji, opened in July 2026 by the company behind Stand Sonoda. The sansho mazesoba (¥1,200) piles sweet-spicy meat miso, egg yolk, menma and crunchy red onion on thick, firm flat noodles. The sansho starts mild, so grind more from the mill on the counter, then add the chili oil or nam pla vinegar halfway; finish the leftover miso with rice. Also chuka soba (¥980) and a banmian (¥880). Open until 2:00. Ticket machine at the entrance; cash only; smoking allowed.

places.cuisine: Tonkotsu ramen · tonkotsu ramen ¥750: smooth, meaty pork-bone soup, thin-to-medium straight noodles, three slices of lean chashu plus chunky chashu pieces, half a seasoned egg · A set: tonkotsu ramen + rice ¥800 · B set: tonkotsu ramen + takana rice ¥850 · chashu ramen · extra noodles ¥150 · beer
places.notes: [Ramen · one-person tonkotsu lunch counter by Morinomiya] A small tonkotsu shop two minutes from Morinomiya, open since 2013 and now lunch-only (11:00–13:45, Mon–Sat), run by one person. You smell the pork as you walk in. The tonkotsu (¥750) is smooth and meaty, rich without a heavy aftertaste, on straight thin-to-medium noodles, with three slices of lean chashu, chunky fatty pieces and half a seasoned egg; one diner calls it among the best tonkotsu in Kansai. The A set adds rice (¥800), the B set takana rice (¥850). Bowls come in about three minutes. Two diners found the rice soft or clumpy. Bus your own dishes. Cash only.

anecdotes.text: "This isn't a thick, heavy pork bone broth. It's light yet has a rich flavor, paired with medium-thick straight noodles. The ramen comes with half a seasoned egg and a generous amount of finely sliced chashu." — October 2026, B lunch set ¥850.
"The broth is smooth, showcasing the rich flavor of pork and a strong meaty essence." — September 2026, tonkotsu ramen ¥750.

It's à la carte, with a run of raw-meat plates (outside-skirt yukhoe, heart and omasum sashimi) before the grill: thick-cut tongue over charcoal, outside skirt and hanging tender. Don't skip the rare shabu-roast, which staff grill and serve over rice with egg yolk. Finish with Morioka cold noodles, ramen or the outside-skirt fried rice. Two diners rate the value highly for the quality. It fills up, so book. Smoking allowed. Closed Wednesdays.

places.notes: [Italian · counter Italian famous for its antipasti platter, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small, lively counter Italian a few minutes from Nagahoribashi, open since 2004 and usually full, so book. The star is the assorted antipasti: more than ten creative little dishes, enough alone with a glass of wine, and one diner saw neighbors do just that. Beyond it, try the roast duck, the black wagyu roast, a seafood bouillabaisse or squid ink pasta in generous portions, and finish with risotto. Staff pick wines to your taste, including some not on the list. One diner found the Genovese short on basil and the pizza ordinary. Seating is a little cramped. ¥200 seat charge. Open until 1:00; closed Tuesdays.

The rest of the menu ranges wide: sukiyaki with udon to finish, sukiyaki-style spring rolls, salt pork with miso, beef tataki with ponzu, beef tendon stew, and seasonal tempura such as whole young corn fried in its husk. A good sake list plus Japanese whiskies. Expect about ¥7,000–10,000 per person. Friendly service. Book ahead; smoking allowed. Closed Sundays.

places.notes: [Chinese · Kikaijima-sesame tantanmen and mapo tofu in Kitahama] A popular Chinese restaurant at Kitahama exit 30 built around sesame from Kikaijima. The shop is run by a former sumo wrestler. The signature tantanmen is the rich Blend; the Aroma 100% serves the meat sauce and chili oil apart and grinds fresh sesame on top, so the sesame leads. On weekends, the Three-Star lunch set gives you a half tantanmen with mapo tofu, steamed chicken salad and almond tofu; weekdays bring a weekly special such as Singapore chicken rice (¥1,400). Dim sum, homemade chili oil and evening courses round it out, with a warm, attentive welcome. Order by QR code. There's a line before noon and it's busy on weekends, so book. Sunday is lunch only; closed Mondays.

The bowl follows the style of Satsumakko: a light, slightly thick tonkotsu, garlic to taste, medium curly egg noodles, crunchy sprouts and tender, juicy pork-belly chashu. It's gentle rather than heavy, which one diner found a little too light; a dab of garlic fixes that. There's also a spicy miso ramen, and the lunch set adds kimchi and rice. places.notes: [Ramen · spicy shoyu meat soba and horumon mazesoba by Tsuruhashi] A twelve-seat counter a minute from Tsuruhashi Station, open since 2016 and usually with a line (write your name on the sheet). The house bowl is a rich shoyu niku soba with Korean chili, sesame oil and thick straight noodles; spice is graded, with level 2 standard and 0 possible, and the soft-bone chashu melts at a touch. In Tsuruhashi, the horumon is the other draw: a spicy horumon mazesoba (¥1,480) loaded with beef offal and kimchi, and a horumon ramen on flat noodles. Finish either with a large rice (¥100) in the leftovers. Garlic and ginger on the counter. Follow on Instagram for a free large or raw egg. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · creamy tonkotsu garlic ramen by Tsuruhashi, open late] A counter shop a minute from Tsuruhashi, next door to Daitsuru, open since 2016 until 1:00, or 3:00 on Fridays and Saturdays. The Sanpei ramen (¥900) is a creamy tonkotsu-and-chicken white soup that drinks lighter than it looks, on slightly curly, chewy noodles, until you stir in the chopped Aomori garlic, which gives it punch. The thick, well-roasted chashu, balanced lean and fat, is the reason to order the chashu ramen (¥1,300) or a rice set. Pickled ginger and pepper on the counter change it up. Seats stay full well past lunch; expect around 20 minutes at weekend lunch. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · additive-free seafood-dashi ramen by Tennoji north exit] The main shop of Menya Wabito, an eleven-seat, Japanese-style counter a minute from JR Tennoji's north gate along the tracks, open since 2015 until 23:00, or 1:00 on weekends. The Wabito ramen is a clear, additive-free seafood dashi, lightly seasoned and clean with no fishiness, on slightly thin, chewy straight noodles with chashu, grilled chicken and a soft egg; finish the soup as ochazuke with rice. For more punch, the special tsukemen (¥1,280) dips thick noodles in a strong sardine-niboshi broth. Large noodles and black oolong tea are free, with five spices to play with. One diner found it too salty. Attentive staff see you out. Cards and QR accepted.

places.notes: [Ramen · Yamagata ramen and Hippa mazesoba inside Tenmabashi Station] A 21-seat counter in the Panante food avenue inside Keihan Tenmabashi Station, open since 2017 and serving Yamagata styles that are rare in Kansai. The signature is the Yamagata Hippa ramen (¥950): thick, stretchy noodles you pull up through egg yolk, canned mackerel, crushed natto and spicy miso over a little chicken broth, then rice with ume-kombu vinegar to finish. The Mazesoba Rekka is the fiery version. For soup, the torichuka is a sweet chicken broth with large chicken pieces and tenkasu on curly noodles, and the Yonezawa ramen is lighter on thin noodles. Busy at lunch. Cards and PayPay accepted.

"As the name suggests, it was all about chicken in both appearance and flavor, with generous chunks of chicken replacing the usual chashu… The tenkasu (tempura scraps) piled on top… soaking up the chicken broth…" — November 2025, Yamagata torichuka.

places.notes: [Monjayaki · Tsukishima-style monja cooked at your table, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A lively second-floor monjayaki spot near Shinsaibashi that cooks in the Tsukishima, Tokyo style, rare in Osaka, with staff doing the work on the hot plate in front of you. The batter has a rich dashi base. The classic is the Mugi Special; the mentaiko mochi cheese is the other standby, best with crispy edges and an egg yolk stirred in. Customize with chikuwa, corn and Baby Star, or try rotating monja such as Komtang or Shin Ramyeon. Tonpei-yaki, okonomiyaki and simple sides (avocado sashimi, diced cucumber) fill the gaps. Open until 2:00, or 5:00 on Fridays and Saturdays. Smoking allowed.

anecdotes.text: "The staff skillfully cooked it right in front of us, making the waiting time enjoyable. The melting cheese paired perfectly with the umami of the mentaiko, and even the crispy edges were delicious until the very end." — July 2026, mentaiko cheese monja.
"This restaurant offers authentic monja-yaki even in Osaka, and the staff prepares it efficiently, allowing us to simply enjoy the meal." — September 2026, Komtang monja.

places.notes: [Kissa · a retro coffee house with European-style curry, Shinsaibashi] An old kissa tucked into an alley just off Shinsaibashi-suji, easy to walk past, with a nostalgic, unhurried interior, a big speaker by the counter and pretty cups. The draw besides the coffee is the Rokumeikan curry (¥1,200): a tangy, gently spicy European-style curry with whole potatoes, a soft-boiled egg and sausage, eaten with knife and fork. One diner found the potato cold in the middle, and coffee on top brings it past ¥1,800. Booth seats are mostly self-service. Tabelog lists 14:00–19:00, but late-2025 reviews describe it opening at night as a bar, so check. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Long-running kissa (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews); featured over two pages in a book on Osaka coffee houses (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The curry comes with chunks of potato, a soft-boiled egg, and sausage… As for the flavor, it has a strong acidity and a hint of spiciness." — September 2026, Rokumeikan curry ¥1,200.
"With its nostalgic atmosphere from a bygone era, the interior is incredibly calming." — December 2025.

cultural_comfort.note: Quiet, old-fashioned kissa; self-service at the booths (December 2025).
